questions.question: The insect shown below is a vector for a disease that is targetted under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme. Identify the disease.
questions.explanation:
The image shown is of the Culex species of mosquitoes, which is a vector for Japanese encephalitis and Bancroftian filariasis.

Mansonia species is the vector for Malayan filariasis.

questions.question:
Which of the following is carried out by the Drug Distribution Centres under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme for Malaria?

1. Collection of the blood slides

2. Distribution of antimalarial tablets

3. Indoor Residual Spray (IRS) spraying operations

4. Case-based surveillance
questions.explanation:
The Drug Distribution Centres are only for dispensing anti-malarial drugs, under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) for Malaria.

The organizational structure for the Anti-Malaria Programme is as follows:

• Central Government: supplies DDT and larvicides.

• State government: procures the Indoor Residual Sprays (IRS) for the districts.

• District Malaria Office: is the key unit for the implementation of the programme.

• District Malaria Officer: has the direct responsibility of IRS spraying operations and is assisted by one Assistant Malaria Officer and Malaria Inspectors.

• Medical officer of the PHC: has the overall responsibility for the surveillance and laboratory services.

• Multi-Purpose Workers and ASHAs: carry out case-based surveillance and case detection in the community.

• Drug Distribution Centres: only for dispensing the antimalarial drugs.

• Fever Treatment Depots: collect blood slides in addition to the distribution of antimalarial drugs.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the surveillance system set up for malaria?
options: Active case detection is carried out when patients report with fever to the peripheral health workers
Blood smears are collected fortnightly during house visits by Accredited Social Health Activists
Antibody detecting rapid diagnostic kits are used for passive case detection as part of surveillance
Passive case detection at the Primary Health Centre is done by examination of blood smears
questions.answer: D. Passive case detection at the Primary Health Centre is done by examination of blood smears
questions.explanation:
Passive case detection at Primary Health Centres (PHCs) is done by examination of blood smears.

Malaria surveillance system:

Active case detection: blood smears are collected by the Multipurpose Health Workers (MPHW)/ Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM) on house visits every fortnight.

Passive case detection: detection of fever case by collecting of blood smears of those that report to ASHAs or peripheral health volunteers.

questions.question: Which of the following measures for controlling malaria is the Urban Malaria Scheme mainly based on?
questions.explanation:
The Urban Malaria Scheme is mainly based on anti-larval measures for controlling malaria. In Urban Malaria Scheme, urban areas with a population of >50,000 and a slide positivity rate of ≥5% are included.

The vector in urban areas breeds in man-made containers. Therefore, anti-larval measures such as larvivorous fish and larvicides are used to control breeding as the primary method of vector control.

In rural areas, anti-adult measures, such as Indoor Residual Spray (IRS) is the primary method of vector control.

questions.question: What is the most efficient anti-larval method to prevent urban malaria?
questions.explanation: The most efficient anti-larval method to prevent urban malaria is to cover overhead tanks and other man-made containers properly. This is because the vector of malaria in urban areas breeds largely in such man-made containers.

questions.question: The blood smear slides (A) and (B) prepared from a patient suspected with malaria are shown below. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding these tests?
options: Slide (A) is used for estimating the parasite concentration
Slide (A) has been air dried for 10 minutes
Slide (B) cannot be used for detecting the species of the parasite
Jaswant Singh Bhattacharya stain is used for both
questions.answer: A. Slide (A) is used for estimating the parasite concentration
questions.explanation:
Slide (A) is a thin blood smear and slide (B) is a thick blood smear. Thin blood smears (slide A) are not used for estimating parasite concentration. They are used to detect the species of parasite.

Microscopy is the best method for the diagnosis of malaria due to its high sensitivity and specificity. Jaswant Singh Battacharya (JSB) stain is used for staining both thick and thin smears.

Thick smear is used to detect infection and estimate parasite concentration. The correct thickness is the thickness through which a newsprint is barely visible. It is prepared by slow-drying for 30 minutes, which leads to hemolysis and distortion of the plasmodia morphology. Hence, species cannot be detected.

Thin smear is used to identify the particular infecting species of Plasmodium. It is prepared by air drying for 10 minutes and fixed in methanol. Thus, the plasmodia morphology is not distorted.

questions.question: The following two diagnostic techniques (A) and (B) were performed in a medical camp conducted for diagnosing malaria. Which is a true statement regarding these techniques?
options: Image (A) - It is used for identifying the species of the malarial parasite
Image (A) - It is not the established method of choice for diagnosing malaria in urban areas
Image (B) - Antibody detection by this test is the method of choice for diagnosing malaria in inaccessible and tribal areas
Image (B) - Bivalent type of this test was used for detecting Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax
questions.answer: D. Image (B) - Bivalent type of this test was used for detecting Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax
questions.explanation:
Image (A) is a thick blood smear and Image (B) is the Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT). Bivalent RDTs detect P. falciparum and P. vivax.

Thin blood smear is used to identify the particular infecting species. Thick blood smear is used to detect infection and estimate parasite concentration.

Antibody detecting Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs) are not the method of choice anymore in diagnosing malaria in inaccessible and tribal areas. The Antigen detecting RDTs and blood smear examination are the recommended methods for diagnosis of malaria.

Note: According to the announcement by Union Health Ministry in April 2018, antibody detecting Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs) for malaria is banned due to the high false-positive rates in endemic areas.

questions.question: According to the National Framework for Malaria Elimination in India, states are classified based on which of the following parameters?
questions.explanation:
The annual parasite incidence (API) is used in classifying states/UTs according to the National Framework for Malaria Elimination in India.

The Annual Parasite Incidence is calculated as: (Cases in one year ×1000) / (Population under surveillance).

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about the classification of malaria endemic states under the National Strategic Plan for Malaria?
options: The states classified under Category 0 are in the elimination phase
The states with API <1 and all their districts reporting API <1 are in the elimination phase
The states with districts reporting API in between 1-2 per 1000 population are in the elimination phase
The states classified under category 2 are in the phase of intensified control
questions.answer: B. The states with API <1 and all their districts reporting API <1 are in the elimination phase
questions.explanation:
The National Strategic Plan for Malaria classifies the states under Category 1 of the NVBDCP to be in the elimination phase.

Category 1 states are all states/UTs with API <1 and all their districts reporting API <1.

questions.question: Which of the following months is observed as the anti-malaria month in India?
questions.explanation:
The anti-malaria month is observed in the month of June every year in our country, just before the onset of monsoon (transmission season of malaria) to enhance the level of awareness.

World Malaria Day is observed on 25th April.

questions.question: A rural medical officer implements Integrated Vector Management in his village. Which of the following measures of vector control would you prefer in a rural area?
questions.explanation:
The measure of vector control preferred for rural areas is indoor residual spray (IRS).

Under integrated vector management (IVM), the preferred measures of vector control for

• Rural areas include: Anti-adult measures, using indoor residual spray (IRS)

• Urban areas include: Anti-larval measures, like environmental control by source reduction, chemical control (mineral oils, Paris green, synthetic insecticides, etc.), and biological control (fish species Gambusia affinis and Lebistes reticulatus which feed on mosquito larvae).

questions.question: Select the correct option regarding Intergrated Vector Management:
options: Malathion is the insecticide of choice used for vector management
Larvivorous fish and larvicides are the main methods of vector control in rural areas
Long Lasting Insecticide Nets are provided in areas with API ≥5
Insecticide treated bed nets are supplied in areas with API ≥3
questions.answer: C. Long Lasting Insecticide Nets are provided in areas with API ≥5
questions.explanation:
Under the Integrated Vector Management initiative, Long Lasting Insecticide Nets (LLIN) are provided in areas with Annual Parasite Index (API) ≥5.

Integrated Vector Management (IVM):

• For adult mosquitoes:

• Indoor Residual Sprays (IRS) are used as the main method of vector control in rural areas. The insecticide of choice will be the insecticide to which the local vector is susceptible as per the best available information.

• Two rounds of spraying are done with DDT, and in DDT resistant areas, three rounds of spraying are done with malathion.

• For larvae:

• Larvivorous fish and larvicides are used. This is the main method of vector control in urban areas.

• For personal protection:

• Insecticide-treated bed nets are supplied in areas with Annual Parasite Index (API) ≥2.

• Long-Lasting Insecticide Nets (LLIN) are provided in areas with API ≥5.

questions.question: You are working as a medical officer in Jharkhand, which is endemic to the disease transmitted by the vector shown below. Which of the following agents would you prefer to control this vector in view of resistance to commonly used agents?
questions.explanation:
The image given is that of a sandfly, which is the vector for kala-azar. In endemic states with increasing resistance to commonly used agents like DDT, synthetic pyrethroids are preferred now.

The four states endemic for kala-azar are Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: According to the revised strategy for the eradication of kala-azar, which of the following drugs would you use across all age groups in order to reduce the human reservoir of infection?
questions.explanation:
A single dose of intravenous treatment with liposomal amphotericin B is used across all age groups in order to reduce the human reservoir of infection. WHO will supply this drug free of cost.

Drugs for Kala Azar:

• Single-dose intravenous liposomal amphotericin B for all age groups and for pregnant and HIV co-infected patients.

• Miltefosine- an oral drug, once daily for 28 days. Contraindicated during pregnancy, lactation, and in women who refuse contraception.

• Combination of miltefosine capsules with paromomycin i.m, for 10 days. Contraindications are the same as miltefosine.

• The drug of choice for Post Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL) is miltefosine 100mg orally per day for 12 weeks.

Ivermectin is used for lymphatic filariasis.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the elimination and eradication of lymphatic filariasis is true?
options: It will be considered as eliminated when the number of microfilaria carriers are less than 5 percent
It will be considered as eliminated when children born after initiation of the programme are free from antigenemia
India has set the target of eliminating lymphatic filariasis by 2025
WHO recommends dual therapy with diethylcarbamazine and albendazole for elimination of transmission
questions.answer: B. It will be considered as eliminated when children born after initiation of the programme are free from antigenemia
questions.explanation:
Lymphatic filariasis will be considered eliminated when the children born after the initiation of the programme are free from antigenemia. Antigenemia refers to the presence of adult filaria worms in the human body.

According to the Elimination of Lymphatic Filariasis (ELF) Programme, there are two criteria to consider elimination of lymphatic filariasis:

• Children born after the initiation of the elimination programme are free from circulating antigenemia.

• The number of microfilaria carriers is <1%.

Following the failure to achieve ELF by 2015, the target set to eliminate lymphatic filariasis by WHO was 2020. To achieve the same WHO recommended the use of triple therapy for lymphatic filariasis. It incorporated ivermectin along with diethylcarbamazine (DEC) and albendazole instead of the traditional DEC and albendazole therapy, for the elimination of transmission of lymphatic filariasis.

In 2021, WHO released the 'Road Map for Neglected Tropical Diseases (2021–2030)'. Under this, lymphatic filariasis is targeted for elimination as a public health problem by 2030.

In February 2023, the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare in India launched a nationwide Sarva Dawa Sevan or Mass Drug Administration (MDA) campaign to eliminate LF by 2027, aiming to achieve this goal three years ahead of the global target.

questions.question: As the medical officer in a Japanese encephalitis endemic area, which of the following measures would you not advocate for controlling its transmission?
options: The use of Indoor Residual Sprays
Keeping pigs away from human dwellings
The use of malathion for outdoor fogging
questions.answer: A. The use of Indoor Residual Sprays
questions.explanation:
Indoor Residual Sprays (IRS) are not used in the vector control measures for Japanese Encephalitis (JE) as its vectors (Culex) are outdoor resters.

Prevention and control of JE include:

• Vaccination

• Keeping pigs away from human dwellings from dusk to dawn (biting time of the vectors). Pigs act as important amplifiers of the virus.

• Use of bed nets for personal protection.

• Use of larvivorous fishes.

• Using malathion for outdoor fogging to control an outbreak.

questions.question: Identify the organization that has the given emblem:
options: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme
National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and Stroke
questions.explanation:
The given image is the emblem of National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP).

Characteristics of NLEP emblem:

• The lotus in the NLEP emblem symbolizes beauty and purity.

• A partially affected thumb, a normal forefinger, and the shape of a house symbolize that leprosy can be cured and a patient with leprosy can be a useful member of the society.

• The rising sun symbolizes hope and optimism.

• The emblem captures the spirit of hope and positivity in the eradication of leprosy.

NLEP is a centrally sponsored health scheme of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt. of India.

Option A: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP)

Option C: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)

Option D: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and Stroke (NPCDCS).

questions.question: The Sparsh campaign was launched to spread awareness about which of the following diseases?
questions.explanation:
Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign (SLAC) was introduced in 2017 on the occasion of the anti-leprosy day (observed on the last Sunday of January) to promote awareness about various aspects of leprosy.

Sapna refers to a local school-going girl who will help to spread awareness in the community.

The other developments under NLEP are:

• Mycobacterium Indicus Prani (MiP) vaccine for multibacillary leprosy patients and their contacts (it is in a project mode).

• Nikusth: A web-based system for the data management of leprosy cases.

Note: Meena is a nine-year-old girl, who is the symbol of UNICEF's Girl Empowerment programme to impart important messages on gender, child rights, education, health and development in the South Asian region.

questions.question: A patient with leprosy comes to the PHC following a pinprick to his foot. He noticed it only after seeing bloodstains on the floor and complains of loss of sensation in his foot. After addressing the issue, the patient is referred to another centre. Where has he been referred to and why?
options: For secondary prevention to a district hospital.
For tertiary prevention to a district hospital.
For secondary prevention to a district nucleus.
For tertiary prevention to a district nucleus.
questions.answer: D. For tertiary prevention to a district nucleus.
questions.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a patient with leprosy having neuropathy needs Micro Cellular Rubber (MCR) footwear, which is a form of tertiary prevention. He is to be referred to a district nucleus which supplies MCR footwear to patients.

questions.question: A patient with leprosy, who has completed a course of multi-drug therapy, presents with complaints of developing painful, tender, and raised lesions on his forehead recently as shown in the image below. What is the first-line treatment for him?
options: Restart multi drug therapy and start thalidomide
Restart multi drug therapy and start prednisolone
questions.explanation:
The presence of new erythematous and tender subcutaneous nodules in a patient with leprosy indicates that he has developed type II lepra reaction. It is also known as Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) and the first line of treatment is prednisolone.

Multi-drug therapy (MDT) should not be restarted in patients who develop lepra reactions after the completion of treatment.

Prednisolone is started at a dose of 40 mg per day and gradually tapered by 5 mg every 2 weeks. 'Prednisolone card' is given when treatment is started. If the patient becomes steroid-dependent, then clofazimine is added.

The key targets of the Global Leprosy Strategy 2021-2023 announced by WHO (Accelerating towards a leprosy-free world) are:

• 120 countries reporting zero new autochthonous cases.

• 70% reduction in the annual number of new cases detected.

• 90% reduction in rate per million population of new cases with Grade 2 disability.

• 90% reduction in rate per million children of new child cases with leprosy.

The current goal is the elimination of leprosy.

questions.question: ABSULS, which is an ASHA-based surveillance project, has been initiated for which of the following diseases?
questions.explanation: ABSULS which stands for Asha Based Surveillance for Leprosy Suspects has been initiated to prioritize leprosy case detection by ASHAs.

questions.question: A District Leprosy Officer is preparing the annual report as per NLEP 2020. Which of the following parameters would he not consider as an essential indicator?
options: Rate of new cases with Grade II disabilities per 10 lakh population per year
Proportion of new cases correctly diagnosed
questions.answer: D. Proportion of new cases correctly diagnosed
questions.explanation:
The proportion of new cases correctly diagnosed is not included under essential indicators. It is a part of the quality of service indicators as per NLEP 2020.

The essential indicators include:

• Annual new case detection rate (ANCDR) per 1 lakh population.

• Rate of new cases with grade II disabilities (G2D) per 10 lakh population per year.

• Treatment completion rate (TCR) as a proxy to cure rate.

• Prevalence rate (PR).

Additional epidemiological indicators include:

• Proportion of Grade II disabilities among new cases.

• Proportion of females among new cases.

• Proportion of multibacillary (MB) among new cases.

• Proportion of child (0- 14 years) among new cases.

• Child rate per 100,000 population.

• Scheduled Caste New Case Detection Rate.

questions.question: As per NLEP 2020, which of the following is not a quality of service indicator?
options: Patient month blister calendar pack stock
Proportion of grade II disabilities among new cases.
Proportion of cases who developed new or additional disability after starting MDT
questions.answer: B. Proportion of grade II disabilities among new cases.
questions.explanation:
Proportion of grade II disabilities among new cases is not a quality of service indicator. It is an additional epidemiological indicator as per NLEP 2020.

The quality of service indicators are:

• Patient month blister calendar pack stock.

• Absolute number of patients made released from treatment (RFT).

• Number of relapse reported.

• Proportion of cases who developed new or additional disability after starting MDT.

• Proportion of treatment defaulters.

• Proportion of new cases correctly diagnosed.

questions.question: You are part of a rural health camp organized under Project Axshya. Which of the following diseases does it aim to control?
questions.explanation:
Project Axshya was launched in 2010 to control TB. Axshya means free from TB which is the ultimate goal of the project and the National TB Elimination Programme.

Project Axshya is being implemented by the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (known simply as The Union). The project works to improve access to quality TB care and control through a partnership between the government and civil society.

The guiding principles of project Axshya are:

• Universal access to quality TB services

• Community participation in TB care and control

• Sustainable interventions and equitable distribution of project benefits with social and gender sensitivity

questions.question: You are working as a medical officer in a PHC where you diagnose a patient with TB. Within how many days do you have to report it to the District Health Officer?
questions.explanation:
The guidelines for TB notification under the RNTCP is within 30 days (a month) of receiving a new case. The notification must be done to the District Health Officer or the Chief Medical Officer of a District Hospital by the practitioner who diagnosed it.

Note: RNTCP has now been renamed to National Tuberculosis Elimination Program (NTEP).

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme?
options: Follow-up sputum smear examination at the end of intensive phase only
Directly Observed Treatment Short course strategy is applied
Treatment is only given to smear positive cases
MDR TB is resistance to either rifampicin or isoniazid
questions.answer: B. Directly Observed Treatment Short course strategy is applied
questions.explanation:
DOTS stands for Directly Observed Treatment Short-course and is given by peripheral and voluntary health workers.

Recent updates in RNTCP:

• Active case finding for TB has been started.

• Follow up:

• On treatment: monthly follow up.

• After treatment: Follow up at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months.

• A sputum smear examination must be done at the end of intensive phase (IP) and at the end of treatment.

questions.question: A patient presents with fever, productive cough, and weight loss. He gives a history of not having completed treatment for tuberculosis thrice in the past. Extensively drug-resistant TB is suspected. How is this entity defined?
options: Resistance to INH + Amikacin + Ofloxacin + Ethambutol
Resistance to INH + Rifampicin + Ofloxacin + Linezolid
questions.answer: D. Resistance to INH + Rifampicin + Ofloxacin + Linezolid
questions.explanation:
XDR-TB (extensively drug-resistant TB) is defined as multi-drug resistant TB (resistant to rifampicin and isoniazid) which is also resistant to one fluoroquinolone (eg. ofloxacin) AND resistant to atleast one additional group A drug (as of 2021, these are bedaquiline and linezolid)

It is usually seen in patients who have previously received treatment for TB and have either failed to complete treatment or relapsed.

questions.question: A patient on HAART presents with complaints of fever and expectorant cough for two weeks. What is the investigation to be ordered first?
questions.explanation:
An HIV patient suspected to have TB is directly investigated by CB-NAAT (Cartridge Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test).

TB is a very serious infection in the immunocompromised and can lead to its most severe form as miliary TB and cause death. Since TB in HIV does not have its typical presentation, early suspicion and advanced diagnosis is the key to preventing mortality.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is false under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme?
options: Continuation phase for new sputum smear positive: HRE for 16 weeks
Intensive phase for sputum smear positive after loss to follow up: HRZE for 8 weeks
Continuation phase for sputum smear positive recurrent case: HRE for 16 weeks
Intensive phase for sputum smear positive after failure to treatment: HRZES for 12 weeks
questions.answer: D. Intensive phase for sputum smear positive after failure to treatment: HRZES for 12 weeks
questions.explanation: Under National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) guidelines Initiation phase (IP) for both new and previously treated cases which are H and R sensitive is HRZE for 8 weeks.

questions.question: Choose the false statement regarding the initiatives and strategies for tuberculosis.
options: The Stop TB strategy was announced by the World Health Organisation
The STOP TB strategy has a target of ending TB by achieving an incidence rate of <10 people per 10,000 population per year
The "Practical approach to lung health" was launched by the WHO for syndromic managment of patients with respiratory symptoms
The End TB strategy is a 20 year programme
questions.answer: B. The STOP TB strategy has a target of ending TB by achieving an incidence rate of <10 people per 10,000 population per year
questions.explanation:
The Stop TB strategy was announced by World Health Organisation to reduce the global burden of TB by 2015 (and not ending TB).

The End TB strategy is a 20-year programme with tagline “A world free of TB - Zero TB deaths, Zero TB disease, and Zero TB suffering”. It aims to:

• end TB by achieving an incidence rate of <10 people/1 lakh population per year by 2035.

• reduce TB deaths by 95% and cut new cases by 90% by 2035.

 The "Practical approach to lung health initiative" was launched by the WHO as a syndromic approach to the management of patients who attend primary health care services for respiratory symptoms.

Ending the TB epidemic is also one of the targets of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) specifically under Goal 3 (to “ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages”).

questions.question: Which of the following group of individuals would you not target under the programme represented by the logo shown below?
questions.explanation:
The red ribbon shown is a part of the logo of the National AIDS Control Organization (NACO) programme. Industrial workers are not included in the target population under NACO.

Target interventions for the control of AIDS transmission are done for:

• High-risk groups like sex workers

• Men who have sex with men

• Transgender

• Injecting drug users

• Bridge population like migrants and long-distance truckers

The services offered through targeted interventions include detection and treatment for sexually transmitted diseases and condom distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the target interventions under National AIDS Control Organisation?
options: Lubricants are given to homosexual men
Clean needles and syringes are given to injecting drug users
Condoms are not given to bridge population
Opioid substitution therapy is given to Injecting Drug Users
questions.answer: C. Condoms are not given to bridge population
questions.explanation:
Bridge populations are supplied with condoms under the NACO target interventions.

Target interventions:

General:

• Detection and treatment for sexually transmitted diseases

• Condom distribution

For injecting drug users:

• Distribution of clean needles and syringes.

• Abscess prevention and management.

• Opioid substitution therapy.

• Linkage with detoxification and rehabilitation services.

For homosexual men and transgenders:

• Provision of lubricants.

• Provision of project-based clinics for sexually transmitted infections.

questions.question: A physician follows the two test protocol for the diagnosis of HIV in a patient. It consists of:
options: Western blot as the first test
Line immunoassay as the second test
HIV ELISA as the second test
Western blot as the second test
questions.answer: C. HIV ELISA as the second test
questions.explanation:
The two test protocol for the diagnosis of HIV consists of ELISA as the second test. If the initial ELISA is positive, a second ELISA is carried out. If the second ELISA is also positive, only then the case is reported to be positive.

Investigations involved in HIV testing strategies:

1. ELISA/ rapid tests.

2. Confirmatory tests with high specificity like western blot and line immunoassays are used in problem cases eg: indeterminate/ discordant cases of rapid tests.

In India, NACO provides western blot (WB) confirmatory testing only to resolve indeterminate results on previous serological testing. It is not used for routine confirmation after a positive result on screening tests. Drawbacks of WB include low rates of detection during acute HIV infection and misclassification of HIV-2 infection.

Note: The western blot is used as a confirmatory test after 2 indeterminate primary tests (ELISA). It is essentially the third test used and does not fit into the two test protocol.

questions.question: As a medical officer involved in the sentinel surveillance for HIV under the National AIDS Control Programme, your duties include all of the following except:
options: Estimation of total infection in the community
Estimation of total cases in hospitals
questions.answer: B. Estimation of total cases in hospitals
questions.explanation:
As a medical officer involved in the sentinel surveillance, the estimation of total cases in hospitals is not included in the sentinel surveillance for HIV under National AIDS Control Programme (NACO).

The aims of the HIV sentinel surveillance include:

• Determine the level of HIV infection in the community.

• Understand the trends of HIV epidemic.

• Understand the geographical spread of HIV infection and classify districts according to epidemiological and vulnerability criteria.

These objectives are achieved by conducting annual cross-sectional surveys of the risk group in the same geographical place.

questions.question: Which of the following is targetted by the establishment bearing the logo shown below:
questions.explanation: The logo shown represents Suraksha Clinics which are established for the management of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) where patients are given color-coded kits.

questions.question: Choose the wrong combination of the colour-coded STI kits among the given options.
questions.explanation: Kit 4 is blue in colour and is used for genital ulcers. These kits are given at Suraksha clinics.

questions.question: A 9-month-old infant who has not been previously vaccinated is brought to the OPD. The mother is however adamant and is allowing you to inject the baby with only one vaccine. Which of the following vaccines would you choose to administer in this situation?
questions.explanation: In this situation, measles vaccine should be administered subcutaneously because, at 9 months of age, it is a priority to give the measles vaccine. OPV and vitamin A should be given orally.

questions.question:
An intern posted in the labour room is administering birth dose vaccines to a newborn baby. According to the National Immunization Schedule, which of the following vaccines would he not administer?

1. OPV

2. IPV

3. BCG

4. Hepatitis B

5. Pentavalent
questions.explanation: Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) and pentavalent vaccine are not given at birth. The vaccines given at birth are BCG, OPV (0 dose) and hepatitis B vaccines.

questions.question: A farmer residing in West Bengal brings his 16-month-old child to the OPD for routine immunization. The child has been adequately immunized till now and has already received a measles vaccine during a supplementary immunization activity drive a few months back. What will you administer to him now?
options: OPV booster, DPT booster and Vitamin A
OPV Booster, DPT booster, MR, JE and Vitamin A
OPV booster, DPT booster, JE vaccine and Vitamin A
OPV Booster, DPT booster, MR and Vitamin A
questions.answer: B. OPV Booster, DPT booster, MR, JE and Vitamin A
questions.explanation:
Vaccines to be given at 16 months of age are OPV booster, DPT booster, MR, JE, and Vitamin A.

The child should receive routine doses of the measles vaccine according to the schedule irrespective of the measles supplementary immunisation activity (SIA) dose. So, the second dose of the measles vaccine is also given.

Japanese Encephalitis (JE) is endemic in rural agricultural areas, often associated with rice cultivation and flood irrigation. Vaccination for JE is given in endemic states only. Two doses of a live attenuated JE vaccine are given under the Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) schedule. Under the Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) schedule, two doses of a new vero cell-derived inactivated JE vaccine are given.

questions.question: A three and a half-year-old child, who is completely unimmunized, is brought to a PHC. Which of the following vaccines can be given to the child now?
options: BCG, DPT-1, OPV-1, Measles, Vit A
questions.answer: C. DPT-1, OPV-1, Measles, Vit A
questions.explanation:
DPT-1, OPV-1, measles and vitamin A can be given to this child of 3.5 years of age in his first immunization visit.

BCG can only be given up to 1 year of age, according to the National Immunisation Schedule (NIS).

Note: BCG can be given up to 5 years of age, as part of the catch-up immunization schedule which is by the Indian Academy of Paediatrics (IAP) and is not followed in government setups.

OPV can be given till 5 years of age.

Measles can be given till 5 years of age.

DPT can be given till 7 years of age (with booster doses).

questions.question: A 5-year-old girl is brought to your clinic for routine immunization. According to the National Immunisation Schedule, which of the following would you administer?
questions.explanation:
At 5 years of age, the 2nd booster dose of DPT must be given along with the 9th (final) dose of vitamin A.

1st booster dose of DPT is given at 16 – 24 months of age.

1st dose of vitamin A is given at 9th month and the 2nd dose is given at 16 months followed by one dose every 6 months thereafter until the age of 5.

Note: DPT booster + Vitamin A is a better answer than DPT booster + OPV because the 9th (final) dose of vitamin A must be given at 5 years but OPV at 5 years is an optional vaccine.

questions.question: A 9-year-old child is brought to the PHC for receiving the JE vaccine. The nurse cleans the injection site with a spirit swab and injects the live attenuated JE vaccine subcutaneously on the left upper arm. Which of the following statements is true regarding this scenario?
options: The procedure of administering the vaccine is wrong
The site of administering the JE vaccine is inappropriate
The JE vaccine cannot be administered under routine immunization in a PHC after 2 years of age
Only live attenuated JE vaccine is currently under use
questions.answer: A. The procedure of administering the vaccine is wrong
questions.explanation:
The procedure of administration is wrong as it is not advisable to clean the injection site with a spirit swab because some of the live components of the vaccine are killed if they come in contact with spirit.

The child is eligible to receive the Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine through routine immunization till 15 years of age. Live attenuated JE vaccine is administered in the left upper arm subcutaneously.

JENVAC is a new inactivated vero cell culture derived JE vaccine produced by Bharath Biotech International limited in India. It is a Kolar strain-derived vaccine. The recommended dose is 0.5ml which is given intramuscularly at left anterolateral aspect of midthigh, 4 weeks apart starting from 1 year of age. Although a booster dose is recommended at a later period, the appropriate time for booster dose administration is not clear.

JEEV is another inactivated vero cell culture derived vaccine from the SA-14-14-2 strain. The recommended dose is:

• 1-3 years: 2 doses of 0.25 ml on 0 and 28 days

• >3years, adolescents, and adults: 2 doses of 0.5ml on 0 and 28 days

• A booster dose of this vaccine is suggested to be given after 12 months of primary vaccination in non-endemic areas.

The inactivated vaccines are currently under the recommendation of IAP. Under the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), a live attenuated vaccine is given.

questions.question: You are visiting a rural area for a vaccination drive conducted under the Intensified Mission Indradhanush scheme. Which of the following vaccines would you not administer in this vaccination drive?
questions.explanation:
Typhoid vaccine is not a part of the Intensified Mission Indradhanush scheme.

The Intensified Mission Indradhanush scheme has been introduced to ensure full immunization (>90%) by December 2018. It now includes 12 vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) (updated from the 7 that Mission Indradhanush focussed on). 4 rounds of immunization are proposed to be held for 7 days each month (from the 7th-13th of each month).

The diseases included in Mission Indradhanush are:

• TB

• Polio

• Hep B

• Diphtheria

• Pertussis

• Tetanus

• Measles

The diseases included recently in Intensified Mission Indradhanush are:

• Rotavirus diarrhoea

• Rubella (as MR vaccine)

• H. influenzae B diseases (as part of the pentavalent vaccine)

• Pneumococcal meningitis

• Japanese Encephalitis

The purpose of Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) is to reach each and every child under 2 years of age and all those pregnant women who have been left uncovered under the routine immunization coverage.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the National Deworming Programme?
options: It is conducted in the months of March and September
Free tablets are given to children up to the age of 15 years
It is carried out in schools and anganwadis
Age appropriate dose of tablet metronidazole is recommended
questions.answer: C. It is carried out in schools and anganwadis
questions.explanation:
The National Deworming programme is carried out in schools and anganwadis.

It is conducted twice a year, in the months of February and August, covering all the children from the age of 1 to 19 years. All the children are given age-appropriate dose of tablet albendazole.

In the states of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, it is carried out only once a year (as the prevalence is <20% in these states).

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke?
options: No separate centres for stroke, DM and cancer
Implementation in over 10 districts in 5 states
Subcentre has facility for diagnosis and treatment
questions.answer: C. District hospital has specialized facilities
questions.explanation:
District hospital has specialized facilities for the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS).

The NPCDCS has separate components for cancer and other non-communicable diseases like diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and stroke. It has been implemented in over 100 districts in 21 states.

At the subcentre level under NPCDCS, screening and referral are done.

Note: The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke(NPCDCS) has been changed to the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases(NP-NCD) to include new diseases and new health initiatives.

The new diseases included in the NP-NCD are:

• Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease

• Chronic Kidney disease

• Asthma and Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

• ST elevation myocardial infarction

questions.question: Which of the following is a false statement about the Indian Hypertension Control Initiative (IHCI)?
options: The IHCI monitoring personnel includes cardiovascular health officers and senior treatment supervisors
Provision of real-time blood pressure monitoring for all patients via information systems
The IHCI provides 30-day medication for individuals registered for hypertension management
The target is a 90% reduction in the prevalence of hypertension by the year 2025
questions.answer: D. The target is a 90% reduction in the prevalence of hypertension by the year 2025
questions.explanation:
The false statement about the Indian Hypertension Control Initiative is a 90% reduction in the prevalence of hypertension by the year 2025.

The IHCI is an initiative by the MoHFW, WHO, ICMR, and state governments to control hypertension in India. It has adopted the goal of “25 by 25” to reduce the prevalence of hypertension in India by 25% by 2025. The activities of IHCI are monitored by the cardiovascular health officers (CVHO's) at the state and district level and by the senior treatment supervisors (STS's) at the sub-district level. The IHCI has strengthened the prevention of hypertension by ensuring the provision of antihypertensive medications for 30 days to all patients registered under the IHCI.

The 5 components of IHCI are:

1. Use of standardized hypertension treatment protocols approved by national and global policies.

2. Availability of recommended protocol drugs to provide a regular and uninterrupted supply of medications.

3. Task-sharing and team-based care involving nurses, health workers, and ASHAs to improve treatment compliance.

4. Patient-centered services provide easy access to BP monitoring at Health & wellness centers and PHCs.

5. Information systems that provide real-time BP monitoring to improve patient follow-ups: Use of the “Simple App” in all IHCI states.

*Note: Amlodipine, telmisartan, and chlorthalidone are the drugs of choice in the standardized treatment protocols of the IHCI.

questions.question: Under the National Programme for Control of Blindness & Visual Impairment, NGO eye hospitals are considered as:
questions.explanation:
NGO eye hospitals are considered secondary level centres under the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI).

Levels of eye care centres according to NPCBVI:

• Primary level: Sub-district level hospitals, community health centres, mobile ophthalmic units, upgraded PHCs, and link workers.

• Secondary level: District hospitals and NGO eye hospitals.

• Tertiary level: Regional institutes of ophthalmology and medical colleges.

The goal of NPCBVI is to reduce the prevalence of blindness to 0.25% by 2025.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to measure the output of the National Programme for Control of Blindness & Visual Impairment?
options: Number of cases of refractory errors corrected
Number of cataract surgeries leading to sight restoration
Number of cases of childhood blindness detected and cured
Prevalence of blindness reduced by 0.5% per year
questions.answer: B. Number of cataract surgeries leading to sight restoration
questions.explanation:
The measure of the output of the National Programme for Control of Blindness & Visual Impairment (NPCBVI) is indicated by the number of cataract surgeries leading to sight restoration.

The most common cause of low vision in India is cataract (low vision is visual acuity <6/18- 6/60).

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is not a part of the Vision 2020 programme in India?
questions.explanation:
Onchocerciasis is not a part of the Vision 2020 programme in India. It is a part of the Global Vision 2020 programme.

Global Vision 2020
India Vision 2020

Cataract

Refractive errors and low vision

Childhood blindness

Trachoma

Cataract

Childhood blindness

Glaucoma

questions.question: A pregnant woman from a rural area registers under Janani Suraksha Yojana. Which of the following services would not be provided to her under this scheme?
options: Safe motherhood services under Vandematharam scheme
questions.explanation:
The Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) does not provide STD counseling.

Janani Suraksha Yojana is a safe motherhood intervention launched under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant women. The services provided by the JSY are:

• Cash is disbursed to the mother at the institution for having an institutional delivery.

• Safe motherhood services (IFA tablets, TT vaccination) under the Vandemataram scheme.

• Village health and nutrition day

• Maternal death review

• Pregnancy tracking: ASHA worker/Anganwadi Worker (AWW) or any other link worker help in monitoring antenatal check-ups, and post-delivery care.

• Safe abortion services: mifepristone followed by misoprostol and manual vacuum aspiration.

questions.question: Where and how often is the Village Health Nutrition Day conducted?
options: Once every two weeks in PHC
Once every two weeks in Anganwadi
questions.answer: B. Once a month in Anganwadi
questions.explanation: Village Health Nutrition Day is conducted once a month in the Anganwadi centres in the village itself. The villagers interact with health workers and are provided with basic services and information about health care.

questions.question: A 20-day old baby is gasping for air and not feeding properly. The mother has no money to go to the nearby hospital. Which national programme has provisions to benefit this woman to take her baby to the health facility?
questions.explanation:
The Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) has provisions for free transport of pregnant women and sick infants from:

• home to the health facilities

• between facilities in case of a referral

• back home from the health facilities

The provisions of JSSK include:

• Free transport

• Free treatment

• Free drugs and consumables

• Free diagnostics and diet

• Free and cashless delivery

• Free C-Section

• Free provision of blood

Note: Previously under JSSK, the free entitlements were provided only for sick newborns till 30 days after birth. Now it is expanded to cover infants also.

questions.question: The Navjat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram was designed for which of the following demographic groups?
questions.explanation:
The Navjat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (NSSK) was designed to train health personnel in basic newborn care and resuscitation.

The training is aimed to improve the delivery of excellent newborn care at every point and is usually done for 2 days.

questions.question: A 10-year-old girl has just started menstruating. Under which of the following national programmes, she will be provided with a pack of sanitary napkins by the ASHA worker in her village?
questions.explanation:
The girl will be provided with a pack of 6 sanitary napkins for 6 Rupees (called Freedays) by the ASHA worker through the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme under the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK).

RKSK focuses on:

• Development of adolescent population (10-19 years).

• Weekly Iron and Folic Acid supplementation (100mg Fe + 500 mcg Folic Acid)

• Menstrual hygiene: A pack of 6 sanitary napkins for 6 Rupees (called Freedays) by the ASHA.

• It also includes enhancement of mental health and prevention of substance abuse and violence.

Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a government-sponsored savings program for parents of girl children <10 years age. It helps parents to set aside money for their female child’s potential college and marriage expenses by opening an account at any post office branch or any commercial bank approved by the central government.

Kishori Shakti Yojana (KSY) seeks to empower adolescent girls, so as to enable them to take charge of their lives. The objectives are to:

• improve the nutritional, health and development status of adolescent girls

• promote awareness of health, hygiene, nutrition and family care

• opportunities for learning life skills

• going back to school

• help them gain a better understanding of their social environment

• take initiatives to become productive members of society.

Recent update: Department of Pharmaceuticals under Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers has recently launched ‘Suvidha’ (100% Oxo-biodegradable Sanitary Napkin), under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) on World menstrual hygiene day. ‘Swachhta, Swasthya and Suvidha’ will be available for Rs. 1 per pad over 3200 Janaushadhi Kendras for the underprivileged women of India.

questions.question: Which among the following is not true about POSHAN Abhiyan?
options: It is a programme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development
The goals are to achieve improvement in neonatal mortality
Launched on the date of International Women's Day 2018
Targets to reduce low birth weight by 2% per annum
questions.answer: B. The goals are to achieve improvement in neonatal mortality
questions.explanation:
The goal of POSHAN Abhiyaan /National Nutrition Mission (NNM) is to achieve an improvement in the nutritional status during the next three years beginning 2017-18. It is a flagship programme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD). Its target population include:

• children from 0-6 years

• adolescent girls

• pregnant women

• lactating mothers

The logo is:

The following image depicts the targets of this mission:

Note: Nikshay Poshan Yojana is a government scheme in India to provide Rs.500 per month for TB patients to buy food.

questions.question: Which of the following is the objective of the Ujjawala Scheme?
options: Provide LPG connections to families below poverty line
Provide LED bulbs in every household
questions.explanation:
The Ujjawala Scheme is for the prevention of trafficking and for the rescue, rehabilitation, and reintegration of victims of trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation.

The Ujjwala Yojana (note spelling without "a") is for providing 5 crores of free cooking LPG connections to all families below the poverty line till 2019.

The Ujala Scheme (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs and Appliances for All) is the largest domestic lighting project in the world, launched under the Ministry of Power. It aims at promoting the use of energy-efficient LED bulbs in every household in the country.

INSPIRE strategy is a set of 7 evidence-based strategies introduced to select, implement, monitor, and evaluate effective policies, programs, and services to prevent and respond to violence against children.

questions.question: An ASHA worker is offering services under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan in her village. All of the following services will be provided by her except:
options: Information, education, communication and public awareness
questions.explanation:
Water pollution is not managed under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.

The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched in 2014 with an aim to eradicate open-air defecation by the year 2019 through the construction of 12 million toilets. The two sub-missions of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan are Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin (SBM-G) and Swachh Bharat Mission Urban (SBM-U).

• Components of this mission include:

• Household toilets including improving unsanitary latrines

• Community toilets

• Public toilets

• Solid waste management

• Information, education, communication, and public awareness

• Capacity building and administrative & office expenses

questions.question: Which of the following statements is false about the Ayushman Bharat-National Health Protection Mission?
options: Government provides health insurance cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per family per year
The limit of the family size that is covered is up to 7 members
All pre-existing diseases of the individual are covered
It covers secondary and tertiary care hospitalization
questions.answer: B. The limit of the family size that is covered is up to 7 members
questions.explanation:
There is no cap on family size or the age of the members. All the families listed under the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) database are covered as per the defined criteria.

The following are the benefits provided under this program:

• Health insurance cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per family per year.

• All families listed in the SECC database, as per the defined criteria, will be covered. There is no cap on family size and age of members.

• Free treatment is available at all public and empanelled private hospitals

• Both secondary and tertiary care hospitalization is covered.

• All pre-existing diseases are covered. Hospitals cannot deny treatment.

• To control costs, the payments for treatment will be done on a package rate (to be defined by the Government in advance) basis.

• Cashless and paperless access to quality health care services.

Logo:

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana?
options: Unemployment allowance is not given in case of closure of factory
Unemployment allowance is given in case of employment injury
Allowance is given at 50% of the daily wage for a maximum of 2 years
To qualify for the scheme, worker must have worked for more than 2 years
questions.answer: C. Allowance is given at 50% of the daily wage for a maximum of 2 years
questions.explanation:
Unemployment allowance under Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (RGSKY) is given at the rate of 50% of daily wage for a maximum of 2 years.

RGSKY is a scheme of ESI that provides unemployment allowance to an insured person going out of employment involuntarily, on account of:

• closure of a factory or establishment

• retrenchment (laying off employees due to economic difficulty)

• permanent disability due to nonemployment injury

Allowance and eligibility criteria of Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (updated in 2019):

• The allowance is given at the rate of 50% of the daily wage for a maximum of 2 years.

• To qualify for the scheme the worker must have worked in that setup for >3 years.

Note: Disability due to employment injury is covered under disablement benefits of ESI Act, 1948.

• Temporary disability: 90% of wages until disablement lasts.

• Permanent disability: 90% of wages as a life pension on the basis of loss of earning capacity.

• Dependants benefit: 90% of wage as monthly payment to the dependants of the deceased person, in cases where death occurs due to employment injury or occupational hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following does the Laqshya initiative launched recently by the Government of India refer to?
options: Initiative for providing free sanitary pads
Initiative to provide vaccination to under-5 children
Initiative for labour room quality improvement
Initiative to provide affordable healthcare to all
questions.answer: C. Initiative for labour room quality improvement
questions.explanation:
The Laqshya initiative launched recently by the Government of India refers to the initiative for labour room quality improvement.

There is enough evidence to support the fact that improving the quality of care in labour rooms, especially on the day of birth, is crucial to maternal and neonatal survival.

Laqshya is expected to improve the quality of care being provided to the pregnant mother in the labour room and maternity operation theatres, thereby preventing the undesirable adverse outcomes associated with childbirth. This initiative is implemented in government medical colleges besides district hospitals, and high delivery load sub-district hospitals, and community health centres.

It plans to conduct quality certification of labour rooms and also incentivize facilities achieving the targets outlined. The goal is to reduce preventable maternal and new-born mortality, morbidity, and stillbirths associated with the care around delivery in labour room and maternity OT, and ensure respectful maternity care.

questions.question: The image below shows the logo of which of the following national programmes?
questions.explanation:
The image shown is the new logo of the 360-degree holistic Family Planning Campaign.

Logo of other options:

"Beti bachao Beti padhao."

India Newborn Action Plan (INAP)

The logo of Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram (JSSK)

questions.question: What is the main objective of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Jan-aushadhi Pariyojana?
options: Improve maternal and child health services
Make quality, generic medicines affordable to all
Enhance quality of life and increase employment for the differently abled
Promote cleanliness and enhance quality of healthcare facilities in India
questions.answer: B. Make quality, generic medicines affordable to all
questions.explanation:
The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Jan-aushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) carries the objective of making quality, generic medicines affordable for everyone, especially the lower socio-economic groups.

BPPI (Bureau of Pharma PSUs of India), under the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers, is the implementation agency for PMBJP. The mission of this programme includes creating awareness and demand for generic medicines through education and supply of such medications.

Kayakalp programme is a national initiative launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) under Swachh Bharat Abhiyan to promote cleanliness and enhance the quality of healthcare facilities in India.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the Vandematharam scheme?
options: Its aim is to provide safe motherhood services
An MBBS graduate or an obstetrician can volunteer
IFA tablets and TT injections are provided by District Medical Officers
questions.answer: A. Free treatment in private clinics
questions.explanation:
The Vandematharam scheme does not include free treatment in private clinics.

Vandematharam scheme is a voluntary scheme for providing safe motherhood services. It can be volunteered by an obstetrician, maternity home, nursing home, lady doctor or an MBBS graduate.

IFA tablets, OCPs, and TT injections are provided by the respective District Medical Officers (DMOs) to the Vandematharam doctors or clinics for free distribution to beneficiaries. Cases needing special care and treatment can be referred to government hospitals.

questions.question: Which of the following is a component of the scheme depicted by the logo given below?
questions.explanation:
National Health Protection Mission is a component of the Ayushman Bharat scheme.

Ayushman Bharat-National Health Protection Mission (AB-NHPM) aims to build a comprehensive need-based health care service and targets to build a 'New India 2022'. Its components are:

• Creation of 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centres- these centres will provide Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC), covering both maternal and child health services and non-communicable diseases, including free essential drugs and diagnostic services.

• National Health Protection Mission (NHPM) provides health protection cover to poor and vulnerable families, screening for non-communicable diseases, and follow-up of hospitalization cases among others.

Beneficiary Level:

• The government provides health insurance cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 per family per year.

• All families listed in the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) database as per defined criteria will be covered. No cap on family size and age of members.

• Priority to a girl child, women, and senior citizens.

• Free treatment is available at all public and empanelled private hospitals in times of need.

• Covers secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.

• 1,350 medical packages covering surgery, medical and daycare treatments, cost of medicines, and diagnostics.

• All pre-existing diseases are covered. Hospitals cannot deny treatment.

• Cashless and paperless access to quality health care services.

• Hospitals will not be allowed to charge any additional money from beneficiaries for the treatment.

• Can reach out for information, assistance, complaints, and grievances to a 24X7 helpline number.

questions.question: As per the new National Policy for Rare Diseases, financial support of up to Rs. 20 lakhs can be given to which group of rare diseases?
questions.explanation:
As per the new National Policy for Rare Diseases, a provision for financial support of up to Rs. 20 lakhs under the umbrella scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi is proposed for the treatment of rare diseases that require a one-time treatment (listed under Group 1 in the rare disease policy).

National Policy for Rare Diseases is a comprehensive policy for the prevention and management of rare diseases. The policy lists rare diseases under 3 groups:

• Group 1: Disorders amenable to one-time curative treatment:

• Disorders amenable to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation eg: lysosomal storage disorders

• Disorders amenable to organ transplantation eg: glycogen storage disorders, urea cycle disorders, ADPKD, etc.

• Group 2: Diseases requiring long term/ lifelong treatment having a relatively lower cost of treatment:

• This group includes disorders managed with special dietary formulae/ hormone/ specific drugs. eg: phenylketonuria, osteogenesis imperfecta, etc.

• Group 3: Diseases for which definitive treatment is available but treatment is lifelong or expensive:

• This group includes diseases such as Pompe disease, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, etc.

The objectives of the policy are:

• Lowering the high cost of treatment for rare diseases with an increased focus on indigenous research.

• Creating a national hospital-based registry of rare diseases.

• Early screening and prevention through primary and secondary health care infrastructure, and through counselling for the high-risk parents.

• Crowdfunding mechanism in which corporates and individuals will be encouraged to extend financial support.

chapters.chapter: Demography I Demographic Cycle, Annual Growth Rate And Age Pyramid

questions.question: Which of the following is not a demographic process?
questions.explanation:
Morbidity is not a demographic process.

Demography refers to the study of the population. Demographic processes include:

• Fertility

• Mortality

• Marriage

• Migration

• Social mobility

These processes continuously bring about changes in the population size, composition, and distribution.

questions.question: In which stage of the demographic cycle does the death rate start declining?
questions.explanation: The death rate starts declining in stage 2 or the early expanding phase of the demographic cycle.

questions.question: In which stage of the demographic cycle does the birth rate start declining?
questions.explanation:
The birth rate starts declining in stage 3 or the late expanding phase of the demographic cycle.

India is currently in this stage of the demographic cycle.

The year 1921 is called the year of the great divide in India. This is because, since 1921, the absolute number of people getting added to the population during each decade has been on the rise. This is the year in which India moved from stage 1 to stage 2 of the demographic cycle.

questions.question:
A group of demographers studied the changes in the birth and death rates of two countries, A and B from the year 2001 to 2011. The collected data is given below. In which stages of the demographic cycle are countries A and B in respectively?

Country A:

2001
2011

Birth rate
38.3
38.3

Death rate
13.7
10.2

Country B:

2001
2011

Birth rate
12.4
12.3

Death rate
6.7
6.6
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, country A is in stage 2 and country B is in stage 4 of the demographic cycle.

According to the given data, in country A, the high birth rate has remained unchanged with a decline in the death rate. This will result in an exponential increase in the population. This means country A is in the early expanding stage of the demographic cycle.

In country B, the low birth rate and death rates have remained unchanged. Thus, the population will attain a plateau phase and remain stationary. This means country B is in the low stationary stage of the demographic cycle.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the fifth stage of the demographic cycle?
options: Birth rate falls below death rate
questions.answer: D. Birth rate falls below death rate
questions.explanation:
In stage 5 of the demographic cycle, the birth rate falls below the death rate.

In this stage, the death rate attains a low stable rate while the birth rate keeps declining. Thus, the curve of the birth rate will cross the curve of the death rate in a graph of the demographic cycle and falls further below.

The demographic gap is negative and the population is declining. So, this stage is known as the declining stage.

questions.question: While studying the birth and death rates of a country, a demographer found it to be in the early expanding stage of the demographic cycle. Which of the following findings would lead him to such a conclusion?
options: Increased birth rate and decreased death rates
Decreased birth rate and increased death rates
Unchanged birth rate and decreased death rates
questions.answer: D. Unchanged birth rate and decreased death rates
questions.explanation: Early expanding stage (stage 2) of the demographic cycle is characterized by an unchanged birth rate and decreasing death rate.

questions.question: A researcher is studying the demographic cycle of various countries. In which stages of the cycle will she notice an increase and a decrease in the demographic gap respectively?
questions.explanation:
The demographic gap starts increasing in stage 2 and starts decreasing in stage 3.

The demographic gap refers to the difference between birth rate and death rate which develops when a country undergoes a demographic transition.

In stage 2 of the demographic cycle, the death rate declines but the birth rate remains unchanged. Hence, the demographic gap increases and reaches a maximum by the end of stage 2. In stage 3, both the death rate and birth rate are declining so the demographic gap starts decreasing.

questions.question: At which stage of the demographic cycle will the demographic gap be maximum?
questions.explanation: The demographic gap starts increasing and becomes maximum in the early expanding phase of the demographic cycle.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the stage of demographic cycle marked by the red arrow?
questions.explanation:
The marked stage is the late expanding phase (stage 3) of the demographic cycle. A demographic gift or demographic dividend is seen in this stage.

This refers to the presence of a higher number of economically productive individuals (young and middle-aged adults) in the population due to a higher birth rate in the previous demographic phase (phase 2). India is currently experiencing the demographic gift.

The birth rate starts declining alongside a death rate that continues to fall in stage 3 causing a decline in the demographic gap. The death rate declines further and the birth rate falls in this stage.

questions.question: In which stage of the demographic cycle will the phenomenon of a demographic trap be maximally seen?
questions.explanation:
The phenomenon of a demographic trap is seen maximally in the early expanding stage (stage 2).

This phenomenon refers to a period in which there is high fertility and birth rate and a declining death rate. The population grows exponentially in this stage and this growing population exceeds the national or regional carrying capacity. Countries in this stage are said to be caught in a demographic trap.

questions.question: While conducting a field study in a village, you found the birth and death rates of the population to be 42 and 31 respectively. What is the current annual growth rate of this population?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, the current annual growth rate is 1.1%.

Here, the birth rate is 42 i.e 42 live births per 1000 population, and the death rate is 31 i.e 31 deaths per 1000 population.

Current annual growth rate = crude birth rate – crude death rate. So, current annual growth rate = 42-31= 11 per 1000 population or 1.1%.

questions.question: The population of a country is 1 lakh in the year 2000 and its annual growth rate is 2%. By which year will the population of this country become 2 lakhs?
questions.explanation:
For the given country, its population would become 2 lakhs i.e, double the population from the year 2000, by the year 2035.

As per the Malthusian growth model, when the annual growth rate is 1%, the population doubles in 70 years. Therefore, when the annual growth rate is 2%, the population will double in 35 years.
