The growth rate of India is estimated at 1% as per 2020 UN data. Therefore, it falls in the rapidly growing phase of population growth.

questions.question: What was the population of India, as of 2021?
questions.explanation: The population of India, as of 2021, was around 1.39 billion. This is as per UN 2021 data.

questions.question: According to the 2021 UN data, what is India's population growth rate?
questions.explanation:
According to UN data, India's population growth rate in 2021 was 1%.

As per the last published SRS data of the Indian government, it was 1.2% in 2018.

India's population is currently increasing at a rate of 16 million each year. It currently falls in the rapidly growing phase of population growth.

questions.question: You have been tasked with studying the age and sex structure of a population with high rates of female infanticide. Which of the following methods will you prefer to use?
questions.explanation:
The age and sex structure of a population may be best represented using a population pyramid.

It is a histogram that shows the distribution of ages across a population. It is divided down the center between male and female members of the population.

questions.question: What does the age pyramid of India look like?
options: Broad at base and narrow at apex
Broad at apex and narrow at base
Broad in the middle and narrow at base
questions.answer: A. Broad at base and narrow at apex
questions.explanation: The age pyramid of India is broad at the base and narrow at the top. This is typical of most developing nations.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a vital statistic?
questions.explanation:
Sex ratio is not a vital statistic, it is a population statistic.

Demographic indicators have been divided into 2 parts:

• Population statistics include -

• Population size

• Sex ratio

• Density

• Dependency ratio

• Vital statistics include -

• Birth rate

• Death rate

• Natural growth rate

• Life expectancy at birth

• Mortality rate

• Fertility rate

questions.question: While conducting a demographic study, you need to calculate the total dependency ratio of the study population. Which of the following will you include in the numerator while calculating this?
options: Population under 10 years and above 60 years
Population under 15 years and above 60 years
Population under 10 years and above 65 years
Population under 15 years and above 65 years
questions.answer: D. Population under 15 years and above 65 years
questions.explanation:
Population under 15 years and above 65 years are part of the numerator used to calculate the total dependency ratio. This is because this population is considered the dependant population.

The dependant population includes children below 15 years of age and adults above 65 years of age. The total dependency ratio is the ratio of the combined dependent population to those in the age group of 15 - 65 years. It is also called the societal dependency ratio. It can also be divided into the young-age and old-age dependency ratios.

Note: As of mid-year 2020, the dependency ratio of India is 48.7%.

questions.question: While studying a community, the researcher found 30% of the population to be below 15 years of age, and 10% was over 65 years of age. What is the total dependency ratio of this population?
questions.explanation:
The total dependency ratio in this population is 66.6%.

This can be calculated as follows.

Here, the total population below 15 years of age is = 30%

Total population above 65 years of age = 10%

So, total population between 15-65 years of age = 100 - (30 + 10) = 60%

Hence, dependency ratio in this population = 100* (30% + 10%)/60% = 66.6%

questions.question: What is potential support ratio?
options: Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per child below 15 years or less
Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per older person aged 65 or more
Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per each older person aged >65 and younger person aged < 15
Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per each older person aged > 60 and younger person aged <15
questions.answer: B. Number of persons aged 15 to 64 per older person aged 65 or more
questions.explanation: The potential support ratio is the number of persons aged 15 to 64 per one older person aged 65 or more. It is the inverse of the old-age dependency ratio.

questions.question: Which of the following is the major contributor to demographic burden?
questions.answer: D. Increased old age dependency ratio
questions.explanation:
Demographic burden refers to an increase in the total dependency ratio. It is mostly caused by an increased old-age dependency ratio.

The term demographic bonus denotes the decline in dependency ratio due to declining fertility. A decline in dependency ratio especially the young-age dependency ratio has been identified to be a key factor in the underlying rapid economic development.

The potential support ratio is the number of persons aged 15 to 64 per one older person aged 65 or more. This is the inverse of the old-age dependency ratio.

questions.question: Which of the following determines the carrying capacity of a population?
questions.explanation: The carrying capacity is the number of individuals of a population that can be supported for a period of time given the resources of that area. Thus, the carrying capacity is determined by the limiting resources of an area.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about crude birth rate?
questions.explanation:
The numerator of crude birth rate only includes live births and does not include stillbirths.

Crude birth rate = No. of live births during the year x 1000/ Estimated mid-year population

questions.question: As part of the national maternity benefit scheme, you have been tasked with conducting a study in a community of 5000 people. What is the expected number of pregnant women in this community if the crude birth rate is 30 per 1000 people?
questions.explanation:
The expected number of pregnant females in the given community would be 165.

Step 1: In the given question, the crude birth rate is 30 per 1000 people i.e 30 children are born from pregnant mothers for every 1000 people. Therefore there are 30 pregnant females per 1000 population.

Step 2: Since the total population is 5000, the total no of pregnant females = 5000 x 30/1000 = 150

Step 3: Since some pregnancies may not result in live births (abortions and stillbirths), a correction factor of 10% should be added to avoid the underestimation of the number of pregnancies. Pregnancy wastage (i.e 10% of total live births) =10 x 150/100=15.

Step 4: Total pregnant females = total live births + pregnancy wastage = 150+15=165.

questions.question: According to NFHS-5, what is the sex ratio in India?
questions.explanation:
According to the NFHS-5 (2019-21), the sex ratio in India is 1020 females per 1000 males. It has increased from the 2011 Census which had found a sex ratio of 940 females per 1000 males.

The sex ratio at birth is 929 females per 1000 males.

questions.question: For a population of 10,000, what does a sex ratio of more than 1000 mean?
questions.explanation:
For a population of 10000, if the sex ratio is more than 1000, it means males are less than 5000 i.e., less than half the population.

The sex ratio refers to the number of females per 1000 males. An ideal sex ratio would be 1000, indicating the population comprises an equal number of males and females.

Sex ratio >1000 indicates that there are more females than males in a population. Sex ratio <1000 indicates that there are fewer females compared to males in the population.

questions.question: What is the definition of the net reproduction rate?
options: No. of children that would be born to married women assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate
No. of girls that would be born to married women assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate
No. of female children a new born girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate
No. of children a new born girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate
questions.answer: C. No. of female children a new born girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age specific fertility and mortality rate
questions.explanation:
Net reproduction rate (NRR) is defined as the number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime assuming fixed age-specific fertility and mortality rate.

India is aiming for an NRR of 1 as it is equivalent to the two-child norm.

questions.question: An epidemiologist would consider the growth of his study population to be inadequate if he found the NRR to be:
questions.explanation:
If the NRR is less than 1, then the population growth of a community is said to be inadequate.

Net reproduction rate (NRR) is the number of daughters a newborn girl will bear during her lifetime assuming age-specific fertility and mortality rates.

questions.question: What should the net reproductive rate of a population be to attain a 2 child norm?
questions.explanation: The net reproductive rate (NRR) should be 1 to attain the 2 child norm.

questions.question: What is the denominator used in the formula for calculating the general fertility rate?
options: Total number of women in the population
Mid-year population of women in the reproductive age group
Total number of married women in the age group 15 – 45
questions.answer: C. Mid-year population of women in the reproductive age group
questions.explanation: The denominator used to calculate the general fertility rate is mid-year population of women in the reproductive age group.

questions.question: To assess the effects of the national population policy, data is being collected at the PHC level. You have been asked to submit data regarding the approximate magnitude of completed family size in the population under your PHC. Which of the following indicators will you calculate?
questions.explanation: The total fertility rate is an indicator of the approximate magnitude of completed family size.

questions.question: What is the infant mortality rate in India as per the SRS Statistical Report (2020)?
questions.explanation:
The infant mortality rate (IMR) in India as per the SRS statistical report (2020) is 28 per 1000 live births.

IMR is defined as the number of infant deaths for every 1000 live births. As per the National Family Health Survey - 5 (2019-2021), the IMR is 35.2 per 1000 live births.

IMR is considered the best indicator of the availability, utilization, and effectiveness of health care.

questions.question: What is the maternal mortality ratio in India according to the Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality (2018-2020) based on SRS data?
questions.explanation:
The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) in India according to the Special Bulletin (2018-2020) based on SRS data is 97.

MMR is defined as the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.

The most common causes of maternal mortality in India are postpartum hemorrhage and infections.

questions.question: While collecting data for the census, which of the following people would you consider to be literate?
options: A person who is able to read, write and understand in any language
A person who is not able to read or write but can sign legal documents
A person who is able to speak fluently in his native language but is not able to read or write
A person who is able to read, but may not be able to write
questions.answer: A. A person who is able to read, write and understand in any language
questions.explanation: A person is considered literate if he or she can read, write and understand in any language.

questions.question: What is the denominator of the formula used to calculate effective literacy rate?
options: Population less than 15 years of age
questions.answer: B. Population aged 7 years or more
questions.explanation:
The denominator used to calculate the effective literacy rate is the population aged 7 years or more. It is calculated as follows.

Effective literacy rate = Number of literate persons aged 7 and above x 100/ Population aged 7 and above in a given year.

This rate is generally used in Indian censuses including those in 1991, 2001, and 2011 for estimating literacy.

questions.question: You are studying the literacy rate of a community with a total population of 10000. Out of these, there are 2000 children from 0-6 years of age, and 4000 literate individuals above 7 years of age. What is the effective literacy rate of this population?
questions.explanation:
The effective literacy rate of this population is 50%.

It is calculated as follows,

Effective literacy rate = (Number of literate persons aged 7 and above x 100) / population aged 7 and above in a given year.

In the given scenario, people aged 7 years and above = 10000 - 2000 = 8000. Out of these 8000 people, 4000 are literate.

Thus, effective literacy rate = 4000 x 100/8000 = 50%.

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding the criteria for an urban Indian city?
options: Having a density of 390 persons per square km
At least half of the adult male population employed in occupations other than agriculture
questions.answer: C. At least half of the adult male population employed in occupations other than agriculture
questions.explanation:
In an urban area, at least three-fourths of the adult male population are employed in occupations other than agriculture.

In the Indian context, the urban areas are places:

• having 5,000 or more inhabitants

• having a density of not less than 1,000 persons per square mile or 390 per square kilometer

• having pronounced urban characteristics

• having at least three-fourths of the adult male population employed in pursuits other than agriculture

questions.question: What is the number of eligible couples per 1000 population in India?
questions.explanation:
There are approximately 150 – 180 eligible couples per 1000 population in India.

An eligible couple refers to a currently married couple wherein the wife belongs to the reproductive age group (15-49 years of age).

questions.question:
A study was conducted in a village with 180 eligible couples, to gather data on the different contraceptive methods used. The data obtained are given below. What is the couple protection rate in the village?

Vasectomy – 15

Tubectomy – 15

Intrauterine device (IUD) users – 8

Oral pill users – 15

Condom users – 7
questions.explanation:
Couple protection rate (CPR) is defined as the percentage of eligible couples effectively protected against childbirth by one or the other approved methods of family planning.

In the given scenario, 60 out of 180 eligible couples are using different contraceptive methods. Therefore, CPR = (60/180) x 100 = 33%.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a barrier method of contraception?
questions.explanation:
Lippes loop is an intrauterine device and not a barrier method of contraception.

Barrier methods of contraception include:

• Physical methods – male and female condoms, diaphragm, vaginal sponge (Today)

• Chemical methods – foam tablets, aerosols, creams, jellies, suppositories, and soluble films (C-films)

questions.question: A sexually active woman has been using Today sponge as a contraceptive. What does this contain?
questions.explanation:
Today is a type of vaginal sponge that contains 9 – nonoxynol.

Today is a barrier contraceptive inserted vaginally. It has to be left in place for 6 hours after coitus. It can lead to toxic shock syndrome if left in place for more than 24 hours (rarely).

questions.question:
Which of the following is a second-generation intra-uterine device?

1. Lippes loop

2. Mirena

3. Nova T

4. Progestasert

5. Cu-T-380 Ag
questions.explanation:
Nova T and Cu-T-380 Ag are second-generation intrauterine devices (IUD).

IUD is a contraceptive method inserted into the uterine cavity. The different generations of IUDs include:

• First-generation IUDs – inert or non-medicated devices like Lippes loop

• Second-generation IUDs - medicated with metallic elements like copper eg: Cu-T-220 C, Nova T, Multi-load Cu-250, Multi-load Cu-375

• Third-generation IUDs – hormone-containing IUDs like progestasert, Mirena (LNG-20)

questions.question: Which of the following women will not be considered ideal candidates for IUD insertion?
options: A woman in a monogamous relationship
A woman with no access to follow up
A woman who has at least one living child
questions.answer: C. A woman with no access to follow up
questions.explanation:
A woman with no access to follow-up is not considered an ideal candidate for IUD insertion.

An ideal candidate for an IUD must have the following attributes:

• Has at least one child

• No history of pelvic disease

• Normal menstrual periods

• Must be willing to check IUD tail

• Has access to follow up and for treatment of potential problems

• Is in a monogamous relationship

questions.question: A patient who underwent an IUD insertion is most likely to develop which of the following in the future?
questions.explanation:
Patients who underwent IUD insertion are most likely to develop vaginal bleeding in the future.

Side effects and complications of IUDs include:

• Vaginal bleeding – most common

• Abdominal pain – second most common

• Pelvic infection

• Uterine perforation

• Pregnancy - due to failure of contraception

• Ectopic pregnancy

• Expulsion of the IUD

• Cancer and teratogenicity

questions.question:
Insertion of an IUD is not contraindicated in patients with which of the following conditions?

1. PID

2. Cardiac problems

3. Carcinoma cervix

4. Anemia

5. Uterine fibroids
questions.explanation:
Cardiac problems are not a contraindication for IUD usage.

Contraindications for IUD usage include:

Absolute contraindications

Relative contraindications

• Suspected pregnancy

• PID

• Vaginal bleeding of unknown etiology

• Carcinoma cervix /uterus/adnexa /other pelvic tumors

• Anemia

• Menorrhagia

• History of PID since the last pregnancy

• Purulent cervical discharge

• Distortions of the uterine cavity due to fibroids

• Uterine malformations

• An unmotivated person

questions.explanation:
Cu-T-380 A has the longest period of use (10 years).

questions.question: You have prescribed an IUCD to a multiparous woman. Which of the following is not a mechanism of action for this type of contraceptive?
questions.explanation:
Prevention of ovulation is not a mechanism of action of IUCDs.

Mechanisms of action of IUCDs include:

• Causing cellular and biochemical changes in the uterus and endometrium.

• Prevention of sperm penetration due to changes in cervical mucus consistency.

• Prevention of implantation by making the uterus hostile to it.

questions.question: All of the following are non-contraceptive benefits of oral contraceptive pills except?
questions.explanation:
Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) do not confer protection against thyroid dysfunction.

OCP usage can confer protection against:

• Benign breast diseases like fibroadenoma and fibrocystic disease

• Ovarian cysts

• Iron-deficiency anemia

• Pelvic inflammatory disease

• Ectopic pregnancy

• Ovarian cancer

questions.question: In patients with which of the following conditions can OCPs be safely prescribed?
questions.explanation:
Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) is not a contraindication for prescribing OCPs.

Absolute contraindications of OCPs: (CULT)

• Cancers - breast and genital

• Cardiac abnormalities

• Congenital hyperlipidemia

• Undiagnosed AUB

• Liver disease

• Thromboembolism - past or present history.

Medical surveillance is required while prescribing OCPs if the patient is/or has:

• Age more than 40 years

• Chronic smoker and age over 35 years

• Amenorrhea

• Chronic renal disease

• Diabetes mellitus

• Epilepsy

• In the first 6 months of nursing

• Gall bladder disease

• History of infrequent bleeding

• Mild hypertension

• Migraine

questions.question: A sexually active woman who was using barrier contraceptives is planning on switching to DMPA injectables. Which of the following is the correct dosage of this contraceptive?
questions.explanation:
The dosage for injectable depot-medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) is 150 mg every 3 months.

It acts by:

• Bringing changes in the cervical mucus

• Making the endometrium hostile

• Preventing ovulation

Disadvantages include spotting and intermediate per vaginal bleeding.

questions.question: Which of the following is also known as the Billings method of contraception?
questions.explanation:
Billings method of contraception is also known as the cervical mucus method (or ovulation method).

It is a natural method of contraception. It is based on the observation of changes in the cervical mucus. At ovulation, the mucus is watery clear, smooth, slippery and profuse. After ovulation, it becomes thicker and scarce.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most effective natural method of contraception?
questions.explanation:
The most effective natural method of contraception is the symptothermic method.

It combines:

• Calendar method

• Cervical mucus method

• Basal body method.

In this method, if a woman is not able to identify one sign, she can double-check with her interpretation of the other signs.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a condition to be fulfilled by a male patient undergoing sterilization?
options: Has at least one living child
Age should be more than 60 years
questions.answer: C. Age should be more than 60 years
questions.explanation:
A man should be below 60 years of age to be eligible for sterilization.

Eligibility for male sterilization:

• Clients should be at least 22 years old

• Clients should be below the age of 60 years

• Clients should be married

• The couple should have at least one child, whose age is above one year unless the sterilization is medically indicated

• Clients or their spouses must not have undergone sterilization in the past (not applicable in the cases of failure of previous sterilization)

• Clients must be in a sound state of mind, so as to understand the full implications of sterilization

• Mentally ill clients must be certified by a psychiatrist, and a statement should be given by the legal guardian/spouse regarding the soundness of the client's state of mind

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of failure of vasectomy?
questions.explanation:
The most common cause of failure of vasectomy is the mistaken identification of the vas.

This can be avoided by examining a stained smear prepared by squeezing the vas on a glass slide. If facilities are available a histological examination is preferred.

Causes of failure of vasectomy include:

• Mistaken identification of the vas - most common

• Spontaneous recanalization of the vas

• Presence of more than one vas on one side

• Sexual intercourse before the disappearance of sperms from the reproductive tracts

questions.question: Which of the following is important in the calculation of the pearl index?
options: Total number of women in the population
questions.explanation:
The numerator used for calculation of the pearl index is total accidental pregnancies.

Pearl index = Total accidental pregnancies x 1200/Total months of exposure

questions.question: As part of the National family planning program, you are conducting a study in a village to gather data on the efficacy of a new contraceptive. 20 out of 100 women became pregnant in the village despite using this contraceptive for a period of 2 years continuously. What is the pearl index of this contraceptive?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, the pearl index is 10 per HWY.

Here, the total number of accidental pregnancies is 20. The total months of exposure are 24 months for each woman.

Hence, the total months of exposure for 100 women are 24 x 100 = 2400.

Pearl index = Total accidental pregnancies x 1200/ Total months of exposure

Hence, pearl index= 20 x 1200/2400 = 10 per HWY

questions.question: Out of 100 women who took oral contraceptive pills for contraception, 10 women got pregnant within 24 months. What is the Pearl index?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, the pearl index is 5 per HWY.

Here, the total number of accidental pregnancies is 10. There are 100 couples who are exposed to the method.

So, the total months of exposure are 24 months x 100 = 2400.

Pearl index = Total accidental pregnancies x 1200/Total months of exposure

Hence, pearl index = 10 x 1200/2400 = 5 per HWY.

questions.question: A pregnant woman has come for her first antenatal visit at 10 weeks of gestation. How many more antenatal visits does she require to fulfill the minimum requirements as per the Maternal and Child Health program?
questions.explanation:
This patient requires 3 more antenatal visits in order to fulfill the minimum requirements according to the Maternal and Child Health Program (MCH).

The minimum number of antenatal visits according to MCH is 4.

• 1st visit – within 12 weeks, preferably as soon as the pregnancy is suspected.

• 2nd visit – between 14 and 26 weeks

• 3rd visit – between 28 and 34 weeks

• 4th visit – between 36 weeks and term

The minimum number of antenatal visits according to the WHO is 8. Ideally, pregnant women should attend antenatal visits according to the following schedule:

• Once a month during the first 7 months

• Twice a month during the 8th month

• Once a week, thereafter if everything is normal.

questions.question: You are a medical officer in a PHC. A pregnant woman comes to you for regular follow-up during her second trimester. Which of the following will you prescribe for her?
options: 100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid
100 mg elemental iron + 100 mcg folic acid
50 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid
60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg of folic acid
questions.answer: D. 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg of folic acid
questions.explanation: As per the Anemia Mukt Bharat program, pregnant women should be given 60 mg of elemental iron and 500 mcg of folic acid in the II trimester. It should be started from the 4th month of pregnancy and continued for 180 days post-partum.

questions.question: What is the average weight gain during pregnancy in Indian women with inadequate calorie intake?
questions.explanation:
Weight gain during pregnancy in women with inadequate calorie intake is around 5 - 6 kgs.

Normally, a woman is expected to gain around 9-11 kgs of weight during pregnancy. An inadequate dietary intake can be suspected if the woman gains < 2 kg/ month.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about congenital syphilis?
options: It can be prevented by procaine penicillin administration
Infection of fetus most commonly occurs in the 1st trimester
Neurological damage with mental retardation is a serious complication
Chances of transmission are lower if mother has late syphilis
questions.answer: B. Infection of fetus most commonly occurs in the 1st trimester
questions.explanation:
The chances of transmission of syphilis during pregnancy is highest after 6th month of gestation. It does not occur before the 4th month.

It is routine to test the mother for syphilis in antenatal clinics during her first visit. The chance of infection of the fetus is higher when the mother is suffering from early (primary or secondary) syphilis and are lower in case of late syphilis. Neurological damage with mental retardation is a serious complication of congenital syphilis. It can be prevented by procaine penicillin administration.

questions.question: The District Maternal Death Review Committee is reviewing the number of maternal deaths in the district during 2020. In order to calculate the maternal mortality ratio, what other parameter is required?
options: Total women in child bearing age
questions.explanation: The maternal mortality ratio is calculated using the number of maternal deaths and total live births.

questions.question: Which of the following maternal deaths is not included when calculating the maternal mortality ratio?
options: Death of a 30-year-old woman following spontaneous abortion at 11 weeks of gestation
Death of a 24-year-old woman due to ruptured ectopic pregnancy
Death of a 26-year-old woman following a road traffic accident at 36 weeks of gestation
Death of a 21-year-woman following secondary PPH on postpartum day 14
questions.answer: C. Death of a 26-year-old woman following a road traffic accident at 36 weeks of gestation
questions.explanation: The death of a pregnant woman following a road traffic accident is not included when calculating the maternal mortality ratio. It includes all deaths anytime during pregnancy or within 42 days of termination from any cause related to or aggravated by the pregnancy.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of maternal deaths in India?
questions.explanation: The most common cause of maternal deaths in India is hemorrhage.

questions.question:
In a town, there were 2500 live births in a period of 6 months. During the same period, 15 women died due to the following causes. What is the maternal mortality ratio?

Peripartum infection - 5

Electrocution - 5

Obstructed labor - 2

Postpartum hemorrhage - 3
questions.explanation:
The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) of this town is 400 per 100,000 live births.

Maternal mortality refers to deaths during pregnancy or 42 days within termination, from causes related to pregnancy. Hence, in this town, there were 10 maternal deaths (peripartum infection, PPH, obstructed labor).

MMR = Number of maternal deaths in a period x 100,000 / Number of live births in the same period

Hence, MMR = 10 x 100000/2500 = 400 per 100,000 live births

questions.question: A baby was delivered at home in a village. Until which day of life should an ASHA worker visit this baby?
questions.explanation:
Under the Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) guidelines, ASHA workers should visit all newborns up to 42 days of life, according to the following schedule.

Mode of delivery
No. of visits
Schedule of visits

Home delivery
7
Days 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42

Hospital-based normal vaginal delivery
6

Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42

(except day 1)

Hospital-based LSCS delivery
5

Days 7, 14, 21, 28, 42

(except days 1, 3)

During her visits, ASHA workers must record weight, ensure vaccination, and registration of births. On completion of all these visits, they receive an incentive of Rs. 250.

questions.question: What is the best indicator of obstetric and neonatal care given before and around the time of birth?
questions.explanation: The perinatal mortality rate is the best indicator to evaluate obstetric and neonatal care given before and around the time of birth.

questions.question: What is the 2030 target of the India Newborn Action Plan with regards to the stillbirth rate?
questions.explanation:
The India Newborn Action Plan targets to achieve a stillbirth rate of < 10/ 1000 live births and neonatal mortality rate of < 10/ 1000 live births (single-digit SBR and NMR) by 2030.

This program was launched to reduce preventable newborn deaths and stillbirths. It provides the following:

• Pre-conception and antenatal care

• Care during labor and childbirth

• Immediate newborn care

• Care of healthy newborn

• Care of small and sick newborn

• Care beyond newborn survival

questions.question:
A group of health workers are conducting a perinatal mortality audit in a hospital. Which of the following must they take into account to calculate the perinatal mortality rate?

1. No. of live births per year

2. No. of stillbirths over 1000 g per year

3. No. of stillbirths after 22 weeks of gestation

4. No. of early neonatal deaths per year

5. No. of late neonatal deaths per year
questions.explanation:
The perinatal mortality rate (PMR) is calculated using the following parameters during a particular time period:

• Late fetal deaths or stillbirths > 1000 g - correlates to 28 weeks of gestation

• Early neonatal deaths - from birth to 7 days of life

• Live births > 1000 g

The neonatal mortality rate (NMR) refers to the deaths within the first 28 days of life. It is calculated using the following parameters:

• Early neonatal deaths

• Late neonatal deaths - after 7th day but before 28th completed day of life

questions.question: In a given population, 4050 births were recorded over a period of 1 year. Among these, 50 were stillbirths, 50 died in the 1st week of life and 150 died within 8-28 days of life. What is the neonatal mortality rate of this population?
questions.explanation:
The neonatal mortality rate (NMR) of the given population is 50 per 1000 live births.

Neonatal mortality rate = No. of deaths of neonates < 28 days within a year x 1000 / Total live births in the same year

In this population, there were 4000 live births (no. of total births - no. of stillbirths).

NMR = (50+150) x 1000/4000 = 100/2 = 50

questions.question: Which of the following is the leading cause of neonatal mortality?
questions.explanation: Prematurity is the leading cause of neonatal mortality.

questions.question: In children aged 1 month to 1 year, all of the following are common causes of mortality except:
questions.explanation: Tetanus is not a common cause of mortality in children between the age of 1 month to 1 year (post-neonatal period). The main causes of post-neonatal deaths are diarrhea, respiratory infections, and malnutrition.

questions.question:
In a given population, there were 5100 births during the year 2020. Of these, 100 babies were stillborn. Among the living children, the following deaths were recorded. Calculate the infant mortality rate for this population.

Time of death
No. of deaths

1st week of life
150

8-28 days of life
150

1st year of life
500
questions.explanation:
The infant mortality rate (IMR) for this population is 100 / 1000 live births.

IMR = No. of deaths within 1st year of life over a period of time x 1000 / No. of live births in the same period

In this population, there were 5000 live births (5100 – 100) and 500 deaths within the 1st year of life.

Hence, IMR = 500 x 1000/5000 = 100 per 1000 live births

questions.question: Which of the following is true for a newborn stabilization unit?
options: It is located in the delivery room.
It is for sick babies and LBW babies < 1800 g
It is present in all community health centres
All cases except major surgeries are managed here
questions.answer: C. It is present in all community health centres
questions.explanation:
A newborn stabilization unit is present in all community health centers (CHC).

India accounts for 30% of neonatal deaths globally and 73.3% of these deaths occur in 1st week of life. To address this issue, the following facility-based newborn care services were introduced:

questions.question: You are a doctor at a child health clinic. You will consider all of the following children as at-risk infants except:
options: A 15-day-old baby with birth weight of 2.4 kgs
An 8-month-old baby being raised by a working mother
questions.answer: A. A 2-month-old baby with 3 older siblings
questions.explanation:
The 2-month-old baby with 3 older siblings has a birth order of 4. Infants with birth order of 5 or more are considered at-risk infants.

The following are considered at-risk infants:

• Birth weight < 2.5 kgs

• Twins

• Birth order of 5 or more

• Artificial feeding

• Weight below 70% of the expected weight

• Failure to gain weight during 3 successive months

• Children with protein-energy malnutrition (PEM), diarrhea

• Working mother or single parent

questions.question: A researcher is calculating the child survival indices for different populations. Which of the following should he use for calculating the same?
questions.explanation: The under-5 mortality rate is used in the calculation of the child survival index. It is calculated as (1000 – Under-5 mortality rate)/10.

questions.question: Identify the false statement about the following tool:
options: Malnutrition can be detected even before signs and symptoms appear
It provides an objective basis for policy making on child healthcare
It can be used to teach the importance of adequate feeding
It can be used to indicate proof of government aid
questions.answer: D. It can be used to indicate proof of government aid
questions.explanation:
The given image shows a growth chart. It is not used as proof of government aid.

The uses of growth charts are as follows:

• Growth monitoring and diagnosis - can detect malnutrition before clinical features appear

• Educational tool - to teach parents about the importance of adequate feeding.

• Objective basis for planning and policy-making on child healthcares

questions.question: A juvenile delinquent was sentenced by the court to be placed in a center under the care of a doctor and psychiatrist. Which of the following fulfills this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A remand home is an establishment where children are placed under the care of a doctor, psychiatrist and other trained personnel.

An orphanage or shelter home is an institution where children who have no home or parents or for some reason can’t be cared for are placed.

Foster homes are arrangements where a family or a couple takes care of a child on a temporary basis.

Borstal is a place that falls between a certified institution and a prison. It is where boys > 16 years who have misbehaved or are too difficult to handle are sent.

questions.question: The police authorities rescued a girl from being trafficked for sexual exploitation. She is identified to be a refugee. As a part of the Ujjawala scheme, which of the following benefits will she not receive?
questions.explanation:
The girl will not receive remuneration (monetary compensation) under the Ujjawala scheme.

The Ujjawala scheme was launched to combat women and child trafficking in India. The components of the scheme include:

• Prevention of trafficking by awareness, vigilance, education

• Rescue of victims from the place of exploitation

• Rehabilitation of victims

• Re-integration of victims into their family and society

• Repatriation of cross-border victims to their place of origin

Some other legislations associated with children in India are:

• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009

• Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000

• Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended in 2006 and 2016)

• Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO), 2012 under the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)

• Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006

questions.question: A 4-year-old girl was brought by her parents who tell you that she fell down while playing. On examination, bruises and ecchymoses of varying ages are noted all over the body. An x-ray showed a spiral fracture of the right femur. Which of the following programs can provide support services to this child and prevent further such incidents?
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario points towards child abuse. The INSPIRE strategy was introduced to eliminate such violence against children and also provide support services.

It refers to a set of 7 evidence-based strategies to eliminate violence against children:

Strategies
Approach

I
Implementation and enforcement of laws

• Banning violent punishment of children and criminalizing sexual abuse

• Preventing alcohol misuse and limiting youth access to weapons

N
Norms and values

• Changing perceptions about harmful gender and social norms

S
Safe environments

• Reducing the spread of violence

P
Parent and caregiver support

• Delivered through home visits and in groups in community settings

I
Income and economic strengthening

• Cash transfers

• Providing small loans

R
Response and support services

• Counseling and therapy

• Treatment programs for juvenile offenders

• Foster care interventions

E
Education and life skills

• Increasing enrolment in schools

• Establishing safe school environments

• Improving sexual education for children and teaching self-defense strategies

questions.question: As a PHC medical officer, which of the following groups would you target as a part of Kishori Shakti Yojana?
questions.explanation:
The Kishori Shakti Yojana (KSY) program is aimed at adolescent girls (11-18 years).

This program is a component of the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme and is a redesign of the already existing Adolescent Girls (AG) scheme.

The objectives of KSY are:

• To improve the nutrition, health, and development status

• To promote awareness on health, hygiene, nutrition, and family care

• To teach life skills and encourage school attendance

• To help understand their social environment

• Aspects aimed at empowerment and enhanced self-perception

• To help them take initiatives to become productive members of society

It also fosters convergence with other sectoral programs, addressing the interrelated needs of adolescent girls and women.

questions.question: A 68-year-old man visits your outpatient clinic for a routine follow-up. Which of the following protocols would you use to assess his health literacy?
questions.explanation:
The SPEAK protocol is used to assess health literacy in the geriatric population in a clinical setting.

Health literacy is defined as the degree to which individuals have the capacity to obtain, process, and understand basic health information needed to make appropriate health decisions. The SPEAK protocol provides a simple framework that healthcare providers can use to assess literacy. SPEAK stands for:

• S - Speech

• P - Perception

• E - Education

• A - Access

• K - Knowledge

Option A: The GATHER approach is mainly used for counseling (usually, family planning and reproductive counseling) to help people make decisions about health. It stands for:

• G – Greet

• A – Ask

• T – Tell

• H – Help

• E – Explain

• R – Return

Option C: The SPIKES protocol is used to convey distressing information and break bad news in an organized manner to patients and families. It stands for:

• S - Setting

• P - Perception

• I - Invitation or information

• K - Knowledge

• E - Empathy

• S - Summarizing or strategizing.

Option D: The S-BAR technique is used for prompt and appropriate communication among health care workers in hospital settings. It stands for:

• S - Situation

• B - Background

• A - Assessment

• R - Recommendation

questions.question: Which of the following comes under the Rashtriya Varishth Jan Swasthya Yojana?
options: Domiciliary visits to homes of elderly in the community by ANMs or male HCWs
Rehabilitation units with physiotherapy at CHCs
Super-specialty geriatric departments for training, guidelines and referral
Weekly geriatric clinics arranged at PHCs by medical officer
questions.answer: C. Super-specialty geriatric departments for training, guidelines and referral
questions.explanation:
The establishment of super-specialty geriatric departments for training, guidelines, and referral comes under the Rashtriya Varishth Jan Swasthya Yojna (RVJSY). It refers to the tertiary component of the National Programme for Healthcare of the Elderly (NPHCE).

The NPHCE was established for geriatric care and includes provisions at primary, secondary, and tertiary levels.

Centers
 Services according to NPHCE

PHCs (primary)

• Weekly geriatric clinics at PHC

• Treatment of minor ailments

• Referral services to higher centers

Sub-centres (primary)

• ANMs/ male health workers make domiciliary visits to the elderly

• Arrange supportive devices for the disabled

• Treatment of minor ailments

CHCs (secondary)

• Dedicated geriatric clinics twice weekly

• Rehabilitation unit with trained physiotherapists

The tertiary component of the program has been renamed as RVJSY and has the following provisions:

• Geriatrics departments at 20 super specialty institutions-

• 30-bedded inpatient facility and referral treatment

• Research and manpower development,

• Development of training, IEC material, and guidelines

• Geriatric units at district hospitals (tertiary) -

• 10 bedded geriatric ward

• Dedicated geriatric OPD

questions.question: Which of the following parameters is not indicative of reference Indian adult woman?
questions.explanation: According to the 2020 guidelines of the National Institute of Nutrition, the weight of the reference Indian adult woman is 55 kg.

questions.question: The energy required by an adult for basal metabolism is:
questions.answer: A. 1 kcal/ hour/ kg body weight
questions.explanation: The energy required by an adult for basal metabolism is 1 kcal/ hour/ kg of body weight.

questions.question: What is the likely energy requirement of a pregnant woman who leads a moderately active lifestyle?
questions.explanation:
The energy requirement of a pregnant woman who leads a moderately active lifestyle is around 2500 kcal/day.

An adult woman leading a moderately active lifestyle requires 2130 kcal daily and an additional 350 kcal is needed in pregnancy. Hence, the total requirement for a moderately working pregnant woman is 2480 kcal/ day (approximately 2500 kcal/ day).

questions.question: A nutritionist is preparing a meal plan for a healthy 32-year-old man. Which of the following principles must she follow?
options: Proteins must constitute 15-30% of the daily energy intake
Fats must constitute 10-15% of the daily energy intake
Carbohydrate requirement must be met first followed by protein and fat
The proportion of nutrients in the diet must be carbohydrates > fats > proteins
questions.answer: D. The proportion of nutrients in the diet must be carbohydrates > fats > proteins
questions.explanation:
The proportion of nutrients in the diet must be carbohydrates > fats > proteins.

While constructing a balanced diet, nutrient requirements must be calculated in the following sequence:

1. Protein requirements - 10-15% of daily energy intake

2. Fat requirement - 15-30% of daily energy intake

3. Carbohydrates - remaining food energy

questions.question: What is the daily requirement of high-quality protein for a 40-year-old man weighing 60 kgs?
questions.explanation:
This man requires 50 g/day of high-quality protein.

High-quality protein refers to proteins containing all the essential amino acids. According to the FAO/WHO 2007 guidelines, the recommended high-quality protein intake for adult men and women is 0.83 g/kg/day. This man weighs 60 kgs. Hence he requires around 50 g (0.83*60 = 49.8) of high-quality protein per day.

questions.question: A dietary protein-energy percentage of which of the following is the threshold for inadequate protein intake?
questions.explanation:
Dietary protein-energy percentage (PE %) < 4% indicates inadequate protein intake. The PE % indicates the proportion of total energy in the diet that is derived from proteins.

PE % = (Energy from protein / Total energy in the diet) * 100

questions.question: Which of the following is the best indicator of protein quality?
options: Protein digestibility corrected amino acid score
questions.answer: B. Digestible indispensable amino acid score
questions.explanation:
Digestible indispensable amino acid score (DIAAS) is the best indicator for protein quality.

DIAAS reflects the digestibility of individual amino acids in the protein. Total protein digestibility does not always reflect the digestibility of individual dietary indispensable amino acids. Hence, DIAAS has replaced the PDCAAS (protein digestibility corrected amino acid score) as the preferred index for the evaluation of protein quality.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest net protein utilization value?
questions.explanation:
Among the given options, meat has the highest net protein utilization (NPU).

The NPU values of various food items in descending order are:

• Egg - 100

• Meat - 80

• Milk - 75

• Rice - 65

• Soya - 61

Low NPU indicates a high protein requirement. The NPU of Indian diets is usually between 50 and 80.

questions.question: A farmer has been consuming a maize-rich diet for many years. Which of the following would be lacking in his diet?
questions.explanation:
His diet would be lacking lysine and tryptophan as maize is deficient in these amino acids.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: You are counseling a diabetic patient to consume foods with low glycemic index. Which of the following would you advise him to eat?
questions.explanation:
The patient should be advised to eat whole grains since it has a low glycemic index (GI).

GI is a number representing the relative ability of a carbohydrate food to increase the level of glucose in the blood. It is calculated by comparing the test carbohydrate to the standard (glucose or white bread). This measure has practical use in the management of diabetes and obesity.

• Low GI foods – most fruits and vegetables, whole grains, pasta foods, beans, and lentils.

• Moderate GI foods – sucrose, basmati rice, and brown rice.

• High GI foods – corn flakes, baked potatoes, white bread, potatoes, watermelon, candies, and syrupy foods.

questions.question: In the Indian population, individuals with BMI falling between which range are defined as overweight?
questions.explanation:
In the Indian (Asian) population, a BMI of 23-24.99 is classified as overweight.

However, in the global population, a BMI of 25-29.99 is considered overweight.

questions.question:
Which of the following indicators are used in Waterlow’s classification?

1. Weight for age

2. Height for age

3. Weight for height

4. BMI for age

5. Head circumference for age
questions.explanation:
Waterlow’s classification makes use of height for age (HFA) and weight for height (WFH) to assess the nutritional status of children.

HFA indicates stunting and denotes the chronicity of malnutrition. On the other hand, WFH indicates wasting and denotes the severity of malnutrition.

The Gomez classification uses weight for age as an indicator of nutritional status. The disadvantage is that it is difficult to determine whether the low weight is due to an acute attack of malnutrition or chronic undernutrition.

questions.question: A patient presents with the following skin finding. You would advise supplementation with which of the following?
options: Vitamin B complex and vitamin K
Safflower oil and vitamin B complex
questions.answer: D. Safflower oil and vitamin B complex
questions.explanation:
The image shows rough, dry skin suggestive of phrynoderma. It is treated by supplementation of safflower oil (rich in essential fatty acids) and vitamin B complex.

Phrynoderma or toad skin is a type of follicular hyperkeratosis. It is caused by a deficiency of vitamin E, B, A, C, and essential fatty acids.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest content of thiamine?
questions.explanation:
Gingelly (sesame) seeds have the highest content of thiamine.

The thiamine content in various foods in decreasing order are as follows:

• Gingelly seeds

• Groundnut

• Bengal gram

• Whole wheat

• Raw rice

Thiamine is lost from rice during the process of milling. As it is a water-soluble vitamin, washing, and cooking rice cause further losses. Hence, it is advisable to avoid highly polished rice and eat parboiled or under-milled rice.

questions.question: A patient presented with loose stools and skin rashes over the sun-exposed areas. Diet history revealed that the patient had been consuming a jowar-rich diet since childhood. This condition results due to excess of which amino acid in the diet?
questions.explanation:
This clinical scenario is suggestive of pellagra. It is caused by the excess of leucine in jowar.

Excess of leucine in jowar (sorghum) and maize interferes with the conversion of tryptophan to niacin causing pellagra. It presents with the following features:

• Diarrhea

• Dermatitis (sun-exposed areas)

• Dementia

People consuming jowar also have a higher risk of developing genu valgum and osteoporosis due to greater retention of ingested fluoride.

questions.question: What is the recommended daily allowance of vitamin A for a 9-month old baby?
questions.explanation: The RDA of vitamin A for infants is 350 mcg.

questions.question: Vitamin A deficiency is considered a public health problem if the prevalence of corneal xerosis among children aged 6 months - 6 years is more than:
questions.explanation:
Vitamin A deficiency is considered a public health problem if the prevalence rate of corneal xerosis among children between 6 months to 6 years (high-risk category) is more than 0.01%.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding the epidemiological assessment of iodine deficiency?
options: Median urinary iodine excretion <200 μg/ L indicates insufficient iodine intake
Neonatal hypothyroidism is a sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency
Serum T4 level is a more sensitive indicator of thyroid insufficiency than T3
Quality control of salt is performed by rapid testing with MBI kit
questions.answer: A. Median urinary iodine excretion <200 μg/ L indicates insufficient iodine intake
questions.explanation:
Median urinary iodine excretion level < 100 μg/L (in non-pregnant population) indicates insufficient iodine intake.

Urinary excretion of iodine is used by the WHO for surveillance and epidemiological studies to classify countries according to the level of iodine deficiency. It is an effective indicator of national programmes against iodine deficiency.

Neonatal hypothyroidism is a sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency. It is also an effective indicator to monitor the impact of a programme. Serum T4 level is a more sensitive indicator of thyroid insufficiency in the population than T3.

Determination of iodine in salt is a part of the quality control of the product. The UNICEF uses MBI kits to rapidly assess the levels of iodine in salt.

questions.question: What is the recommended dietary allowance of folic acid for a 5-year-old child?
questions.explanation: The recommended dietary allowance of folic acid in a 5-year-old child is 135μg.

questions.question: Under the Anemia Mukt Bharat programme, what dose of iron and folic acid tablets will you prescribe for a 6-year-old child?
options: 20 mg iron and 100 mcg folic acid
45 mg iron and 400 mcg folic acid
50 mg iron and 350 mcg folic acid
100 mg iron and 500 mcg folic acid
questions.answer: B. 45 mg iron and 400 mcg folic acid
questions.explanation: Under the Anemia Mukt Bharat programme, a 6-year-old child should be given 45 mg elemental iron + 400 mcg folic acid (1 iron and folic acid tablet weekly). The tablet is sugar-coated and pink in color.

questions.question: How much calcium does a premenopausal woman require on a daily basis?
questions.explanation: A premenopausal woman requires 1000 mg calcium on a daily basis.

questions.question: Individuals with fluoride intake above which of the following are at risk of developing crippling fluorosis?
questions.explanation:
Individuals with fluoride intake > 10 mg/L are at risk of developing crippling fluorosis.

Complications of fluorosis seen with corresponding levels of fluoride intake are:

• Dental fluorosis - 1.5 mg/L

• Skeletal fluorosis - 3-6 mg/L

• Crippling fluorosis - > 10 mg/L

Genu valgum may occur in people who consume jowar (sorghum), as it promotes greater retention of ingested fluoride.

The Nalgonda technique is used for the defluoridation of water bodies. It involves the addition of lime and alum followed by flocculation, sedimentation, and filtration.
