questions.question: Which of the following is true about pathogenic mosquitoes?
questions.explanation:
Aedes and Anopheles lay eggs singly.

Culex lays eggs in rafts and Mansonia lays eggs in star-shaped clusters.

Anopheles has spotted wings while the other pathogenic species have unspotted wings.

Aedes transmits yellow fever, dengue and chikungunya. Culex is the main vector for JE and filariasis.

questions.question: You are posted in a PHC in a coastal region as a part of your rural postings. Which of the following Anopheles species is most commonly found here?
questions.explanation:
Anopheles stephensi and Anopheles sundaicus are found in coastal regions.

Anopheles stephensi is also the main vector of malaria in urban regions. Anopheles culicifacies and Anopheles philippinensis are found in the plains. Anopheles fluviatilis and Anopheles minimus are found in foot-hill regions.

questions.question: Which of the following species of Anopheles mosquitoes transmits urban malaria?
questions.explanation: Urban malaria is transmitted by Anopheles stephensi.

questions.question: What is the distance around an airport or seaport that has to be kept free of all mosquitoes?
questions.explanation: The distance around an airport or seaport that has to be kept free of all mosquitoes is 400 metres. This helps in limiting the spread of vector-borne diseases to new geographic regions.

questions.question: Identify the following vector.
questions.explanation: The given image is of a housefly, whose scientific name is Musca domestica.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a method of disease transmission by houseflies?
questions.explanation:
Houseflies do not transmit diseases by biting. They transmit diseases by mechanical transmission by their legs or feet, vomit drop, and defecation.

They transmit a variety of diseases like:

• Typhoid

• Polio

• Dysentery

• Amoebiasis

• Anthrax

• Yaws

questions.question: Which disease is transmitted by the following vector that is found in cracks and crevices of walls in the day time?
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a sandfly. It transmits visceral leishmaniasis.

Note: Sandfly acts as a vector for the following diseases:

• Kala-azar

• Oriental sore

• Sandfly fever

• Oroya fever

Japanese encephalitis is transmitted by the Culex mosquito. Dengue is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito.

Trypanosomiasis is transmitted by the tsetse fly.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by the vector shown in the image given below?
questions.explanation:
The vector shown in the image is a tsetse fly. It transmits African sleeping sickness (African human trypanosomiasis).

Tsetse flies belong to the genus Glossina. They have not demonstrated insecticide resistance. Methods of tsetse fly control include spraying of DDT, clearing of vegetation, destruction of wild game and genetic control.

questions.question: A patient presents with blurring of vision and a painless swelling over his left elbow which has gradually been increasing in size over the past 1 year. On examination, he is noted to have patchy depigmentation on his legs. Which of the following vectors transmits the disease he's suffering from?
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of onchocerciasis, also known as river blindness. It is transmitted by blackfly.

The usual presentation of onchocerciasis is the formation of a subcutaneous nodule or onchocercoma. It is a firm non-tender nodule arising from bony sites like the scalp, elbow, ribs, and iliac crest. It is associated with pruritus and rashes. Patients also present with patchy depigmentation on the legs called leopard skin.

The presence of microfilaria in the eye causes photophobia and gradual loss of vision. The most severe manifestations are sclerosing keratitis and chorioretinitis which can lead to blindness.

Blackfly is also called Simulium. It has a flight range of almost 100 miles, making control of adult flies difficult. Abate is widely used as a larvicidal insecticide. The image given below shows a blackfly.

questions.question: Spot the wrongly matched arthropod and disease.
questions.explanation:
Blackflies (Simulium) are the vector for onchocerciasis and not Chaga's disease.

An arthropod or an invertebrate that transmits infection is called a vector. It transmits infection by:

• Inoculation into or through the skin or mucous membrane

• Biting

• Deposit of infective materials on skin or food or other objects

Note: Chagas disease is transmitted by the reduviid bugs or kissing bugs or triatomines.

chapters.chapter: Medical Entomology Ticks, Fleas And Mites

questions.question: A veterinarian with fever, chills, and myalgia is diagnosed with Q fever. Which of the following is the most common reservoir of this disease?
questions.explanation:
Ticks are the most common reservoir of Q fever.

Coxiella burnetii is the causative pathogen. The most commonly identified sources of human infection are farm animals, such as cattle, goats, and sheep.

Infected mammals shed C. burnetii in their urine, feces, milk, and placenta. Human exposure to C. burnetii may occur as a result of inhalation of contaminated aerosols arising from the placenta or parturient fluids of infected livestock or from contaminated secretions on the surface of newborn animals.

People working with farm animals and veterinarians are at a higher risk of infection.

questions.question: Which of the following is not transmitted by hard ticks?
questions.explanation: Relapsing fever is not transmitted by hard ticks, but by soft ticks.

questions.question: Peripheral smear of a patient with high grade fever, arthralgia, and myalgia is given below. Which of the following transmits this disease?
questions.explanation: The given clinical scenario with peripheral smear showing maltese cross appearance is suggestive of babesiosis. It is transmitted by ticks.

questions.question: A patient with fever and joint pain presented with the following lesion on his left leg. Which of the following transmits this disease?
questions.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the image showing bulls eye rash is suggestive of Lyme disease. It is transmitted by Ixodes tick.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about the vector in the given image?
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a soft tick. It can withstand starvation for over a year.

The head of the soft tick lies ventrally and it does not have a scutum. It serves as a reservoir for Q fever and transmits relapsing fever.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about the vector in the given image?
options: Its nymphal stage has seven stages
It lays hundreds of eggs at once
questions.answer: C. Its nymphal stage has seven stages
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a hard tick. The hard tick has only one nymphal stage.

It has a hard chitinous shield called the scutum which covers the entire back in males a small portion in the front in females. It feeds night and day and cannot withstand starvation. It lays several hundreds or thousands of eggs in one sitting.

questions.question: Which of the following are also known as chiggers?
questions.explanation:
Larval forms of trombiculid mites are also known as chiggers.

They are spider-like arthropods which are vectors for scrub typhus. The image given below shows trombiculid mite.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by the vector shown in the image given below?
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a reduviid bug. It transmits American trypanosomiasis, also known as Chagas disease.

Reduviid bug is also known as the kissing bug or triatomine bug. It lives in cracks, fissures and other spaces in the walls and ceilings of human dwellings. Residual spraying with HCH or dieldrin is used for the control of these bugs.

Option B: African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) is transmitted by the tsetse fly.

Option C: Onchocerciasis is transmitted by the blackfly (Simulium).

Option D: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is transmitted by the sandfly.

questions.question: A 10-year-old boy presents with complaints of nocturnal pruritus. Examination shows burrows over the skin of his hands. KOH mount prepared from these lesions is given below. Which of the following vectors transmits this disease?
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario and KOH mount showing the itch mite are suggestive of scabies. It is transmitted by itch mite or Sarcoptes scabiei.

The female parasite burrows into the epidermis where it breeds. It is a small parasite, barely visible to the naked eye, with 4 pairs of legs.

Its life cycle consists of four stages—egg, larva, nymph, and adult stages. Its spread can be through close contact or contaminated clothes.

Benzyl benzoate is very effective as a sarcopticide. HCH, tetmosol, and sulphur ointments are also used.

The image given below shows itch mite.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by mites?
questions.explanation:
Kyasanur forest disease is not transmitted by mites. It is a viral hemorrhagic fever transmitted by hard ticks.

Scabies, scrub typhus, and rickettsial pox are transmitted by mites.

questions.question: You are given the following slide during your community medicine practicals. Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by this vector?
questions.explanation:
The above image is of a head louse. It does not transmit endemic typhus which is transmitted by fleas.

Lice transmit epidemic typhus, relapsing fever, and trench fever.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by lice?
questions.explanation:
Epidemic typhus is transmitted by lice and caused by Rickettsia prowazekii.

Murine typhus is transmitted by the rat flea. Tick typhus is transmitted by a hard tick. Scrub typhus is transmitted by trombiculid mite.

questions.question: Which of the following is not transmitted by lice?
questions.explanation:
Q fever is not transmitted by lice. It is spread by the inhalation of contaminated aerosols containing Coxiella burnetti.

Soft ticks are the most common reservoirs of Q fever. The aerosols arise from the placenta or parturient fluids of infected livestock or from contaminated secretions on the surface of newborn animals.

questions.question: Identify the following vector which transmits murine typhus.
questions.explanation: The given image is of a rat flea-Xenopsylla cheopis. It transmits murine typhus.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is not transmitted by rat fleas?
questions.explanation:
Pneumonic plague is not transmitted by rat fleas. It is transmitted by inhalation of aerosolized droplets.

Rat fleas are vectors for murine or endemic typhus, bubonic plague, and hymenolepiasis caused by Hymenolepis nana and Hymenolepis diminuta.

questions.question: A flea survey is being conducted in an area prone to outbreaks of plague. Which of the following indices is not used for this purpose?
questions.explanation:
Incidence of plague is not an index used in flea surveys. Flea indices that are used in flea surveys are:

• General flea index

• Specific flea index

• Percentage incidence of flea species

• Rodent infestation rate

questions.question: Which of the following is true about sand fleas?
questions.explanation:
Sand fleas cause ulcers in the feet.

They are also called jigger or chigoe fleas. The species called Tunga penetrans is of particular importance as it causes tungiasis.

The fertilized female burrows into the skin of the feet, often beneath the nail and causes ulcers. Tetanus and gas gangrene frequently occur because of secondary infection.

They flourish best in sandy soil and are found in the western parts of India.

The below image shows a sand flea.

questions.question: Which of the following is transmitted by the vector shown in the image given below?
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a cyclops or water flea. It is the vector for guinea worm disease or dracunculiasis and fish tapeworm infection.

Humans are infected with these diseases by drinking water that contains cyclops. Its average life span is 3 months.

Physical methods like straining and boiling of water can ensure the killing of this organism. Chemicals that can be used to control cyclops are chlorine, lime, and abate. Biological methods include Gambusia fish and barbel fish.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is not associated with rodents?
questions.explanation:
Ascariasis is not associated with rodents.

Diseases related to rodents are:

• Bacterial -

• Plague

• Tularemia

• Salmonellosis

• Leptospirosis

• Rat-bite fever

• Viral -

• Lassa fever

• Encephalitis

• Hemorrhagic fever

• Rickettsial -

• Scrub typhus

• Endemic typhus

• Rickettsial pox

• Parasitic -

• Hymenolepis diminuta

• Leishmaniasis

• Amoebiasis

• Trichinosis

• Chagas disease

• Fungal -

• Histoplasmosis

• Ringworm

questions.question: Which of the following would you advise as the best approach to control arthropods?
questions.explanation:
Environmental control is the best approach to control arthropods.

The principles of arthropod control include:

• Environmental control - Best approach

• Chemical control - Use of insecticides, pesticides, etc.

• Biological control - Use of larvivorous fish like Gambusia

• Genetic control

• Newer methods -

• Chemosterilants

• Insect growth regulators

• Sex attractants

• Integrated approach involves usage of more than one modality of arthropod control

questions.question: Which of the following is the best method to control houseflies?
questions.explanation:
The best method to control houseflies is environmental control by the elimination of breeding places.

They have shown resistance to a number of insecticides, including DDT.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an organo-phosphate insecticide?
questions.explanation: Dieldrin is an organo-chlorine insecticide. It is a broad-spectrum insecticide that acts as a contact, stomach, and inhalation poison.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an aryl organo-phosphate insecticide?
questions.explanation: Malathion is an alkyl organophosphate insecticide. It is used as an ultra-low volume spray in mosquito control.

questions.question: Which of the following insecticides is least toxic to man?
questions.explanation: Among the given options, malathion is the least toxic to man. It is the least toxic organo-phosphate insecticide.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about fenthion?
options: It is used as a residual spray
It is used as a repellent
questions.answer: B. It is used as a repellent
questions.explanation:
Fenthion is not used as a repellant. A commonly used repellant is N,N-diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET) that is used for protection from mosquitoes and ticks.

Fenthion is a broad-spectrum insecticide that acts as both contact and stomach poison. It is used as a larvicide in mosquito control and also as a residual spray.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about pyrethrum?
options: Residual action as good as DDT
Can be used synergistically with DDT
questions.answer: A. Residual action as good as DDT
questions.explanation:
Pyrethrum does not have a residual action like DDT or other synthetic insecticides. So, most space sprays contain pyrethrum and DDT for synergistic action.

Pyrethrum is a natural insecticide of vegetable origin. It is extracted from the flowers of Chrysanthemum cinerariafolium. It kills adult mosquitoes and other insects instantly on mere contact.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be used to describe pyrethrum?
questions.explanation: Pyrethrum is not used as a residual spray. It is a contact and nerve poison that is also used as a space spray.

questions.question: Which of the following is a synthetic pyrethroid insecticide?
questions.explanation: Permethrin is a synthetic pyrethroid. Pyrethroids are synthetic insecticides, which are derived from naturally occurring pyrethrins. Pyrethroids modify the sodium channels in neuronal membranes and thereby disrupt the electrical signalling in the nervous system.

questions.question: Which of the following vectors has not shown resistance to synthetic pyrethroids, in a widespread manner in India yet?
questions.explanation: Sandflies (Phlebotomus) have not shown resistance to synthetic pyrethroids, in a widespread manner in India yet.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes DDT?
questions.explanation: DDT is a contact poison that belongs to the organochlorine family. It has been widely used but a number of organisms have become resistant to its effects now.

questions.question: During a dengue outbreak, the municipal corporation plans a DDT spraying initiative. Which of the following is false about this insecticide?
options: Para-para isomer is the most active fraction
It has residual action up to 18 months
It causes immediate death of insects
questions.answer: D. It causes immediate death of insects
questions.explanation:
DDT does not cause the immediate death of insects. It takes several hours for its action to be complete.

It contains 70 – 80% of para-para isomer that is the most active fraction of DDT. It acts on the nervous system of insects. The residual action of DDT may last as long as 18 months depending upon the treated surface.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the usage of Paris green for mosquito control?
options: Harmful in normal doses to man and animals
questions.explanation:
Paris green is very effective against surface-feeding Anopheles.

It is an anti-larval measure and is a stomach poison. It is not harmful in normal doses to man and animals.

questions.question: Which of the following mosquitoes can be controlled by destroying aquatic plants with herbicides?
questions.explanation: Mansonia mosquitoes breed in water with aquatic vegetation, and destroying this vegetation with herbicides would control this mosquito.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a mosquito anti-larval measure?
questions.explanation:
Pyrethrum is an anti-adult measure and not an anti-larval measure.

Mineral oils, Gambusia, and Paris green are anti-larval measures used in mosquito control.

questions.question: Which among the following insecticides is most widely used as a space spray?
questions.explanation: The insecticide most widely used as a space spray is pyrethrum.

questions.question:
Match the following methods of mosquito control to the appropriate examples.

Method of control
Example

l.Biological control
a.Larvicidal oil

ll.Genetic control

questions.answer: D. I – d, II – b, III – a, IV – c
questions.explanation:
The correctly matched methods of mosquito control are:

Method of control

questions.question: To curb an outbreak of plague in your locality, the municipal corporation decides to use rodenticides. Which of the following can be given as a single dose for this purpose?
questions.explanation:
Zinc phosphide is a single-dose rodenticide that causes death in a one-time exposure.

Acute or single-dose rodenticides are classified according to the precautions that need to be taken before their use:

• Those requiring ordinary care - Red squill, norbormide, zinc phosphide

• Those requiring maximal precaution - Sodium fluoroacetate, fluoroacetamide and strychnine

• Too dangerous for use - Arsenic trioxide, phosphorus, thallium sulphate

Multiple-dose or cumulative rodenticides cause death after multiple times of exposure. Examples include:

• Warfarin

• Coumafuryl

• Diphacinone

• Pindone

questions.question: Which of the following color labels is used to indicate the most hazardous pesticides?
questions.explanation:
The most hazardous pesticides must have labels in red color.

Pesticide toxicity labels:

Category of Pesticide
Color of Label

Extremely toxic
Bright red

Highly toxic
Bright yellow

Moderately toxic
Bright blue

Slightly toxic
Bright green

These labels are depicted in the image below.

questions.question: What proportion of healthcare waste is hazardous waste?
questions.explanation:
15% of health care waste is hazardous waste. It may be infectious, toxic, or radioactive in nature. The remaining 85% is general, non-hazardous waste.

Bio-medical waste means any waste that is generated during:

• Diagnosis, treatment, or immunization of human beings or animals

• Research activities pertaining thereto

• Production or testing of biologicals

Bio-medical waste is handled as per the Bio-medical Waste Management Rules, 2016. However, these rules do not apply to the following:

• Radioactive wastes

• Hazardous chemicals

• Solid wastes

• Lead-acid batteries

• Hazardous wastes

• e-Waste

• Hazardous microorganisms

questions.question: Which of the following category of wastes are treated by autoclaving and microwaving?
questions.explanation:
The final treatment of catheters, urine bags, and gloves is done by autoclaving and microwaving.

They belong to recyclable contaminated waste and are disposed of in a red bag.

Option A: Human anatomical waste is disposed of by incineration.

Option C: Cytotoxic and expired/discarded medicine is disposed of by incineration/plasma pyrolysis/disposal in a secured landfill.

Option D: Microbiological waste such as culture plates and slides are pre-treated with nonchlorinated chemicals and later disposed of by incineration.

questions.question: While working as a 1st-year resident in the labor ward, where would you dispose of the placenta following a delivery?
questions.explanation: Human anatomical wastes, like the placenta, are discarded in a yellow bag and disposed of by incineration/ plasma pyrolysis/ deep burial.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true about yellow waste disposal bags?

1. They are made from non-chlorinated plastic material

2. Chemical liquid wastes are collected in it

3. Metallic body implants are discarded in it

4. Polyvinyl chloride gloves are discarded in it and sent for incineration

5. Animal anatomical waste is collected in it and sent for chemical treatment
questions.explanation:
Yellow waste disposal bags are made from non-chlorinated plastic material and chemical liquid wastes are collected in them.

Chlorinated items, glass, metal, and rubber are not sent for incineration as incinerating them would produce carcinogenic gases.

The right disposal methods of the other options are:

• Animal anatomical waste - Collected in yellow bags and later sent for incineration.

• Metallic body implants - Collected in cardboard boxes with blue coloured marking and sent for recycling following autoclaving.

• PVC gloves - Collected in red bags and sent for autoclaving followed by shredding.

questions.question:
Which of the following should not be incinerated?

1. Sharps and waste with heavy metals

2. Reactive chemical waste

3. Specimens of microorganisms

4. Pressurized gas containers

5. Live or attenuated vaccines
questions.explanation:
Specimens of microorganisms and live or attenuated vaccines can be incinerated.

Wastes that should not be incinerated are:

• Sharps

• Pressurized gas containers

• Reactive chemical waste

• Waste with heavy metals like mercury and cadmium

• PVC

• Photographic or radiographic waste

questions.question: An orthopedic resident has removed a K-wire from the fractured olecranon of a 13-year-old boy. Where should he discard this?
questions.answer: B. Cardboard box with blue marking
questions.explanation:
Metallic body implants are disposed of in cardboard boxes with blue-colored markings.

The contents of the blue box are sent to Common Biomedical Waste Treatment and Disposal Facility (CBWTF). In the facility, these items are sterilized by autoclaving or microwaving and then sent for recycling.

questions.question: An HIV-positive man is brought to you following an accident. How would you discard his blood-soaked dressing material?
options: Pour 1% hypochlorite on the dressing material and send for incineration
Pour 5% hypochlorite on the dressing material and send for incineration
Put the dressing material directly in an appropriate bag and send for incineration
Pour 10% non chlorinated chemicals on the dressing material and send for incineration
questions.answer: C. Put the dressing material directly in an appropriate bag and send for incineration
questions.explanation:
The blood-soaked dressing material should be disposed of in a non-chlorinated yellow bag and sent for incineration. Pretreatment is not a requisite for incinerating soiled waste.

Items that require pretreatment with non-chlorinated chemicals before incineration:

• Used blood bags

• Other infectious plastic and liquid wastes

• Laboratory cultures, stocks, or specimens of microorganisms

• Live or attenuated vaccines

• Human and animal cell cultures used in research

• Dishes, and devices used for cultures

questions.question: Which of the following disposal methods is not as per biomedical waste management guidelines?
options: Disposal of a dead fetus of 21 weeks in a yellow bag by deep burial in rural areas
Pre-treatment of laboratory cultures with non-chlorinated disinfectant
Disposal of a glass ampoule with its cytotoxic drug through incineration
Disposal of radiological waste by deep burial
questions.answer: D. Disposal of radiological waste by deep burial
questions.explanation:
Radiological waste is not considered biomedical waste. Hence, deep burial is not done.

Disposal of radiological is covered under the provisions of the Atomic Energy Act. The radiological effluents are incinerated in a dedicated incinerator having off-gas cleaning facility. Another method is to convert the organic base into an aqueous form by treating it with sodium hydroxide.

Option A: Dead fetuses under the age of viability are considered human anatomical waste. Anatomical waste can be disposed of by deep burial in rural areas, where a common biomedical treatment facility and incineration is not available.

Option B: Laboratory cultures are classified under the category of microbiology, biotechnology, and other clinical laboratory waste. They are pretreated with a non-chlorinated disinfectant before they are sent for incineration.

Option C: The cytotoxic drugs are disposed of along with their packaging, through incineration.

questions.question: You are asked to catheterize an HBsAg-positive man before hernia surgery. According to the BMW management rules, where would you dispose of the plastic cover of the catheter?
questions.explanation:
The outer plastic cover of the Foleys catheter is discarded in a black bag.

Foleys catheters are packaged in plastic covers to keep them sterile. The plastic cover is not biomedical waste but is a part of general (municipal) waste. Hence, it is discarded in the black bag. The foleys catheter is disposed of in a red bag.

As per Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, the general waste must be disposed of in green bins (for recyclable waste) and blue bins (for non-recyclable waste) containing black plastic bags.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases should healthcare workers involved in handling biomedical waste be vaccinated against?
questions.explanation:
Healthcare workers involved in handling biomedical waste should be vaccinated against hepatitis B and tetanus.

These are most likely to be transmitted by the handling of biomedical waste. Yearly health check-ups should be done, and a booster dose should be given if needed.

questions.question: An on-site waste treatment and disposal facility should be built in a hospital if the nearest common biomedical treatment facility is:
questions.explanation:
According to biomedical waste management rules of 2016, healthcare establishments shall establish an on-site treatment and disposal facility only when a common biomedical treatment facility (CBMWTF) is more than 75 km away.

According to these rules, biomedical waste (BMW) from healthcare facilities is to be transported to a CMBWTF. The establishment of CBMWTF reduces the need for transport and cost of treatment/ kg of BMW.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a high-heat system for the treatment of biomedical waste?
questions.explanation:
Microwaving is a low-heat system for the treatment of biomedical waste.

The heating systems used for the treatment and disposal of biomedical waste are:

Low-heat system
High-heat system

Autoclaving: Uses steam. It is of two types-

1. Gravity flow autoclave

2. Vacuum autoclave

Microwaving: Uses moist heat and steam generated by microwave energy

Incineration: Waste is destroyed/denatured under high temperatures

Plasma pyrolysis: Waste is treated at high temperatures under controlled conditions to form gases that are subjected to combustion in the secondary chamber

Hydroclaving: The waste is subjected to indirect heating by applying steam to the outer jacket

Dry heat sterilization: Waste sharps are treated using dry heat at a temperature >185 C for 150 minutes

questions.question: Which of the following disposal methods uses high temperature and dry oxidation?
questions.explanation:
Incineration is a high-temperature dry oxidation process.

Waste that is incinerated need not undergo any type of pre-treatment. It helps to reduce weight as well as volume. The temperature in the incinerator is 800⁰C in the primary chamber and 1050⁰C in the secondary chamber.

Types of incinerators:

• Rotary kilns

• Single chamber pyrolytic

• Double chamber pyrolytic

The heating systems used for the treatment and disposal of biomedical waste are:

Low-heat system
High-heat system

Autoclaving: Uses steam. It is of two types-

1. Gravity flow autoclave

2. Vacuum autoclave

Microwaving: Uses moist heat and steam generated by microwave energy

Incineration: Waste is destroyed/denatured under high temperatures

Plasma pyrolysis: Waste is treated at high temperatures under controlled conditions to form gases that are subjected to combustion in the secondary chamber

Hydroclaving: The waste is subjected to indirect heating by applying steam to the outer jacket

Dry heat sterilization: Waste sharps are treated using dry heat at a temperature >185 C for 150 minutes

questions.question: In a treatment facility, which of the following cannot be used to verify the treatment of biomedical waste done by incineration?
questions.explanation:
Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis is not used to verify thermal methods of biomedical waste disposal. It is a biological larvicide, used in nonpotable water for killing mosquito larvae.

The following can be used to verify the adequacy of thermal methods of biomedical waste disposal:

• Bacillus atropheus

• Bacillus subtilis

• Geobacillus stearothermophilus

questions.question: At a waste treatment facility, pharmaceutical waste was mixed with cement, lime, and water before disposal. What is this method known as?
questions.explanation:
Inertization is the process of mixing biomedical waste with non-toxic substances to reduce the toxicity of the waste and to reduce the contamination of groundwater. It is most commonly done for incineration ash with high metal content.

The typical composition of the inertization mixture is:

• 65% pharmaceutical waste

• 15% cement

• 15% lime

• 5% water

questions.question: What is the correct combination of temperature and duration used in a hot air oven?
questions.explanation:
The correct combinations of temperature and duration of sterilisation in a hot air oven is:

• 180°C for 30 mins

• 170°C for 60 mins

• 160⁰C for 2 hours

It can be used to sterilize powders, glasswares, and oils.

An autoclave is another apparatus that is used for sterilization. It uses steam at a temperature of 121⁰C for 30 mins under 15 lbs of pressure.

questions.question: All the following are the characteristics of waste that can be incinerated except:
questions.explanation:
Only waste material containing <5% of noncombustible solids can be incinerated. Wastes that are incinerated go in the yellow bag.

Waste products with the following characteristics can be incinerated:

• Combustible matter >60%

• Non-combustible solid <5%

• Non-combustible fine <20%

• Low heating volume

• Moisture content <30%.

questions.question:
Correctly match the following logos.

1. Cytotoxic

2. Radiation

3. Biohazard
questions.explanation: The correctly matched logos are as shown below.

questions.question: You are working in a covid ward. After doffing, where will you dispose of the plastic coverall?
questions.explanation: The plastic coverall used by a healthcare worker during the COVID-19 pandemic should be disposed of in the red bin.

questions.question: An intern asks for your advice regarding the disposal of needles from the needle tip cutter after a vaccine drive. Which of the following bins will you advise her to discard them in?
questions.explanation: Waste sharps including metals (both used, discarded, and contaminated metal sharps) are to be discarded in the white bin.

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding a disaster?
options: Occurrence that causes damage to life and property
Occurrence that has the potential to cause disruption or damage to people
Occurrence that causes deterioration of health and health services
Occurrence that can cause substantial economic harm
questions.answer: B. Occurrence that has the potential to cause disruption or damage to people
questions.explanation:
A disaster is defined as any occurrence that causes damage, ecological disruption, loss of human life, or deterioration of health and health services. It usually requires an extraordinary response from outside the affected community or area.

A hazard is any phenomenon that has the potential to cause disruption or damage to people and their environment.

questions.question: Which type of natural disaster causes the most deaths?
questions.explanation:
Hydrological natural disasters cause the most deaths.

The Disaster Information Management System of Deslnventar classifies natural disasters into five major categories. They are:

• Geophysical - earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcano eruptions

• Hydrological - floods, debris flow, and landslides

• Meteorological - cyclones, tornadoes, extreme temperatures, sandstorms, blizzards etc.

• Climatological - drought, forest wildfire, glacial lake outburst etc.

• Biological - epidemics and insect infestations

questions.question: Which of the following steps of disaster management is in correct order?
questions.answer: C. Disaster impact – Response – Rehabilitation – Mitigation
questions.explanation:
The correct order is Disaster impact – Response – Rehabilitation – Mitigation.

Disaster management includes three aspects:

1. Disaster impact and response: It involves immediate management of mass casualties as follows:

• Search, rescue, and first-aid

• Field care

• Triage

• Tagging

• Identification of dead

2. Rehabilitation or recovery: It involves the restoration of the pre-disaster conditions by taking steps such as:

• Water supply

• Basic sanitation and personal hygiene

• Food safety

• Vector control

3. Mitigation: Measures designed either to prevent hazards from causing disaster or to reduce the effects of the disaster. This also includes preparedness for any impending disasters or in disaster-prone areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about disaster management?
options: Measures to prevent hazards are designed in mitigation phase
Rescue and evacuation occur in recovery phase
Measures on vector control are done in rehabilitation phase
Field care and tagging are done in disaster impact and response phase
questions.answer: B. Rescue and evacuation occur in recovery phase
questions.explanation:
Rescue and evacuation occur in the response phase, not in the recovery phase.

Disaster management includes three aspects:

1. Disaster impact and response: It involves immediate management of mass casualties as follows:

• Search, rescue, and first-aid

• Field care

• Triage

• Tagging

• Identification of dead

2. Rehabilitation or recovery: It involves the restoration of the pre-disaster conditions by taking steps such as:

• Water supply

• Basic sanitation and personal hygiene

• Food safety

• Vector control

3. Mitigation: Measures designed either to prevent hazards from causing disaster or to reduce the effects of the disaster. This also includes preparedness for any impending disasters or disaster-prone areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common disease after a disaster?
questions.explanation:
Gastroenteritis is the most commonly reported disease after a disaster.

It occurs due to contamination of water supply, damage to the sewerage system, overcrowding and poor sanitation. Therefore, supply of safe drinking water and proper disposal of excreta are the most practical and effective strategies of disease prevention in the post–disaster period.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is not commonly seen in the post-disaster period?
questions.explanation:
Leishmaniasis is not commonly seen in the post-disaster period.

Diseases that are commonly seen in the post-disaster phase are:

• Gastroenteritis (most common)

• Acute respiratory infections

• Leptospirosis

• Rickettsiosis

• Rabies

• Equine encephalitis

questions.question: A district in Andhra Pradesh reported severe drought. Which of the following vitamin deficiencies would you expect to see in this population?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency is the most common deficiency in areas of famines and droughts. It leads to xerophthalmia and blindness.

questions.question: Following a drought in Bihar, the government launched an immediate mass vaccination program. Which of the following vaccines is recommended in such cases?
questions.explanation:
Measles vaccination is recommended for infants and children, immediately following a disaster. This should be given along with vitamin A supplementation as measles can exacerbate vitamin A deficiency.

The vaccination of infants and children against measles is one of the most important public health response measures during a humanitarian crisis when less than 90% of the children or an unknown percentage have already been vaccinated against measles.

Measles and polio vaccines are recommended immediately after an emergency.

Option A: Cholera vaccine is not recommended.

Option B: Hepatitis A vaccine is recommended at the outset of an outbreak.

Option C: Tetanus vaccine is recommended in the early stages and post-emergency stage.

questions.question: Immediately following a disaster, mass vaccination of which of the following vaccines does the WHO recommend?
questions.explanation: The WHO does not recommend typhoid, cholera, and rabies vaccines for mass vaccination after a disaster. However, high-risk populations are recommended to take the cholera vaccine. The rabies vaccine is given only for post-exposure prophylaxis.

questions.question: You are a field doctor at the site of an earthquake. You assist in rapidly classifying the injured on the basis of the likelihood of their survival and need for intervention. What is this process called?
questions.explanation:
The process of rapidly classifying the injured in a disaster on the basis of severity of injury and likelihood of survival with prompt medical intervention is called triage. It is carried out at the site of disaster.

Tagging is the identification of patients in a disaster with tags stating their name, age, place of origin, triage category, diagnosis, and initial treatment.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about reverse triage?
options: Classifying the victims based on the severity of their injuries and their survival with treatment
Highest preference is given to severely injured patients
More injured victims are given the lowest preference
Color coding is done with red as the highest priority.
questions.answer: C. More injured victims are given the lowest preference
questions.explanation:
Reverse triage is a situation where the less injured are treated earlier than the ones that are injured more.

This is used in wars and military settings, where soldiers may need to return to the field of battle soon after treatment. It is also done when there is a scarcity of medical resources after a disaster.

The surge capacity of hospitals is increased to accommodate for the natural disaster, by discharging non-emergent existing patients. This enables hospitals to allow for an acute increase in incoming patients.

questions.question: What is the level of residual chlorine to be maintained in the water bodies after a disaster?
questions.explanation:
The advisable level of residual chlorine in water bodies after a disaster is 0.7-0.9 mg/L.

Chlorine is a disinfectant that is added to water bodies. In normal conditions, water should have free residual chlorine (FRC) of 0.2 - 0.5 mg/L. However, during a disaster, there is an increased risk of fecal contamination of water sources from the sewage systems. Therefore, it is necessary to increase FRC to 0.7 - 0.9 mg/L.

questions.question: Which of the following gas was responsible for the Bhopal Gas Tragedy?
questions.explanation: The gas responsible for the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, which occurred on 3rd December 1984 at the Union Carbide Pesticide Plant, was methyl isocyanate.

questions.question: Which of the following emission occurred in Chernobyl explosion accident of 1986?
questions.explanation: Chernobyl nuclear explosion occurred on 26th April, 1986, in the Soviet Union. It caused the release of Iodine-I131, Cesium-Cs134­, Cs137, and Strontium-Sr90, and other isotopes into the atmosphere.

questions.question: What is the nodal ministry for disaster management in India?
options: Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate change
questions.explanation:
The Ministry of Home Affairs is the nodal ministry for disaster management at the Centre except for dealing with droughts which are under the purview of the Ministry of Agriculture.

Other parts of the Indian government involved in disaster management are the Emergency Medical Relief Wing under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

The Indian Meteorological Department plays a role in mitigation of disaster and its preparedness.

questions.question: Which of the following is a nodal centre in case of disaster management?
questions.explanation:
The district disaster management authority is the nodal center for disaster management.

It is chaired by either, the District Collector, District Magistrate or the Deputy Commissioner. The Chief Medical Officer of the district is a part of this authority.

questions.question: The NIDM is involved in the mitigation and management of disasters in India. Who is the president of this institution?
questions.explanation:
The National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) is under the Ministry of Home Affairs of India. Its president is the Union Home Minister.

National Institute of Disaster Management is a premier institute for training and capacity development programs for managing natural disasters in India, on a national as well as regional basis.

questions.explanation:
National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) is an apex body of the Government of India, with a mandate to lay down policies for disaster management. It is chaired by the Prime Minister of India.

questions.explanation: Inhalation of dust particles in the size range of 0.5 to 3 microns is considered to be the most dangerous. It can lead to various occupational lung diseases called pneumoconioses.

questions.question: While working as an MO, you noticed an increased number of bagassosis patients in the area. Which of the following fungal control measures would you advise the sugarcane farmers to implement?
questions.explanation:
Fungal control on bagasse can be done by using 2% propionic acid and keeping the moisture content above 20%.

Bagassosis is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by inhaling bagasse dust contaminated by the fungus Thermoactinomyces sacchari. It is a reaction to the various antigens present in sugarcane molasses.

questions.question: A shipyard worker is diagnosed with asbestosis. Which of the following is false about his condition?
options: The symptoms usually occur after 5-10 years of exposure
Peribronchial fibrosis is a characteristic finding
The most dangerous form of asbestos is chrysolite type
questions.answer: D. The most dangerous form of asbestos is chrysolite type
questions.explanation:
Amphibole is the most dangerous form of asbestos. Chrysolite is a safer form of asbestos compared to amphibole.

Asbestosis is a pneumoconiosis that occurs after 5-10 years of exposure to asbestos. It progresses even after the removal of contact with asbestos. Asbestosis affects the basal part of the lung causing diffuse peribronchial fibrosis.

Sputum shows asbestos bodies, which are asbestos fibers coated with fibrin. The image given below shows asbestos bodies:

The complications that can occur are:

• Pulmonary fibrosis

• Carcinoma of the lung

• Mesothelioma of the pleura

• Malignancy of the gastrointestinal tract

questions.question: A patient presents with abdominal colic and constipation. On examination, pallor and blue stippled lines on gums are observed. What is the most common mode of exposure to this particular toxicity?
questions.explanation:
A patient presenting with constipation, pallor, and Burton's lines (blue stippled lines on gums), most likely has lead poisoning. The most common mode of exposure to lead toxicity is the inhalation of lead fumes.

Lead poisoning occurs by lead exposure via the following modes:

• Inhalation- lead fumes in gasoline and petroleum products

• Ingestion- lead paint

• Absorption through the skin– seen only with organic leads

The most toxic forms of lead are lead oxide, lead carbonate, and lead arsenate. The least toxic form is lead sulfide.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about lead poisoning?
options: Signs and symptoms occur when blood lead levels >70mcg/dL
Wrist drop is the earliest sign
questions.answer: A. Signs and symptoms occur when blood lead levels >70mcg/dL
questions.explanation:
The signs and symptoms of lead poisoning occur only when the blood lead levels exceed 70mcg/dL, which is known as the threshold phenomenon.

Lead poisoning is also known as plumbism/ Saturnism/ painter's colic.

questions.question: Barosinusitis is likely to be seen in which of the following patients?
options: A person who is suffering from mountain sickness
A patient Infected by gas-forming bacteria
A patient diagnosed with Aspergillus sinusitis
A diver who developed decompression sickness
questions.answer: D. A diver who developed decompression sickness
questions.explanation:
Barosinusitis occurs in decompression sickness or Caisson's disease. It is due to the sudden expansion of air in the sinuses.

It can be seen in:

• Divers who ascend rapidly from deep-sea (high pressure) to the surface of the earth (low pressure)

• Pilots of unpressurized aircraft or mountaineers who rapidly ascended from the surface of the earth (high-pressure zone) to a high altitude (low-pressure zone)

Under high pressure, gases get compressed, and their solubility increases. When a person is in deep-sea (high-pressure zone) for a long time, an increased amount of nitrogen gets dissolved in his body. When he suddenly comes back to the surface (atmospheric pressure or a low-pressure zone), the solubility of gases decreases and they escape from the dissolved state forming nitrogen bubbles.

These bubbles can cause sudden expansion of air in various parts of the body such as the middle ear (barotitis), sinuses (barosinusitis), beneath teeth (barodontalgia), intestinal loops (abdominal distension), and emphysema.

Nitrogen bubbles can also cause chokes (dyspnoea), bends (joint pain), and prickles (nerve irritation).

The definitive treatment for Caisson's disease is recompression.

questions.question: Workers working at which of the following industries require periodical examination on a daily basis?
questions.explanation:
Workers handling irritant chemicals like dichromates require periodical examination on a daily basis.

Most occupational exposures require an annual periodical examination. Certain exposures like lead, radon, and dyes require monthly periodical examination.

questions.question: Serial chest X-rays of an elderly man reveal progressive massive fibrosis. Which of the following pneumoconiosis is associated with this?
questions.explanation:
Progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is associated with anthracosis. PMF classically develops in anthracosis and silicosis.

Exposure to coal dust causes progressive lung injury called anthracosis. Initially, it manifests as simple coal worker pneumoconiosis, which occurs after exposure for 10–12 years and is reversible. Later, it can progress to progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) which is irreversible.

questions.question: Bronchoalveolar lavage from a patient with pneumoconiosis showed Micropolyspora faeni. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Farmer's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by thermophilic actinomycetes like Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula (formerly known as Micropolyspora faeni). It occurs due to inhalation of moldy hay and grains causing an immunological reaction.

Woodworker's lung is a hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by Alternaria species, and Bacillus subtilis in persons exposed to oak, cedar, pine, and mahogany dust.

Bird fancier's lung is caused by proteins derived from birds like pigeons and parakeets in persons exposed to their feathers and droppings.

Malt worker's lung is caused by Aspergillus species in persons exposed to barley.

questions.question: Which of the following does not belong to the 4 P's of occupational dermatitis?
questions.explanation:
Post-selection check-up does not belong to the 4 P's of occupational dermatitis.

The 4 P's help in the prevention of occupational dermatitis, which include:

• Pre-selection check-up

• Protection

• Personal hygiene

• Periodic inspection

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about occupational cancer?
options: Age of incidence is same as compared to general population for the same cancer
The localization of the tumor is variable within a particular industry
The most common occupational cancer is squamous cell carcinoma
Onset of cancer does not occur after the person has left the industry
questions.answer: C. The most common occupational cancer is squamous cell carcinoma
questions.explanation:
The most common occupational cancer is squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. It is associated with exposure to radiation, dyes, and coal tar.

In occupational cancers, the age of incidence of cancer is earlier than that in the general population, affected by the same cancer type. The onset of cancer can occur even after leaving the industry. The localization of the cancer is remarkably constant for a particular industry.

questions.question: Cystoscopy performed on a patient with painless hematuria showed a fungating mass in the bladder. Exposure to all of the following agents can cause this disease except:
questions.explanation:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of bladder carcinoma. Benzol does not cause bladder cancer, it causes leukemia.

Bladder carcinoma is associated with exposure to aniline dyes like benzidine, beta-naphthylamines, auramine, magenta, and drugs like cyclophosphamide.

questions.question: A young woman is being evaluated for infertility. She gives a history of being employed in the printing industry. Exposure to which of the following is likely to cause this situation?
questions.explanation:
A woman working in the printing industry is likely to suffer from infertility due to lead toxicity.

More industrial workers are exposed to lead than to any other toxic metal. Occupational exposure to lead is seen in several industries including the manufacturing of storage batteries, glass, shipbuilding, printing, potteries, and rubber industries.

The effects of lead poisoning include abdominal colic, blue-line on the gums (Burton's line), stippling of red cells, anemia, wrist & foot drop, headache, and convulsions. In young or pregnant women, prolonged lead exposure can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, premature birth, and low birth weight.

questions.question: What is the definition of ergonomics?
options: Fitting the job to the worker
Process of improving industrial safety standards
Prevention of health problems of factory workers
questions.answer: A. Fitting the job to the worker
questions.explanation:
Ergonomics is defined as fitting the job to the worker. The aim of ergonomics is to achieve the best mutual adjustment of man and his work, for the improvement of human efficacy and well-being.

Emporiatrics, also called travel medicine, deals with the prevention and management of health problems of international travelers.

Union Minister of Human Resources Development

questions.question: Which of the following establishments is covered by the Employees' State Insurance Act?
questions.answer: B. Private medical and educational institutions
questions.explanation:
Currently, private medical and educational institutes employing >20 people are covered under the ESI Act.

The ESI Act is applicable to all industries except:

• Defence

• Railway

• Mines

questions.question: What percentage of the total wage bill is contributed by the employer under the ESI Act?
questions.explanation:
The employer contributes 3.25% of the total wage bill under the ESI Act.

The government has revised the rates of ESI contribution by employers (from 4.75% to 3.25%) and employees (from 1.75% to 0.75%) in 2019.

The distribution of the financial contribution is given below:

• Employee: 0.75% of the total wage bill

• Employer: 3.25% of the total wage bill

• Medical benefit: 1/8th by the state government and 7/8th by the central government

questions.question: Under the ESI Act, which of the following is not given as a cash benefit?
questions.explanation: Under the ESI Act, medical benefit is not given as a cash benefit. It is provided in the form of consultations, investigations and treatment by means of the ESI hospitals or ESI dispensaries.

questions.question: What is enhanced sickness benefit?
options: Benefit given at 70% of the wage for 91 days
Benefit given at 80% of the wage for 120 days
Benefit given for a duration of 2 years for 34 specified diseases
Benefit given at full wages for undergoing sterilization procedure
questions.answer: D. Benefit given at full wages for undergoing sterilization procedure
questions.explanation:
Enhanced sickness benefit under the ESI Act is the benefit given at full wages for undergoing sterilization procedures.

Under the ESI Act, sickness benefit is given at 70% of the daily wage for a duration of 91 days in one year. There are two special types of sickness benefits given:

• Enhanced sickness benefit: Benefit given at full wages for sterilization procedures; for a duration of 7 days post-vasectomy and 14 days post-tubectomy.

• Extended sickness benefit: Benefit given for a duration of 2 years for 34 specified diseases.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit given under the ESI Act?
questions.explanation:
Welfare benefit is not given under the ESI act.

The following benefits are given under the ESI act:

• Medical benefit

• Sickness benefit

• Maternity benefit

• Dependance benefit

• Disablement benefit

• Funeral benefit

• Rehabilitation benefit

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about ESI Act?
options: State government covers 1/8th and ESI corporation covers 7/8th of the cost of medical care
Maternity benefit is payable at full wages for upto 24 weeks
It covers all employees getting income up to Rs.18,000/- per month
questions.answer: B. State government covers 1/8th and ESI corporation covers 7/8th of the cost of medical care
questions.explanation:
The state government's share of expenditure on medical care is 1/8th, and the ESI corporation's share of expenditure on medical care is 7/8th of the total cost.

Few important points about the ESI Act:

• It covers all employees getting income up to Rs.21,000/- per month.

• The employer contributes 3.25% of the total wage bill.

• An employee contributes 0.75% of wages.

• State and Central government share medical expenditure in the ratio 1:7.

• Medical benefit: Full medical care

• Sickness benefit: 70% of the average daily wages and is payable for 91 days.

• Extended sickness benefit: Payable for 2 years for a set of 34 diseases.

• Enhanced sickness benefit: Full average daily wage for a duration up to 7 days in case of vasectomy and up to 14 days in case of tubectomy.

• Maternity benefit: Full average daily wage for a duration up to 26 weeks (confinement) or 6 weeks (miscarriage/MTP) or 4 weeks (sickness arising out of pregnancy).

• Funeral expenses: Cash not exceeding Rs.15,000.

questions.question: Who is the beneficiary under the Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana scheme of ESI?
options: An insured person rendered unemployed, involuntarily
An insured employee who is pregnant
questions.answer: B. An insured person rendered unemployed, involuntarily
questions.explanation:
Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (RGSKY) is a scheme of ESI that benefits an insured person rendered unemployed, involuntarily.

Unemployment allowance under RGSKY is given when an insured person is going out of employment involuntarily, on account of:

• Closure of a factory or establishment

• Retrenchment (laying off employees due to economic difficulty)

• Permanent disability due to nonemployment injury

Allowance and eligibility criteria of Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana (updated in 2019):

• The allowance is given at the rate of 50% of the daily wage for a maximum of 2 years.

• To qualify for the scheme the worker must have worked in that setup for more than 3 years.

Note: Disability due to employment injury is covered under disablement benefits of ESI Act, 1948.

• Temporary disability: 90% of wages until disablement lasts.

• Permanent disability: 90% of wages as a life pension on the basis of loss of earning capacity.

• Dependants benefit: 90% of wage as monthly payment to the dependants of the deceased person, in cases where death occurs due to employment injury or occupational hazards.

questions.question: What is the correct order for the process of communication?
questions.explanation:
The correct order for the process of communication is:

Sender→Message→Channel→Receiver→Feedback

The sender (communicator) is the originator of the message. A message is the information which the communicator transmits to his audience. Channel is the media of communication between the sender and the receiver (e.g., interpersonal communication, mass media, traditional or folk media). The audience who receives, understands, and acts upon the message is called the receiver. Feedback is the reaction to the message which flows from the receiver to the sender.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an approach to health education?
questions.explanation:
Socio-environmental approach is not an approach to health education.

There are four approaches to health education:

Regulatory approach- external control or laws placed on people by the government. Ex: Child Marriage Act, No smoking in public places, Helmet law

Service approach- government aims at providing health services to the people at their doorsteps. Its drawback is that people will not accept a service, even if it is offered free of cost unless it is based on their felt needs. Ex: Government provided latrines free of cost yet people did not use them because its need was not felt

Health education approach- creates awareness of health needs and problems. Awareness leads to motivation which includes the stages of interest, evaluation, and decision-making. It is followed by acceptance of the new idea which becomes part of his existing values, known as internalization. Ex: Adoption of ORS for diarrhea

Primary health care approach- delivery of health services with the active involvement of people. Principles of community participation and intersectoral coordination are stressed here. Its objective is to help individuals become self-reliant in health matters. Ex: People receive guidance from healthcare providers (Rogi Kalyana Samiti, Mahila Arogya Samiti).

questions.question: In which model of health education does internalization occur?
questions.explanation:
Internalization belongs to the motivation model.

There are three models of health education:

• Medical model: transfer of proven medical information into education. It does not bridge the gap between knowledge and behavior.

• Motivation model: creates awareness of health needs and problems. Awareness leads to motivation which includes stages of interest, evaluation, and decision-making. It is followed by acceptance of the new idea which becomes part of his existing values, known as internalization.

• Social intervention model: focuses on changing the social environment which subsequently shapes the behavior of individual and the community.

questions.question: A group discussion was conducted among villagers to assess their knowledge on personal hygiene. Which of the following statements is false regarding this format of health education?
options: Many different topics can be spoken about in one discussion
A group leader guides the conversation
It can bring about change in the attitude of participants
It usually consists of 6 to 12 people
questions.answer: A. Many different topics can be spoken about in one discussion
questions.explanation:
A group discussion discusses one topic on its agenda.

Group discussion is an aggregation of people interacting in a face-to-face manner. Exchange of ideas, knowledge, and opinions is done by participants which influence a change in their attitudes.

It usually involves 6–12 people with a group leader who guides the conversation, giving equal opportunity to everyone to voice themselves. In a group discussion, everyone must speak and be open to criticism without interrupting others.

A limitation to this form of health education is that not everyone is open to speaking in public. There is also a high possibility of diversion of the topic of discussion when many people are involved.

questions.question:
Match the following:

A. Series of lectures on a subject by experts after which the audience is allowed to ask questions

Role play is the dramatization of social situations for health education by those taking part in it.

questions.explanation:
Delphi method is a systematic interactive forecasting method, which is used to obtain a consensus forecast among a large number of people. It determines the degree of agreement on a topic.

This can help in setting priorities or selecting alternatives in planning. This method uses questionnaires, which are answered by experts in two or more rounds.

questions.question: What is total communication used for?
questions.explanation:
The philosophy of total communication is used in the education of hearing-impaired children.

It requires the incorporation of aural, oral, and manual modes of communication for effective communication with and among hearing-impaired people.

questions.question: In which of the given scenarios would you use the GATHER approach?
questions.explanation:
The GATHER approach is mainly used for counseling, like in contraceptive counseling, wherein a person is helped to make a decision about health.

GATHER stands for:

• G – Greet

• A – Ask

• T – Tell options or give answers

• H – Help in making choices

• E – Explain everything about the decision

• R – Return for follow-up

questions.question: Which of the following is the ultimate long-term desired state towards which all the resources are directed?
questions.explanation:
The goal is the ultimate desired state towards which objectives and resources are directed. It is long-term and not constrained by time or resources.

The plan is the blueprint for taking action in order to achieve the goal.

Option A: Target refers to the quantifiable and achievable mid-term endpoints in the plan.

Option B: Mission describes the cause of the existence of the programme.

Option D: The objectives are short-term endpoints. They are precise points in the plan. They are either achieved or unachieved.

questions.question: Which of the following is a set of rules that helps ensure maximum use of the resources and efforts?
questions.explanation:
Procedure is a set of rules for carrying out work. It helps to ensure the maximum use of resources and efforts.

Option B: Programme is a sequence of activities designed to implement policies and accomplish objectives.

Option C: Schedule is a time sequence for the work to be done.

Option D: Target refers to the quantifiable and achievable mid-term endpoints in the plan.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of the evaluation of health programs?
questions.explanation:
Repeatability is not a component of the evaluation of health programs.

Components of evaluation are:

• Relevance

• Adequacy

• Accessibility

7. Re-evaluate

questions.question: Which of the following is a quantitative method of management?
questions.explanation:
Cost-benefit analysis is a quantitative method of management.

In this method, the economic benefits of any programme are compared with the costs incurred. The benefit of the programme is expressed in monetary units. The main drawback here is that the benefits of a health programme cannot always be expressed in monetary terms.

Management methods used in health programmes are either quantitative or based on behavioral sciences.

Methods based on behavioral sciences include:

• Organizational design

• Personnel management

• Communication

• Information systems

• Cost-benefit analysis

• Cost-effective analysis

• Cost–accounting

• Input-output analysis

• Model

• Systems analysis

• Planning–programming–budgeting system (PPBS)

• Work sampling

• Decision making

questions.question: What is the programme evaluation and review technique used for?
questions.explanation:
The programme evaluation and review technique (PERT) is used for network analysis.

It is a type of quantitative management technique which helps in detailed planning and comprehensive supervision.

It proceeds from resource to target
It is not a priority-based budgeting
questions.answer: A. It does not rely on data from previous budget

questions.question: A hospital administrator is systematically recording the activities of his team at regular intervals. What is this known as?
questions.explanation:
Work sampling is a systematic observation and recording of activities of one or more individuals carried out at regular or random intervals.

It is a type of quantitative method of management. It helps in standardizing the methods of performing the jobs and determining the need for manpower.

questions.question: Which committee had recommended a bachelor degree in medical education for rural health services?
options: High-level expert group on universal health coverage
Committee on Integration of Health Services
questions.answer: B. High-level expert group on universal health coverage
questions.explanation:
The high-level expert group (HLEG) on universal health coverage under the aegis of the Planning Commission of India suggested a 3.5 year bachelor degree course in medical education for rural health services.

This was planned for the 12th five-year plan (2012-2017). The degree given was B.Sc Community Health, and these rural health care practitioners were to be called community health officers.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the chairman of the Health Survey and Development Committee in 1943?
questions.explanation: Sir Joseph William Bhore was appointed as the chairman of the Health Survey and Development Committee in 1943. This committee was hence named the Bhore committee.

questions.question: Which health planning committee proposed the 3 million plan?
questions.explanation:
The 3 million plan was proposed by the Bhore Committee.

It proposed to set up the following in the long-term:

• Primary health units with 75-bedded hospitals for each 10,000 to 20,000 population

• Secondary units with 650 beds

• District hospitals with 2,500 beds

 As a short-term measure, it was proposed that each PHC must cater to 40,000 people and have:

• 2 medical officers, 4 public health nurses, 1 nurse

• 4 midwives, 4 dais, 2 sanitary inspectors, 2 health assistants

• 1 pharmacist

• 15 other class IV employees

questions.question: What is the provision of preventive, curative, and promotional health services to every individual called?
questions.explanation: Comprehensive health care as stated by the Bhore committee means giving integrated preventive, curative, and promotional health care to every individual, irrespective of their ability to pay.

questions.question: In the inventory management of drug stores, which of the following is a component of the VED method?
questions.explanation:
The 'D' in the VED method stands for desirable.

VED is a method of inventory management used mainly in drug stores and pharmacies.

The drugs are classified in three categories as follows:

• V - Vital drugs. Items whose absence cannot be tolerated (10% of total items).

• E - Essential drugs. Items whose absence can be tolerated for some time (40% of total items).

• D - Desirable drugs. Items whose absence can be tolerated for a long time (50% of total items).

questions.question: Which of the following is not true regarding the National Health Policy of 2017?
options: Increase public health expenditure to 5% of GDP by 2025
Access to safe water and sanitation to all by 2020
Achieve elimination of lymphatic filariasis by 2017
questions.answer: A. Increase public health expenditure to 5% of GDP by 2025
questions.explanation:
National Health Policy (NHP) 2017 aims to increase the public health expenditure from existing 1.15% to 2.5% of the GDP by 2025.

The draft of the policy from 2015 was passed by the government in 2017 and is called the National Health Policy (NHP) 2017.

Components of NHP 2017
Quantitative goals and objectives

Health status and programme impact

• ↑ life expectancy at birth from 67.5 to 70 by 2025

• ↓ infant mortality rate to 28 by 2019

• ↓ neonatal mortality to 16 and stillbirth rate to a single digit by 2025

• ↓ maternal mortality ratio from current levels to 100 by 2020

• Elimination of lymphatic filariasis by 2017

Health systems performance

• ↑ utilization of public health facilities by 50% by 2025

• ↑ Antenatal care coverage above 90%

• > 90% of newborns to be fully immunized by 1 year of age by 2025

• Access to safe water and sanitation to all by 2020 (Swachh Bharat Mission)

Health systems financing

• ↑ public health expenditure to 2.5% of GDP by 2025

• ↑ state sector health spending to > 8% of budget by 2020

Priority actions to improve the environment for health

• Swachh Bharat Abhiyan

• Balanced healthy diets and regular exercise

• Addressing tobacco, alcohol, and substance abuse

• Yatri Suraksha to reduce death due to accidents

• Nirbhaya Nari for action against gender violence

• Reduced stress and improved safety in workplaces

• Reducing indoor and outdoor air pollution

Other provisions

• NEET exam for UG

• ↑ provisions for treatment and diagnosis in HIV-centered communities

• Establishment of nursing schools in every district

• Food safety

questions.question: Which of the following is not included in the secondary level of the healthcare system?
questions.explanation: Medical colleges are included in the tertiary level of the health care system, which is also the second referral centre.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an element of primary healthcare?
questions.explanation:
Providing physical rehabilitation is not an element of primary health care. Primary health centers (PHCs) are only responsible for the popularization and mainstreaming of PMR in the community.

Primary health care refers to essential health care made universally available to individuals and acceptable to them, through their full participation and at a cost the community and country can afford.

questions.question: All of the following are pillars of primary health care except:
questions.explanation: Health education is an element of primary health care, not a pillar.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is false regarding ASHA workers?
options: Few of their responsibilities are integrated with Anganwadi workers
They should have formal education at least up to class 10
A population of 1000 should have at least 1 ASHA
They have to procure ORS, OCPs, IFA tablets from CHC
questions.answer: D. They have to procure ORS, OCPs, IFA tablets from CHC
questions.explanation:
Accredited social health activist (ASHA) workers do not need to procure supplies from CHCs. They only act as depot holders for certain essential supplies so that they are readily available to their community.

These essential supplies may include ORS, contraceptives, iron-folic acid tablets, chloroquine, disposable delivery kits, oral contraceptive pills, condoms, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding Anganwadi workers?
options: One AWW serves a population of 5000
They are appointed under the ICDS scheme
They link the community with the health services
Their responsibilities include counsel for immunization, health education, and nutrition
questions.answer: A. One AWW serves a population of 5000
questions.explanation:
The norm is one Anganwadi worker (AWW) per 400-800 population.

Anganwadi workers (AWW) are allotted under the integrated child development services (ICDS). AWW are selected from the community they are to serve and act as links between the community and health services. They are mostly part-time workers.

Responsibilities of an AWW include:

• Health checkups and growth chart maintenance

• Counsel women on birth preparedness, importance of safe delivery, immunization and contraception and prevention of common infections including STD and RTIs.

• Nutrition

• Health education

• Non-formal school education

• Referral services

questions.question: One male health assistant is posted for a population of:
questions.explanation: One male and female health assistant are required for a population of 30,000 in plain areas and of 20,000 in hilly or remote areas.

questions.question: How many people does a Mahila Arogya Samiti member cater to?
questions.explanation: 1 Mahila Arogya Samiti member is appointed for a population of 250-500 (covering about 50-100 households).

1. Chlorination of water bodies

2. Maintenance of eligible couple registers

3. Distribution of conventional contraceptives

4. Universal Immunization Program

5. Reproductive and child health services
questions.explanation:
The duties of a male health worker include chlorination of water bodies, distribution of conventional contraceptives, and reproductive and child health services.

Maintanence of eligible couple registers (part of family planning activities) and immunization are duties of female health workers.

Health workers (male and female) are 1 per 5000 in plains and 1 per 3000 in remote or hilly areas.

questions.explanation:
Malaria surveillance activities, in accordance with the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, are the duty of a male health worker.

• Anganwadi workers - 1 per 400-800 in plains and 1 per 300-800 in hilly or remote areas.

questions.explanation:
