questions.question: Which of the following is the principal unit of administration in India?
questions.explanation:
The principal unit of administration in India is the district under a collector.

Under districts are the sub-divisions, tahsils or talukas, municipalities or corporations, villages, panchayats, etc. As of 2021, there are 748 districts in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation:
The Panchayat Samiti or Janpada Panchayat operates at the block level.

Panchayati Raj is a three-tier structure of rural self-government in India. It operates at the following levels:

• Panchayat at the village level (includes Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, and Nyaya Panchayat)

• Panchayat Samiti or Janpada Panchayat at the block level

• Zilla Parishad at the district level

questions.question: Community or village health guides are selected by:
questions.explanation:
Village health guides (VHGs) are selected by the medical officer-in-charge (MO).

2-3 candidates are put forward by the community for the position of a VHG. The MO selects one of them after consultation with the block development officer and field staff.

questions.question: As a PHC medical officer, you would keep all of the following in mind while selecting a village health guide except:
options: They must be above 45 years of age
They must be a resident of the community that they will serve
They must be educated up to 6th grade
They should be able to spare 2-3 hours in a day for community work
questions.answer: A. They must be above 45 years of age
questions.explanation:
Village health guides (VHG) are chosen by the medical officer-in-charge (including PHC MO). Age is not a criterion for selection.

The VHG scheme was introduced in 1977. Guidelines for choosing a VHG include:

• They can be of either sex but must be residents of the village

• They must know to read and write and have education up to 6th grade

• They must be able to spare around 2-3 hours a day for community work

• They must be acceptable to all parts of the community

VHGs are trained for 2-3 months before beginning work. The norm is to have 1 VHG per 1000 population.

questions.question: Which of the following public health centers do First Referral Units (FRUs) and non-FRUs belong to?
questions.explanation:
First Referral Units (FRUs) and non-FRUs belong to the Community Health Centers (CHCs).

The Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) guidelines are a code of standards for uniformity in health facilities in the Indian public health system, under the National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), India. It aims to provide guidance on the infrastructure, human resources, drugs, diagnostics, equipment, quality, and governance requirements for delivering health services at all levels of facilities in the system.

The 2022 edition of IPHS mainly concentrates on comprehensive primary health care, increasing the human workforce, decentralized access to healthcare, and better implementation of universal health coverage.

questions.question: A district has a population of 20 lakhs. According to the IPHS 2022 guidelines, approximately how many beds should the district public health system have for this population?
questions.explanation:
In a district having a population of 20 lakhs, the number of beds the district public health system should have is given as follows: 2000 essential and 4000 desirable.

According to IPHS 2022 norms for the number of beds in district hospitals, 1 bed per 1000 population is essential and 2 beds per thousand population would be desirable.

Therefore, in a population of 20,00,000 the district public health system should have 2000 essential and 4000 desirable beds.

The essential number of beds should be achieved through the public health system of tertiary care (medical colleges), secondary care (DH, SDH, CHCs), and primary care in the district (PHCs and CHCs).

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about district and sub-district hospitals?
options: All districts need at least two district hospitals.
The minimum essential number of beds in a sub-district hospital is 100.
All districts do not need a sub-district hospital.
DNB training can be done in district hospitals.
questions.answer: A. All districts need at least two district hospitals.
questions.explanation:
Every district should have at least one comprehensively functioning district hospital (DH).

District hospitals and subdistrict hospitals provide secondary care health services. Every district should have at least one comprehensively functioning DH. Districts with a population of less than 5 lakhs and with a functional DH do not need a subdistrict hospital (SDH). Districts with a population of 5–10 lakhs can have one SDH. For a population of more than 10 lakhs, 1 SDH is needed for every 10 lakh population.

The three pillars of district hospital services are providing clinical care, providing a knowledge hub for capacity development, and public health programs.

Important functions of DHs:

• Providing curative services

• Palliative and rehabilitative services

• Implementation of health programs

• Drugs and diagnostic services

• Administrative and other support services

• Health promotion and prevention, education

• Providing educational services, like Diplomate of National Board (DNB) training; training courses for healthcare professionals (HCPs) in auxiliary nursing and midwifery (ANM), telemedicine, and technology; and partnerships with universities

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding Community Health Centers (CHCs)?
options: Non-FRU CHCs should have 50 essential beds.
Non-FRU CHCs can be located in urban areas.
FRU-CHCs can be located in rural areas.
Elective surgeries will not be performed at FRU-CHCs.
questions.answer: C. FRU-CHCs can be located in rural areas.
questions.explanation:
First Referral Unit - Community Health centers (FRU-CHCs) can be located in rural areas.

Community health centers (CHC) can be classified into the following types:

• Non-FRU-CHCs - They are located in rural areas. They provide preventive, promotive, palliative, and rehabilitative services. They also have curative services for normal delivery, stabilization of common emergencies, etc.

• FRU-CHCs are the first centers of referral from smaller centers such as sub-centers or primary health centers. They can be located in rural as well as urban areas. Apart from providing the abovementioned essential services, they also provide specialized services and elective surgeries. All the CHCs located in urban areas are FRU-CHCs.

In addition to the above centers, CHCs called Block Health Public Units (BHPU) may be located in the block headquarters. Apart from clinical and public health services, they have a health management information system (HMIS). They also help in decentralizing health services.

questions.question: You are posted as a medical officer in a rural Health and Wellness Center - Primary Health Center (HWC-PHC). According to the IPHS 2022 guidelines, which of the following is incorrect regarding the essential manpower required for this PHC?

According to the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) 2022 guidelines, a total of 12 staff is considered essential manpower for a PHC. They include 1 Medical Officer (MBBS), 2 staff nurses, 1 pharmacist, 1 health worker female/ANM, 1 health worker/health assistant (male), 1 health assistant (female)/lady health visitor, 1 laboratory technician, 1 data entry operator, 1 dresser, 1 accountant, and 1 sanitation staff.

chapters.chapter: Descriptive Statistics I Probability And Data

questions.question: You are conducting a study to determine the mean height of children visiting the local PHC. Which type of statistical study is being done here?
questions.explanation:
A study to determine the mean height of children is an example of a descriptive statistical study.

Descriptive statistics are the statistical methods that merely organize, describe or summarize the actual data available. For example, a study determining the mean blood pressure of patients visiting a PHC on a single day.

Analytical statistics are the second major category of epidemiological studies, after descriptive statistics. The objective of an analytical study is to test the hypothesis.

An observational study is an empiric investigation in which the objective is to establish a relationship between cause and effect. It falls under the category of analytical statistics.

It is performed when controlled experimentation cannot be feasibly used to determine a hypothesis. For example, in the case of cigarette smoking causing lung cancer, it would be unethical and not feasible to conduct a controlled experiment. So, an observational study is preferred.

Inferential statistics involve inductive reasoning i.e., generalizing observations to a population after having observed only a sample. An example of such a study would be a study determining the expected success rate of vasectomy

Theoretical statistics is a mathematical approach to describe something, predict events, or analyze the relationship between things. Some of the concepts of theoretical statistics are mean, median, mode, standard deviation and correlation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about statistical terms is incorrect?
options: Population is the universe about which an investigator wishes to draw conclusions
A sample is a representative subset of the population that is being studied
An element is a group of observations in the population
A population need not be only people but can be measurements too
questions.answer: C. An element is a group of observations in the population
questions.explanation:
An element is a single observation in a study. For example, in a study of blood pressure values, the blood pressure value of one person is an element.

In a statistical study, the population refers to the group about which information is to be gathered. The composition of the population in terms of its age, sex, occupation, cultural characters, etc need to be defined before a study is conducted. The population need not consist of just people but can also be made of measurements. For example, in a study of blood glucose measurements in Indians, the population consists of the blood glucose measurements.

The part/subset of the population, which is being studied is known as a sample. For example, in a questionnaire-based study on cervical cancer in a population, the sample would include females attending the out-patient departments of a hospital. This is a subset of the entire population.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about probability is true? (Probability of event occurring is p)

1. p=1 means absolute certainty of event occurring

2. p can be positive or negative

3. The addition rule can be used to calculate probability

4. The probability of the event not occurring (q ) = p + 1

5. The multiplication rule can be used to calculate probability
questions.explanation:
If the probability of an event occurring is 1, it means there is an absolute certainty that the event will occur.

The addition rule and multiplication rule can be used to calculate the probability of an event. The addition rule is used to calculate the combined probability of the occurrence of two or more mutually exclusive events. The multiplication rule is used to calculate the combined probability of two or more statistically independent events occurring together.

Probability values range from 0 (no probability) to 1 (absolute certainty). So negative value of p is not possible.

Since p is the probability of an event occurring and q is the probability of the event not occurring,

q = 1 - p

questions.question: In which of the following processes is binomial distribution widely used?
questions.explanation:
Binomial distribution is widely used in genetic counseling.

Binomial distribution helps determine the probability of occurance of a specific combination of mutually exclusive independent events. In a binomial distribution, there are only two possible events like Yes/No or Male/Female or Alive/Dead. The results of the distribution gives the probabilities of obtaining an exact number of successes in a series of independent trials.

For example, the inheritence of cystic fibrosis follows a binomial distribution. There are:

a. Two possible events - inheriting the disease/ not inheriting it

b. Events are mutually exclusive - one person cannot both have the disease and not have it

c. Independent possibilities - if one child has inherited it, this will not affect if the other child will inherit it.

The physician using this technique can explain to the patients the probabilities of their children suffering from the disease.

questions.question: If the events A and B are mutually exclusive events, what is the probability of either A or B occurring?
questions.explanation:
If the events A and B are mutually exclusive, then the probability of either A or B occuring is given by,

p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B)

This is as per the addition rule of probability.

The probability of both the mutually exclusive events happening at the same time is given by,

p (A and B) = p (A) x p (B)

The probability of any of two mutually non-exclusive events occuring at a point of time is given by,

p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B) - p (A and B)

If p(A) and p(B) are the only two outcomes possible in a given event then,

p (A) + p (B) = 1

For example, probability of patient suffering from lung cancer dying within 5 years and probability of patient suffering from lung cancer surviving these 5 years adds upto 1.

questions.question: You are conducting a study on birth weight. As per your data, the probability of a baby having birth weight <2500 grams is 0.50 and of having birth weight of 2500-2999 grams is 0.20. What is the probability that a baby will have a birth weight of < 3kg?
questions.explanation:
The probability that a baby will have a birth weight of < 3kg is 0.70.

In this scenario, the probability of having a baby with BW < 2500 grams, p (A) = 0.50 and that of having a baby with BW between 2500 – 2999 grams, p (B) = 0.20.

Since both events are mutually exclusive, i.e., they cannot happen together, it satisfies the condition for the addition rule of probability.

Thus, the probability of having a baby that weighs less than 3 kilos is,

p (A or B) = p (A) + p (B) = 0.50 + 0.20 = 0.70.

If p(A) and p(B) were non-mutually exclusive events, then the probability would have been calculated by

p(A or B) = p(A) + p(B) - p(A and B).

questions.question: You select 3 people from a population where the prevalence of anemia is 20% .What is the probability that all the three randomly selected people from the population would have anemia?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, the probability of all 3 randomly selected individuals having anemia is 0.008.

In this scenario, the prevalence of anemia is 20%.

So, the probability of a person having anemia in the given population (p) = 20/100 = 0.2.

If selecting 3 people from the population randomly, the chance of the first person having anemia is independent of the second or third person also having it and vice versa. This satisfies the condition for the multiplication rule of probability which states that the probability of two or more statistically independent events all occurring together is equal to the product of their individual probabilities.

Thus, here the probability that all the 3 randomly selected people from the population would have anemia = 0.2 x 0.2 x 0.2 = 0.008.

questions.question: There are 50 patients admitted in a ward of your medical college. Here 20 are girls and 30 are boys. Out of this, 10 girls and 20 boys require surgery. What is the probability that a randomly selected boy and girl both require surgery?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, the probability that a randomly selected boy and girl both require surgery is 1/3.

First, we have to calculate the probability of picking the boys requiring surgery and the girls requiring surgery separately. These are mutually exclusive events.

In this scenario, the probability of correctly picking a girl requiring surgery is p(A)=10/20= 1/2

The probability of correctly picking a boy requiring surgery is p(B)=20/30= 2/3

Next, we apply the multiplication rule of probability.

The probability of picking boys and girls that require surgery,

p(A and B)= p(A) x p(B)= ½ x ⅔ = 2/6= 1/3.

questions.question: The chance of passing a genetic disease X by affected parents to their first child is 0.16. If they plan to have two children, what is the probability that both the children will have the disease?
questions.explanation:
The probability of both children having the disease is 0.0256.

In this scenario, the chance of each child having the disease is 0.16. The second child having the disease is independent of the first child having it. So, the events are statistically independent.

Applying the multiplication rule of probability, the probability of both children having the disease is,

0.16 x 0.16 = 0.0256.
These are non-mutually exclusive events as the first child having the trait does not rule out the chance of the second child having it.

On the other hand, the probability of one of the two children having the disease is given by,

p(A or B)= p(A) + p(B) - p(A and B)= 0.16 + 0.16 -(0.16 x 0.16)= 0.32- 0.0256= 0.2944

questions.question: Which of the following is not a measurement scale for data?
questions.explanation:
A proportion is not a measurement scale for data. It is a ratio, where the numerator is always a part of the denominator. It indicates a value as a part of the whole. It is usually expressed as a percentage.

The four scales of measurement used for data can be remembered with the mnemonic NOIR. This stands for nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio data scales.

questions.question: Which of the following scales of data measurement do blood groups belong?
questions.explanation: Bloods groups are nominal scale data or categorical data. This is because they are just labels and have no numerical value or meaningful order.

questions.question:
Which of the following are examples of nominal scale data?

1. Genders

2. Types of hospitals

3. Height

4. Kuppuswamy scale

5. Types of anemia
questions.explanation:
Genders, types of anemia and types of hospitals come under nominal scale data.

There is no meaningful order or quantifiable variable in this kind of data. It is arranged on the basis of labels, titles or categories.

Kuppuswamy scale is an ordinal scale data. It is a scale representing socio-economic data.

Height is a ratio scale data as it can be arranged in a meaningful order with a well-defined size interval.

questions.question: A physician classifies a group of patients based on disease severity as normal, mild, moderate and severe. Which of the following scales of data does this classification system belong to?
questions.explanation: The classification of this disease as normal, mild, moderate and severe belongs to the ordinal scale. This is because this arrangement is not only qualitative but also has a meaningful order with no interval in between.

questions.question:
Which of the following are representative of ordinal scale data?

1. Hemoglobin level

2. TNM staging

3. Likert scale

4. HIV positive or negative

5. Severity of pain
questions.explanation:
TNM staging, Likert scale and severity of pain are measured on the ordinal scale.

In such cases, the arrangement is qualitative, with a meaningful order but there is no way of quantifying the difference between the individual variables. For example, grading of pain as mild, moderate, and severe.

The Likert scale is used in collecting self-reported data in questionnaire-based research. It is a psychometric scale used to understand people’s attitudes from responses. Usually, a 5-point scale of agreement is used which includes:

• 1 – Strongly disagree

• 2 – Disagree

• 3 – Neither agree nor disagree

• 4 – Agree

• 5 – Strongly agree

TNM staging is done for the staging of cancer. It is based on tumor size, lymph node status and metastasis. Lower stages indicate better prognosis than higher stages.

Hemoglobin level is an example of ratio scale data.

HIV positive or negative status falls under the category of nominal scale data.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a continuous variable?
options: Blood glucose value of a diabetic patient
Number of visits to the hospital in a year
questions.answer: C. Number of visits to the hospital in a year
questions.explanation:
The number of visits to the hospital in a year is a discrete variable. The only values it can take are whole numbers and none in between. For example, you can’t visit the hospital 2.5 times.

Blood glucose value, mid-arm circumference and birth weight are continuous variables. They can have any value within a limit or a range.

questions.question:
Match the following.

Data
Scale of data

1) Number of cancer patients in a hospital
a) Discrete data

2) Height and weight
b) Interval scale data

3) Blood pressure measurements
c) Ratio scale data

4) Temperature measurement in Celsius

5) Temperature measurement in Kelvin
questions.explanation:
The number of cancer patients in a hospital is an example of discrete data. They can only take certain values and none in between.

The temperature measured in the Celsius scale is an example of interval scale data. Such data are arranged in a meaningful order but they can not have an absolute zero value. For example, 80 degree celcius to not twice as hot as 40 degree celcius and 0 degree celcius does not indicate an absolute abscence of heat.

Height and weight, blood pressure and temperature in the Kelvin scale are examples of ratio scale data. Such data are arranged in a meaningful order and the scales they are measured in have absolute zero value. For example, a temperature of 0 kelvin indicates an absolute abscense of heat.

Height and weight, blood pressure, and temperature are examples of continuous data as they can take any values between limits or a range.

questions.question: Identify the following representation of data.
questions.explanation:
The image shown is of a boxplot. This is a method for graphically depicting groups of numerical data through their quartiles.

Box plots may also have lines extending vertically from the boxes (i.e., whiskers) indicating variability outside the upper and lower quartiles. Hence, they are also known as box-and-whisker plots and box-and-whisker diagrams.

The below image shows a boxplot depicting a series of experiments done to calculate the velocity of light.

A stem and leaf plot is used to depict frequency distribution and individual values for numerical data. The stem is are usually arranged in ascending or descending order vertically, and a vertical line is drawn to separate it from the leaf. The number of leaf items total up to the number of observations. It is difficult to represent a large number of observations using this method.

The below image shows a stem and leaf plot.

questions.question: Identify the following graphical representation of data.
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a frequency polygon. It is obtained by joining the midpoints of histogram blocks. It is used to diagrammatically represent frequency distribution.

Scattergram is a graph in which the values of two variables are plotted along two axes. The pattern of the resulting points reveals any correlation that may be present. The below image shows a scattergram.

A line diagram is a type of chart that displays information as a series of data points called 'markers' connected by straight line segments. It is usually used to study time trends.

questions.question: During a cholera outbreak, you are asked to map the geographical distribution of the disease. What is the best method of doing this?
questions.explanation:
Dot-density maps are the best way to plot the geographical distribution of diseases.

The image given below shows a dot-density map of London that was plotted during the 1854 outbreak of cholera.

questions.question: A doctor is taking history from a diabetic patient and decides to make a chart to assess joint involvement. Which chart should he make to explain this?
questions.explanation:
In this case, a tree diagram would help the doctor in explaining the possible outcomes to the patient’s diabetes, with the perspective of joint involvement.

A tree diagram is used mainly to chart the possible outcomes of a sample event.

The following image shows the outline of a tree diagram.

questions.question: What type of data does the image given below represent?
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a histogram. It is used to represent frequency distributions of continuous quantitative data.

Nominal and ordinal data can be represented by a bar chart.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to represent quantitative data?
questions.explanation:
An ogive, a line diagram and a histogram can be used to represent quantitative data.

The images shown above are:

A – Ogive

B – Bar graph

C – Line diagram

D – Histogram

Quantitative data cannot be represented by a bar graph. It is used mostly for nominal scale or qualitative data.

chapters.chapter: Descriptive Statistics Ii Measures Of Location

questions.question: Which of the following is not a measure of location?
questions.explanation:
Percentile is a measure of position. It can be defined as a number that states the percentage of observations that fall below any particular score.

Measures of location help in summarizing the data by locating its centre or middle. The three main measures of location include mean, median and mode. They are also called measures of central tendency.

questions.question: The mean can be calculated only if data is on:
questions.explanation:
The mean can be worked out only for quantitative values. Thus, it can be calculated for interval or ratio scale data.

A dichotomous scale is a type of nominal scale data that can take only two values. Example: Male/ Female. For nominal scale data, the preferred measure of central tendency is mode. For ordinal scale data, both median and mode can be calculated.

Median can be derived from ordinal, interval and ratio data scales. Mode can be derived from all scales of data- nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio.

questions.question: During a school health survey on malnutrition, the children are arranged according to ascending order of their heights. Which of the following can be obtained by this arrangement?
questions.explanation:
The 50th centile can be obtained when values are arranged in order and the central value is picked out. This is the same as the median.

In a distribution that has an odd number of elements, the median is the middle value.

In a distribution that has an even number of elements, the median is the average of the middle values, i.e., the arithmetic mean of the two middle values.

An example of how to calculate the median of an odd and an even number of elements is given below.

Option C: Geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.

Option D: Mean deviation is a measure of dispersion. The average of deviations from the arithmetic mean gives the mean deviation.

questions.question: Which of the following can have more than one value?
questions.explanation:
The mode of a given sample can have more than one value. It is the most frequently occurring value in a distribution.

For example, in the sample [1, 3, 6, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7, 12, 12, 17], the most repeated value i.e., the mode is 6.

For the list of data [1, 1, 2, 4, 4], the mode is 1 and 4. Therefore, the mode is not unique. This dataset may be said to be bimodal, while a set with more than two modes may be described as multimodal.

Median can have only one value, obtained by arranging values in order and then picking out the central value. In a sample with an even number of elements, median is obtained by taking the average of the middle 2 elements.

Mean can only have a single value. The harmonic mean is the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals of the data values. The geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.

questions.question: While collecting data on which of the following variables would median not be the preferred measure of central tendency?
questions.explanation:
Blood pressure usually forms a normal symmetrical distribution for which mean is the preferred measure of central tendency.

Distributions of survival time, incubation period and health expenses have the probability of having extreme values, i.e., outliers. Thus, they form skewed distributions and in such cases, median is the preferred measure of central tendency.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true for the given distribution of ages of patients who are visiting a family planning clinic in a day?

Age in years: 20, 31, 31, 31, 25, 28, 35, 38, 31.
questions.explanation:
The arithmetic mean from the following data is given by the sum of all the values, 270 divided by the number of values, 9 = 30.

The data can be arranged in ascending order as 20, 25, 28, 31, 31, 31, 31, 35, 38.

After arranging in order, the median is obtained by picking out the central value which is 31.

The mode is the most frequently occurring value, which is 31 here.

questions.question: You are conducting a study on birth weights in your hospital. Out of 11 births, 5 babies weighed over 2.5 kg, one baby weighed 2.5 kg and 5 weighed less than 2.5 kg. What does the value 2.5 represent in this distribution?
questions.explanation:
Out of the 11 birth weights, 2.5 kg would represent the middle value or the median. 5 babies weigh more than 2.5 kg and 5 less than that.

This can be understood from the image below.

Option A: Mean or arithmetic mean is the average value. In this case, the mean is the average of all the 11 values. It need not be 2.5.

Option B: Geometric mean is obtained by taking the arithmetic mean of values on a logarithmic scale.

Option D: Quartile is a measure of position, where the data is divided into four equal sets. 3/4 of the values are below the 3rd quartile reading. Hence, it cannot be the central reading.

questions.question:
You are conducting an epidemiological study on malaria in a town X. The number of cases reported during the last 10 years is given below. What is the most appropriate measure of central tendency for this data?

questions.explanation:
In this scenario, median is the preferred measure of central tendency as there are outliers.

The value of 5000 is an outlier in the given set, i.e., an observed value which is very distant from other observations in the distribution. This indicates the usage of median as the measure of central tendency as it is not sensitive to extreme values, unlike the mean.

By arranging the data in order: 100, 160, 190, 250, 260, 300, 320, 320, 350, 5000, we get the median as (260 + 300) / 2 = 280.

Options A and B: Mean is the most affected by the presence of outliers. Mode is the least affected by outliers but it is used mainly for measuring the central tendency of nominal data.

Option D: Geometric mean can be used for datasets with extreme values but it is not used when the values can be zero or negative. In the given scenario, the number of malaria cases reported in a town can also have a zero value.

questions.question: During a school health assessment, the mean value of weight for a group of 10 boys was found to be 18.2 kg. Later, it was found that the weight of one of the boys was wrongly recorded as 2.0 kg instead of 20 kg. What is the true mean weight of the group?
questions.explanation:
The true mean weight of the group is 20 kg.

Mean is given as x̄ = ∑x / n, where n is the number of elements and ∑x denotes the sum of all the elements in the series.

In this scenario, the incorrect mean is 18.2, i.e.,
 ∑x / 10 = 18.2, making ∑x = 182.
But this is incorrect as one of the 10 weights was wrongly recorded as 2 instead of 20.

The corrected ∑x = (Incorrect ∑x – incorrect value) + correct value.

The incorrect sum of all elements = 182, incorrect value =2 and the correct value = 20.

Thus, the correct sum of all the 10 weights would be,
∑x = (182 – 2) + 20 = 200.

From this, the correct mean value of the 10 weights can be given by:
∑x / 10 = 200/ 10 = 20.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct about the given distribution of ages of patients attending a geriatric medicine clinic?

Age in years: 70, 70, 76, 76, 80, 83, 84, 85
questions.explanation:
For the given dataset, the modes are 70 and 76. The mode is the most frequently occurring value. It can have multiple values. In this scenario, the values 70 and 76 have been repeated twice.

Median of this distribution is the central value, (76 + 80) / 2 = 78.

questions.question:
