Two packs
questions.explanation:
The distribution in this scenario in terms of the number of cigarettes smoked is 5, 10, 10, 10, 20, 40.

The mean here is ∑x/n = 95/6 = 15.833 rounded off to 16.

The median here is the central value = average of 3rd and 4th values since the distribution has an even number of values. This comes to (10 + 10) / 2 = 10.

The mode here is 10 which has a frequency of 3 in the given dataset.

questions.question: While reviewing a data distribution, you find that the highest value of 58 was wrongly recorded as 85 and so you correct it. How will this correction change the measures of central tendency?
options: No change in mean, decreased median
Decreased mean, no change in median
questions.answer: B. Decreased mean, no change in median
questions.explanation:
The given change in a dataset would cause a decrease in the mean but the median would remain unchanged.

The mean is sensitive to every value in the distribution. Since the correct value of 58 is much lesser than the wrongly recorded value of 85, the final mean will be decreased compared to the earlier recorded value.

However, as only the highest value was wrongly recorded, the median i.e., the central value, will remain the same.

questions.question:
While conducting a study on the age at death in males of a population Y, the distribution curve given below is obtained. Which of the following is true?

1. It is a positively skewed distribution

2. It is a left skewed distribution

3. Mean > median > mode

4. It is a bimodal distribution

5. Mean < median < mode
questions.explanation:
The given image shows a negatively skewed or a left-skewed distribution curve. Here, mean < median < mode.

Mode is the most frequently occurring value in the distribution and is given by the highest point of the graph. Since the given graph has only one peak, it is unimodal.

A positively skewed distribution refers to a right-skewed distribution. In such cases, mean > median > mode.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of measures of central tendency is likely to match the distribution depicted in the given image?
questions.explanation:
The given image is of a right-skewed or positively skewed distribution. So, among the given options, the most likely values of mean = 3, median = 2, and mode = 1.

We can tell the direction of skew of a distribution by observing the direction of the tail. Here, the tail of the distribution is towards the positive direction and thus it is positively skewed or right-skewed. In a positively skewed distribution, mean > median > mode.

If the tail of the distribution is towards the negative direction, the distribution would be negatively skewed or left-skewed. In such distributions, mode > median > mean.

questions.question: You are conducting a study on blood pressure in a population. The systolic blood pressure values have a mean of 130 mmHg, a median of 140 mmHg and mode of 160 mmHg. What type of distribution is this?
questions.explanation:
This is a unimodal negatively skewed distribution.

In this scenario, the mean of 130 mmHg is less than the median of 140 mmHg which is less than mode of 160mmHg. Since mean<median<mode, this is an asymmetrical negatively skewed or left-skewed distribution.

It is a unimodal distribution as there is only a single value for mode.

In a symmetrical distribution, the mean = median = mode.

In a positively skewed distribution, mean > median > mode.

questions.question: The mean of a dataset is 2 and the median is 3. What is the mode?
questions.explanation:
As the mean ≠ median, this is an asymmetric distribution and so we can use the formula:

Mode = 3 median - 2 mean.

Using the given values, mode = (3x3) – (2x2) = 9 – 4 = 5.

A distribution is termed symmetric when the mean, median and mode coincide i.e., mean= median= mode.

chapters.chapter: Descriptive Statistics Iii Measures Of Dispersion

questions.question: Which of the following is not a measure of dispersion?
questions.explanation:
Z scores are not a measure of dispersion, they are measures of position. It indicates the position of any element in a distribution in terms of how many standard deviations it lies from the mean of the distribution.

The most common measures of spread/dispersion are range, standard deviation and variance. They help in determining the extent to which data is stretched/scattered or squeezed/clustered.

They are also called measures of spread or scatter or variability.

questions.question: What is standard deviation a measure of?
questions.explanation:
Standard deviation is a measure of spread or dispersion or variability.

Range and variability are other measures of spread.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct relationship between variance and standard deviation?
options: Variance = square root of standard deviation
Standard deviation = square root of variance
questions.answer: B. Standard deviation = square root of variance
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance.

questions.question: You are conducting a study on chronic kidney disease in a population. Your sample size is 28. What formula for standard deviation will you use here?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the sample size is 28, which is <30. For a small sample, usually less than 30, the formula for standard deviation used is:

It is better to use n-1 in the denominator in the case of a small sample. But in the case of a very large sample subtracting 1 from a huge number will not make much of a significant correction. In those cases, we may choose to ignore subtracting 1.

questions.question: Which among the following is true about standard deviation?
options: One standard deviation covers 95% of the values
It can be used only in normal distributions
It is a measure of central tendency
questions.explanation:
The standard deviation (S.D) indicates the distribution of variables. It is a measure of dispersion.

It can be used in normal and skewed distributions, but it is particularly useful in normal distributions.

1 S.D covers 68% of the values. 2 S.D covers 95% of the values.

Measures of central tendency are mean, median and mode.

questions.question: You are using the Kuppuswamy scale to calculate the socio-economic status of 10 families in the railway staff quarters. You find that every family has a total monthly income of Rs. 73,355. What is the standard deviation of this sample?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the standard deviation will be zero.

The monthly income of every family is Rs. 73,355. So, all the elements in this distribution are the same. Hence, there is no variability. Both the standard deviation and variance which is the square of standard deviation will be zero.

questions.question: Each value of a study sample is multiplied by 10. What would be the new standard deviation of the observations?
questions.explanation:
When each element of a sample is multiplied by 10, the new standard deviation= 10 x original standard deviation.

The formula for standard deviation, SD = √∑(x - x̄)2/n-1.

If each element of the distribution is multiplied by 10, the new mean will become 10 times the original mean.

If all observations are multiplied by 10, then the new SD = √∑(10x-10x̄)2/n-1

= 10 √∑(x - x̄)2/n-1

= 10 x Original SD

Change in variance: variance = square of standard deviation, so when SD becomes 10 times,

the variance will be 10² = 100 times the original variance.

questions.question:
On plotting the blood pressure values of a population on a graph, you obtain the curve given below. Which of the following is true?

1. It is a Gaussian distribution

2. Mean = median ≠ mode

3. It is defined by the mean and standard deviation

4. There is no skew in the distribution

5. The area under the curve depends on the mean
questions.explanation:
The given image shows a normal distribution, also called bell curve or Gaussian distribution. It has no skew. It is defined by the mean and standard deviation. In a normal distribution, mean = median = mode.

The total area under the curve of a normal distribution is 1.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true about the standard normal distribution?

1. It has a mean of 1.0

2. It is bell shaped

3. It has a standard deviation of 0.0

4. It has a variance of 1.0

5. Standard deviation = variance
questions.explanation: A standard normal distribution is a type of normal distribution. It is bell-shaped, has a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Thus the variance, the square of standard deviation is also 1 = the standard deviation.

questions.question: During a study on anaemia in a population, a normal distribution curve with a mean of 13.5 g% is obtained. What proportion of the population constitutes people with haemoglobin values above 13.5 g%?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, 0.50, i.e., 50% of the population would have haemoglobin more than the mean, i.e., 13.5 gm%. In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie above the mean.

questions.question: The IQ scores of your study population form a bell-shaped curve. How much of the population falls between the median (Mdn) and Mdn + 1 S.D?
questions.explanation:
34% or 0.34 of the population in a normal distribution falls between the median and median plus one standard deviation.

The IQ values form a bell-shaped curve, which is seen in normal symmetric distributions.

According to the empirical rule of normal distributions, 68% of the distribution falls within 1 standard deviation of the mean, i.e., mean ± 1 SD covers 68% of the distribution.

Now, in a normal distribution, mean = median. Therefore, this 68% includes values from median -1SD to median +1SD.

The question asks about the percentage that falls under median +1SD, which would be half of 68%, that is 34% or 0.34.

Below is the graphical representation of the question. The question is asking to calculate the shaded region in the graph.

questions.question:
The fasting blood glucose levels of adults in a population forms a normal distribution. The statistical measures obtained are given below. Within what limits would 95% of the population have their blood glucose values?

Mean- 105 mg per 100 ml

Standard deviation- 10mg per 100 ml
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, 95% of the population would have their blood sugar within the limits of 85 and 125 mg. Here, the mean blood sugar is 105 mg and the standard deviation is 10 mg.

According to the empirical rule of normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean.

In this question, 2 S.D = 10 x 2 = 20. We do, + and - 2 S.D from the mean to arrive at the limits within which 95% of the population would have their blood sugar, i.e., 85 and 125 mg.

+ and - 1 S.D = 10 from the mean, we get the limits within which 68% of the population would have their blood sugar value, i.e., 95 and 115 mg.

+ and - 3 S.D = 30, from the mean, we get limits within which 99% would have their values, i.e., 75 and 135 mg.

questions.question:
While conducting a study on malnutrition, you record the following data. If it forms a normal distribution curve, which of the following is true for this sample?

No. of children: 100

Mean weight: 15kg

Standard deviation: 1.5kg
options: Weight of 95 children is between 12 and 18 kg
Weight of 95 children is between 10.5 and 19.5 kg
Weight of 99 children is between 10 and 19 kg
Weight of 34 children is between 13.5 and 16.5 kg
questions.answer: A. Weight of 95 children is between 12 and 18 kg
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the weight of 95 children will be between 12 and 18 kg as the mean is 15 kg and the standard deviation is 1.5 kg.

According to the empirical rule of normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean. Two standard deviations = 2 x 1.5 = 3 kg

The weight of 99.7% of children will be between 10.5-19.5 Kg, i.e., within three standard deviations.

The weight of 68% of children will be between 13.5 to 16.5 Kg, i.e., within one standard deviation. Half will weigh between 13.5 and 15kg and the other half between 15 and 16.5kg

questions.question: The distribution of intraocular pressure (IOP) in 100 glaucoma patients form a normal distribution curve. It has a mean of 30 mm of Hg with a standard deviation (SD) of 1 mm of Hg. 97.5% of patients would have an IOP more than what value?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, 97.5% of patients would have an IOP of more than 28 mm of Hg.

The mean IOP is 30mm of Hg and SD is 1.0 mm of Hg. According to the empirical rule of the normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean ± 2 SD. So 95% of patients will have their IOP between 30 ± 2 = 28 to 32 mm of Hg.

Out of the remaining 5%, half will have IOP < 28 and the other half will have > 32. So half of 5%= 2.5% has IOP <28mm Hg. Thus the remaining 97.5% has IOP > 28mm of Hg.

This is shown in the image given below

questions.question: A study is being conducted on anaemia in pregnancy. A normal distribution curve with a mean haemoglobin level of 10.6 gm/dL with a standard deviation of 2 gm/dL is obtained. Below what level would 5% of the women in the group have their haemoglobin values?
questions.explanation:
5% of the pregnant women in this group will have their haemoglobin levels below 7.31 g/dL.

Solution:
Given Data :

• Mean: 10.6 g/dL

• Standard deviation : 2 g/dL

Step 1:

According to the empirical rule of a normal distribution, 95% of the population fall within 2 standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean ± 2SD.
This implies that the remaining 5% lie outside 2 SD, i.e. 2.5% below 2 SD and 2.5% above 2 SD.
Therefore , Mean - 2SD = 10.6 − 2 (2)
 = 10.6 − 4
 = 6.6 g/dL
Thus, 2.5% of pregnant women have Hb levels below 6.6 g/dL.

However, the question asks about 5% and not 2.5%. So options C and D have been ruled out.

Now Let's move to the next step.

Step 2:

According to the empirical rule of a normal distribution, 68% of the population fall within 1 standard deviation of the mean, i.e., mean±1SD.
This implies that the remaining 32% lie outside 1 SD, i.e., 16% below 1 SD and 16% above 1 SD.
The value of mean−1 SD is 8.6 g/dL (i.e. 10.6 − 2)
Thus, 16% of pregnant women have Hb levels below 8.6 g/dL.

so now option A is ruled out

Step 3:

The value for 5% must lie between the values where 2.5% and 16% of the population lie, i.e., between 6.6g/dL and 8g/dL. Only option B, 7.31 g/dL, satisfies this condition.

Hence, 5% of pregnant women have their Hb levels below 7.31 g/dL.

questions.question: The peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) values of a group of 11-year-old girls have a mean of 300 l/min and a standard deviation of 20 l/min. What are the deviation scores for the PEFR values of two girls recorded as 280 l/min and 330 l/min respectively?
questions.explanation:
The deviation scores for PEFR values 280 l/min and 330 l/min are -20 and 30 respectively.

The Deviation score of an element in a distribution is the difference between the mean of the distribution and the element itself, i.e., it is obtained by subtracting the distribution’s mean from the element.

Applying this here, deviation score of the value 280 l/min = the element - the mean = 280 - 300 = -20.

For the value 330 l/min, deviation score = 330 - 300 = 30.

questions.question: The shape of a normal distribution curve depends on?
questions.explanation:
The shape of a normal distribution curve depends upon its mean and standard deviation.

For example, for a particular mean value, a smaller standard deviation value gives a taller and narrower curve whereas, a larger value gives a flatter curve.

The curve is centered at the mean μ which coincides with the median and the mode and is located at the point beneath the peak of the curve. The mean, median and mode are equal.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of a normal distribution curve?
questions.explanation:
In a normal distribution curve, mean = median.

mean > median in positively/ rightward skewed distribution.

mean < median in negatively/ leftward skewed distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about the standard normal distribution?
questions.explanation: In a standard normal distribution, mean = 0.

questions.question: A population study showed a mean glucose of 86 mg/dL. In a sample of 100 showing normal distribution, what percentage of people will have blood glucose above 86 mg/dL?
questions.explanation:
In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie above the mean.

In this scenario, 50% of the people will have a blood glucose level of more than 86 mg/dL.

questions.question: The mean value of marks in a distribution of 100 students in a class is 105 and standard deviation is 10. How many students will have their marks between 85 and 125?
questions.explanation:
According to the empirical rule of normal distribution, 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean ± 2 SD.

In this scenario, the marks between 85 and 125 fall within 2 standard deviation of the mean which is 105. Thus 95% of the students will have the marks in this range.

questions.question: The systolic blood pressure of a group of normal people between the ages of 25–27 years was taken and a mean of 120 mmHg was found. What will be the expected number of individuals among a group of 100 people taken for the study whose BP will be below 120 mmHg?
questions.explanation:
In a normal distribution, 50% of the values lie below the mean.

In this scenario, 50%, i.e., 50 of the 100 people will have a systolic BP of less than 120 mmHg.

questions.question: In a normal distribution, what percentage of the distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean?
questions.explanation: According to the empirical rule of normal distributions, 95% of the distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean, i.e., mean ± 2 SD covers 95% of the distribution.

chapters.chapter: Descriptive Statistics Iv Measures Of Position

questions.question: Which of the following is not a measure of position?
questions.explanation:
Range is not a measure of position, it is a measure of dispersion or spread.

The most common measures of position are quantiles, quartiles, centiles and z-scores (standard scores). Measures of position give the position of specific data in relation to other data in the set.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about quantiles are true?

1. They divide data into equal groups

2. They are used for discrete data

3. Median is a type of quantile

4. Quintiles divide the distribution into 4 equal parts

5. They are also known as fractiles
questions.explanation:
Quantiles are elements in a distribution that divide data into equal groups. They are also known as fractiles. Median divides a distribution into two equal parts, so it is considered as a quantile.

Quantiles are used for continuous, quantitative data.

Quintiles are a type of quantile that divides data into 5 equal groups.

questions.question: Centiles divide data into ____ equal parts?
questions.explanation: Centiles divide data into 100 equal parts.

questions.question: During a school health camp, a group of 250 students are arranged in the ascending order of their height. Which student would have the 40th percentile value for height?
questions.explanation:
Here, the 100th student will have the 40th percentile value for height.

To arrive at this, we use the formula R = P/100 x (n + 1).
 where R is the rank of the desired observation, P is the quantile/percentile desired and n is the number of variables in the data.

Thus, R = 40/100 x (250 + 1) = 0.4 x 251 = 100.4.

This is rounded up to the closest number making R = 100.

questions.question: By calculating which of the following can we obtain the central value of a sample with 180 elements?
questions.explanation:
The 2nd quartile gives the central value of 180 elements. The central value of a distribution is given by the median. It divides the distribution into the ratio of 1:1.

In quartiles elements of the distribution are divided into 4 equal parts by 3 values. Each part contains a quarter, i.e., 25% of the values. So two quarters would give half of the values. So the element present at the position of the 2nd quartile would be the central value, i.e., the median, with half the values before and half the values after it. This is shown in the image given below.

The 5th decile and 50th percentile represent the median values of a distribution in decile and percentile respectively.

questions.question: Which measure of position divides the distribution in a ratio of 3:1?
questions.explanation:
Third quartile Q3 divides the distribution into the ratio of 3:1.

In quartiles:

• the first quartile Q1 divides the distribution in the ratio of 1:3

• the second quartile Q2 divides it in the ratio of 1:1.

The division of data by quartiles is shown in the below image.

Centiles divide data into 100 equal parts. 33rd centile divides the distribution in the ratio of 33:67.

Deciles divide data into 10 equal parts. 7th decile divides the distribution in the ratio of 7:3.

questions.question: You are recording the blood pressure values of 200 adults in a population. The first quartile diastolic BP is 68 mmHg and the third quartile is 105 mmHg. How many patients are there in the 3rd and 4th quarters?
questions.explanation:
In a quartile, the data is divided into 4 equal parts, i.e., 4 quarters. Therefore, in this scenario, there are 50% of patients in the 3rd and 4th quarters, i.e 100 patients.

The division of data by quartiles is shown in the image given below.

questions.question: The forced expiratory volume (FEV) of 300 patients visiting the respiratory medicine outpatient department is recorded. The data has a median value of 2.5 litres with the first and third quartiles being 1.5 litres and 4.5 litres respectively. How many persons in the sample are expected to have an FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres?
questions.explanation:
150 persons are expected to have FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres.

In a quartile, the data is divided by 3 values into 4 equal parts. Thus, each part will have 25% of the values in the distribution.

In this scenario, each part will have 75 persons. Here, 1.5 is the first quartile Q1, 2.5 is the second quartile Q2 and 4.5 is the third quartile Q3. Between Q1 and Q3 there are two quarters, thus there will be 150 people with FEV between 1.5 and 4.5 litres.

Data division by quartiles is shown in the below image.

questions.question: Which of the following distributions is preferred for the calculation of z scores?
questions.explanation: Z scores are usually calculated in normal distributions.

questions.question: In a study on haemoglobin levels in healthy women, the data recorded has a mean of 13.5 gm/dL and a standard deviation of 1.5 gm/dL. What is the z score for an element with a haemoglobin value of 15.0 gm/dL?
questions.explanation:
The Z score for the element with a haemoglobin value of 15 gm/dL is 1.0.

The formula for z score, z = (X- µ)/σ.

X is the value of the element, µ is the mean and σ is the standard deviation.

In this scenario, z = (15 – 13.5) / 1.5 = 1.5/1.5 = 1.

questions.question: The diastolic BP of 125 women aged between 18 and 60 years was recorded. The mean of the data is 70 mmHg with a standard deviation of 10 mmHg. What will be the 5th percentile value?
questions.explanation:
The z value for the 5th percentile is -1.645.

Using the formula for z scores, z = (X- µ)/σ, we get X = zσ + µ.

In this scenario, X = (-1.645 x 10) + 70 = -16.45 + 70 = 53.55 = 53.6.

questions.question: The statistical methods that go further than merely summarizing data are a part of:
questions.explanation:
Inferential statistics are those statistical methods that go further than just summarizing data.

They involve inductive reasoning and using a statistic to estimate a parameter. E.g., the expected success rate of vasectomy or mean blood pressure of all Indians.

One of the most common problems faced in research is using information gathered by researching a sample and then drawing conclusions about the population from which the sample is drawn. Here, sample statistics (sample mean and SD) are known and population parameters (population mean and SD) are unknown.

Inferential statistical methods are used to draw conclusions about the population parameters from sample statistics.

questions.question: Which of the following measures relative variation between two different units?
questions.explanation: Co-efficient of variation (CV) measures the relative variability between two different units, by using the mean and standard deviation.

questions.question: The weight of the 100 children that presented in the pediatric OPD in the last week was analyzed. The median weight was 12 kg and the standard deviation was 3. This data formed a normal distribution. What is the coefficient of variation?
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, coefficient of variance (CV) = 25%.

Coefficient of variation, CV = standard deviation x 100/ mean = 3 x 100/12 = 25%.

In a normal distribution, mean = median.

questions.question: The means of all possible samples from a population are plotted on a linear graph. What is this called?
questions.explanation: The random sampling distribution of means is the distribution formed when all possible sample means from a population are plotted in a frequency distribution.

questions.question: Central limit theorem is related to:
questions.explanation:
The central limit theorem is related to the random sampling distribution of means.

According to this theorem, as the sample size increases:

1. The sampling distribution tends towards a normal distribution curve (bell curve)

• Regardless of the population's actual distribution shape

• Assuming all samples are identical in size

2. The sample mean and standard deviations become closer to the population mean and standard deviations

questions.question: A researcher wanted to calculate the mean age of onset of type II diabetes mellitus in a population. He got a sample mean of 45. To measure the extent of deviation from the population mean, which of the following should he use?
questions.explanation: The standard error is a measure of the extent to which the sample means deviate from the true population means.

questions.question: Standard deviation of mean measures variations caused by:
questions.explanation: The standard deviation of mean or standard error of means measures variations caused by sampling errors.

questions.question: Consider a sample of 100 women with an average Hb of 10 g% and standard deviation of 1. What is the standard error of this sample?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the standard error SE = 0.1.

The formula for standard error:

SE = Standard deviation/ √sample size =1/√100 = 1/10 = 0.1

questions.question: All of the following are true about standard error except:
options: It increases as the sample size increases.
It is based on a normal distribution
It depends on the standard deviation of means
It is used to estimate confidence limits
questions.answer: A. It increases as the sample size increases.
questions.explanation:
As the sample size increases, the standard error will decrease, not increase.

The standard error is inversely related to the square root of the sample size.

questions.question:
The incubation period for measles in a group of 25 children was calculated. Following findings were recorded. What is the standard error?

Standard deviation = 2.

Median incubation period = 8 days.
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the standard error = 0.4.

The formula for standard error:

SE = Standard deviation/√sample size = 2/√25 = 2/5 = 0.4

questions.question: The uppermost and lowermost values of standard errors within which a parameter value is expected to lie are called the:
questions.explanation:
The uppermost and lowermost limits of standard errors within which a parameter value is expected to lie are called the confidence limits.

The difference between upper and lower confidence limits is called the confidence interval.

questions.question: Which of the following parameters are used to calculate the confidence limit?
questions.explanation: Confidence limits are calculated with the sample mean and standard error.

questions.question: During screening of a population, the mean cholesterol levels were found to be 230mg/dL. The standard error was 10. Calculate the 95% confidence limits.
questions.explanation:
In the given scenario, 95% confidence limits are 210 – 250.

In inferential statistics, 95% confidence limits = Sample mean (x̄) ± 2 standard errors.

In this case, mean is 230 and the standard error is 10. Hence, confidence limits are 210-250.

questions.question: What is the hypothesis which states that an apparent effect is only due to chance, called as?
questions.explanation: The hypothesis that an apparent effect is only due to chance is a null hypothesis. If this is rejected as false, we have an alternative hypothesis.

questions.question: What is the significance level in hypothesis testing called as?
questions.explanation: Significance level in hypothesis testing is called alpha level (α) or criterion.

questions.question: What is the p value?
options: Probability of declaring a significant difference when there is none in reality
Probability of declaring a significant difference when it is actually present
Probability of not declaring a significant difference when actually it is not present
Probability of not declaring a significant difference when actually it is present
questions.answer: A. Probability of declaring a significant difference when there is none in reality
questions.explanation: p-value can be defined as the probability of declaring a significant difference when there is none in reality.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is false about the p-value?
options: It is equal to the probability of committing a type I error
It is the chance that the presence of difference is concluded when actually there may be none
When the p value is less than α, the result is statistically significant
questions.explanation:
The power of a test is 1 – beta.

The p value is the probability that a type I error is being made. It is the chance that the presence of difference is concluded when actually there may be none. When the p value is less than α, the result is statistically significant.

questions.question: A randomized control trial comparing the efficacy of two chemotherapy regimens for Hodgkin's lymphoma showed that their difference is statistically significant with p < 0.001. However, in reality the two drugs do not differ in their efficacy. What type of error is this an example of?
questions.explanation:
This is an example of a type I error.

In this scenario, let us take the null hypothesis as the efficacy of two drugs being the same, which as the question states, is true in reality. The alternative hypothesis will then be that one drug is better than the other.

The questions states that p-value was found to be < 0.001, which is statistically significant and so the null hypothesis is rejected. But we already know that the null hypothesis is true and we are forced to accept the alternative hypothesis even though it is false.

When an alternative hypothesis is accepted even when it is false and the null hypothesis is true, it is called as a type I error or an alpha error or a false positive error.

questions.question: An investigator is conducting a study to assess the effect of a mood stabiliser on patients with bipolar I disorder. What does it mean if the difference is significant in the results?
options: p > 0.05 and it is likely by chance
p > 0.05 and it is unlikely by chance
p < 0.05 and it is unlikely by chance
p < 0.05 and it is likely by chance
questions.answer: C. p < 0.05 and it is unlikely by chance
questions.explanation: When the difference is significant, it means that the difference is unlikely by chance and p will be ≤ 0.05.

questions.question: While assessing the effect of a new intervention for type II DM, you obtain the p-value of the study as 0.023. Based on this observation, what is your inference?
options: Null hypothesis is accepted and the study is rejected
Null hypothesis is rejected and the study is accepted
Null hypothesis is accepted and the study is accepted
Null hypothesis is rejected and the study is also rejected
questions.answer: B. Null hypothesis is rejected and the study is accepted
questions.explanation: By convention, if the p value ≤ 0.05, the difference is said to be statistically significant. Thus, the null hypothesis is rejected and the study is accepted.

questions.question: Which of the following is a false statement regarding hypothesis testing?
options: Alpha is the maximum tolerable probability of a type 1 error being made
Beta is the probability of a type II error
When the null hypothesis is true but rejected, it is a type II error
p value can be more or less than alpha
questions.answer: C. When the null hypothesis is true but rejected, it is a type II error
questions.explanation:
When the null hypothesis is true but is still rejected, it is a type I error and not a type II error.
Type II errors are when an alternative hypothesis is rejected even though it is true.

questions.question: You are conducting a randomised clinical trial to see if a new drug 'A' has better efficacy than the standard drug 'B', in patients with grade III hypertension. While analysing the results of this study, you conclude that no difference exists between the two. But in reality, a difference between them truly exists. What type of error are you making?
questions.explanation:
Type II errors are when an alternative hypothesis is rejected when it is true.

In this scenario, the null hypothesis is that there is no difference and the alternative hypothesis is that there is a difference.

We failed to reject the null hypothesis that says there is no difference, and so we are making a type II error. In other words, we have rejected the alternative hypothesis that there is an difference when it is true.

questions.question: Power of a study is the ability of a test to _____
questions.explanation:
The power of a study is its ability to avoid or decrease beta errors or type II errors.

The statistical power of a test is represented by 1 – β.

questions.question: You are an investigator conducting a statistical test. You obtain the p value as 0.01 for your study. What does this mean?
options: The probability of finding a significant difference is 1%
There is a 1% probability that the difference is not by chance
The difference is not significant 1% of times and significant 99% of times
The power of the test used is 99%
questions.answer: C. The difference is not significant 1% of times and significant 99% of times
questions.explanation:
If the p-value = 0.01, then the difference is not significant 1% of the time and significant 99% of the time.

In other words, there is a 99% probability that the difference is not by chance and there is a 1% probability that the difference is only by chance.

questions.question: Which of these tests is used in case of a nominal data?
questions.explanation:
Chi-square test deals with nominal/ non-parametric data (qualitative).

Nominal data is one with a name and does not have a numerical value. Ex blood group, gender, religion

Student's t test, ANOVA, and paired t test are used for parametric data (quantitative).

questions.question: Which of these terms is used for paired t tests?
questions.explanation: Paired t tests are also called correlated pairs t test, paired samples t test, or dependent samples t test.

questions.question: A researcher can use the chi-square test in all of the following situations, except:
options: To test the hypothesis that drug A has the same potency as drug B
To calculate the degree of freedom of a 3 x 4 contingency table
To compare the mean corpuscular volume in normal subjects versus those suffering from hereditary spherocytosis
To compare the proportions of overweight boys and girls in a class
questions.answer: C. To compare the mean corpuscular volume in normal subjects versus those suffering from hereditary spherocytosis
questions.explanation:
The Chi-square test is not used for comparing means for different groups as means can only be calculated for quantitative data.

The Chi-square test is used for qualitative data. It can be used:

• To test the null hypothesis

• To compare proportions

• To calculate the degree of freedom

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about the Chi-square test?
options: Tests the significance of difference between two proportions
Tells about the presence or absence of an association between two variables
Directly measures the strength of association
It is usually used for skewed data
questions.answer: C. Directly measures the strength of association
questions.explanation: A Chi-square test does not directly measure the strength of association. It merely tells about the presence or lack of association.

questions.question: A Chi-square test would be most appropriate for testing which of the following hypotheses?
options: The mean AIPGE score of Chennai students is greater than Mumbai students
A smaller proportion of people who were immunized against chicken pox subsequently develop zoster than those who were not immunized
The mean BP of indian, american and english hypertensive men taking ACE inhibitors is the same as that of indian, american and english hypertensive women on ACEIs
The mean cost of treating a patient with CAD by angioplasty is greater than the mean cost of providing medical treatment
questions.answer: B. A smaller proportion of people who were immunized against chicken pox subsequently develop zoster than those who were not immunized
questions.explanation:
The Chi-square test is used to compare proportions or qualitative variables e.g., whether people developed zoster or not.

Options A and D: Two independent groups are being compared with quantitative variables (exam scores and cost, respectively). Thus, an unpaired t test will be used.

Option C: The blood pressure of 3 groups are being compared, thus making analysis of variance (ANOVA) the most appropriate method of testing significance.

questions.question: A cardiologist wants to study the effect of the atorvastatin drug. She measures the initial cholesterol levels of 50 patients. After a month's treatment, she measures the cholesterol level again. Which of the following tests will she use to test the statistical significance of the change in the cholesterol level?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the variable (cholesterol level) is quantitative. Moreover, the comparison is being done before and after the treatment (dependent). Hence, a paired t test will be used.

questions.question: In a particular trial, the association of lung cancer with smoking is found to be 40% in one sample and 60% in another. What is the best test to compare the results?
questions.explanation: Chi-square tests are best used in comparing proportions and associations.

questions.question: A pediatrician carried out a study to assess the difference in growth velocities in boys and girls. The average height of a group of 20 boys aged 10 years was 140 ± 13 cm and for 20 girls of the same age was 135 ± 7 cm. To test the statistical significance of the difference in height, which test would she use?
questions.explanation: In the given scenario, two independent groups are being compared with quantitative variables. Thus, a student t test or unpaired t-test is used.

questions.question: Analysis of variance test is used in which scenario among the following?
options: Comparing proportions in more than 2 groups
Comparing means in more than 2 groups
Comparing means in same groups before and after intervention
Comparing means in less than or equal to 2 groups
questions.answer: B. Comparing means in more than 2 groups
questions.explanation: Analysis of variance or ANOVA is used when more than 2 groups are compared for a quantitative difference (means).

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate test for testing the statistical significance of the difference in heights of school children?
questions.explanation:
Analysis of variance or ANOVA is used when more than 2 variable groups are compared.

In the scenario of comparing heights of school children, we would divide the school children into classes or grades or sections or by schools themselves, etc. This would involve comparing more than 2 groups and thus ANOVA is used.

Remember if the question limits its comparison within 2 groups, for example, comparison between boys and girls in a class then we have to choose unpaired t test.

questions.question: An investigator wants to study the association between maternal intake of iron supplements and the incidence of low birth weight. He collects relevant data from 100 pregnant women regarding the status of usage of iron supplements and the status of birth weight in their newborns. Which of the following tests will he use for his study?
questions.explanation: Here, two qualitative variables are being evaluated. First, whether the child belongs to the low birth weight category or not (and not the actual weight of the child, which is a quantitative value). Second, whether or not the mother took iron supplements in the gestational period. Hence, the chi-square test is used as the test the significance of the association.

questions.question: In a study, two groups of newborns are checked for differences in their birth weights based on whether mothers received supplements or not. Which of the following would be most appropriate test of significance?
questions.explanation: The unpaired t-test is used to test the difference between two groups of parametric variables or means when the samples are independent of each other. Here, birth weights (quantitative variable) of the two groups of newborns are being compared, which are independent of each other.

questions.question: A study was planned to find out the effect of iron supplementation during pregnancy on the birth weight of newborn children. Two groups, one with iron supplementation and the other without, were compared. Birth weights of newborns were recorded as means + SD. Which statistical test is appropriate for the comparison of birth weights between the two groups?
questions.explanation: In the given scenario, we aim to compare only the birth weights of the two groups, which is a quantitative data, and thus an unpaired t test is most appropriate.

questions.question: While applying the Chi-square test to a contingency table of 4 rows and 4 columns, what would the degree of freedom be in this case?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, df = (4 – 1) (4 – 1) = 9.

In a Chi-square test for a contingency table, the degrees of freedom (df) = (r-1) (c-1), where r is the number of rows and c is the number of columns.

questions.question: In a Chi-square test for the following data, the degrees of freedom will be:
questions.explanation:
In this scenario,contingency table has 3 rows and 4 columns. Hence, the degree of freedom, df = (3 – 1) (4 – 1) = 6.

In a Chi-square test for a contingency table, the degrees of freedom (df) = (r-1) (c-1), where r is the number of rows and c is the number of columns.

questions.question: A study is conducted to find the relationship between the height and weight of school students. Which of the following would be useful in this study?
questions.explanation:
The coefficient of correlation can be used to determine the relationship between both variables in this scenario. It is used to express the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables.

It is represented by the letter 'r'. Its value ranges from -1 to +1.

questions.question: Which among the following is false about correlation?
options: It indicates the strength of relationship between 2 variables
Correlation coefficient of 1 indicates a linear relationship
questions.answer: D. Correlation implies a causal relationship
questions.explanation:
A correlation between 2 variables only indicates the strength of the relationship between two variables, not causation.

A correlation coefficient of 1 indicates a linear relationship. It cannot measure the risk.

questions.question: During a study conducted to assess the effect of smoking on life expectancy, the correlation coefficient was found to be 0.60. Calculate the coefficient of determination for this study.
questions.explanation:
The coefficient of determination (CD) for this study is 0.36 (36%).

It is calculated by r2, where r is the correlation coefficient. In this study, the correlation coefficient (r) is 0.6.

Hence CD = (0.6)2 = 0.36

The coefficient of determination refers to the percentage variability in one variable due to a change in the other variable. In the above study, a coefficient of determination of 0.36 means that 36% of the variation in life expectancy is accounted for by smoking.

questions.question: What is the best way to study relationship between two variables?
questions.explanation:
A scattergram/ scatter plot is the best way to study the relationship between 2 variables.

The following image shows a scatter plot.

The following image shows a forest plot.

The following image shows a funnel plot.

The following image shows a frequency polygon.

questions.question: A psychiatry resident is conducting a study to assess the relationship between prefrontal blood flow under cognitive load and the severity of psychotic symptoms in schizophrenic patients. He calculates the correlation coefficient as -1.24. You can therefore conclude that:
options: Prefrontal blood flow is a good predictor of the severity of psychotic symptoms
Prefrontal blood flow accounts for most of the variance in symptoms
Schizophrenia causes low prefrontal blood flow
The correlation coefficient has been calculated incorrectly
questions.answer: D. The correlation coefficient has been calculated incorrectly
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the correlation coefficient (r) of -1.24 is incorrect, as 'r' can only lie between -1 to +1.

questions.question: In a random sample of 5000 corporate workers, the correlation coefficient of work satisfaction and life expectancy was found to be +0.7 with a p-value of 0.01. What is your interpretation?
options: Work satisfaction does not improve life expectancy
Strong statistically significant positive association between the variables
70% people who enjoy work will live longer
30% people who do not enjoy work will have a shorter life expectancy
questions.answer: B. Strong statistically significant positive association between the variables
questions.explanation:
The above study is statistically significant (p-value = 0.01) and indicates a strong positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +0.7) between work satisfaction and life expectancy.

Correlation is a measure of the statistical association of the variables, not a causal relationship.

Here, the coefficient of determination (r2) = 0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49. This means that 49% of the variation in life expectancy can be explained by satisfaction at work.

questions.question: A group of cardiologists found a correlation coefficient of 0.90 (p-value = 0.01) between the systolic BP and serum cholesterol levels of patients attending their clinics. Which of the following statements is an incorrect interpretation of this study?
options: The magnitude of systolic BP and serum cholesterol levels are closely related
A patient with a high systolic BP is likely to have high serum cholesterol
A patient with a low systolic BP is likely to have low serum cholesterol
80% of the variation in BP can be explained by serum cholesterol and vice versa
questions.answer: A. The magnitude of systolic BP and serum cholesterol levels are closely related
questions.explanation:
Correlation is an indicator of the strength and direction of the relationship between 2 variables, not the magnitude.

The given study is statistically significant (p-value = 0.01) with a strong positive correlation (r = +0.90) between systolic BP and cholesterol levels. Thus, it is likely that patients with high systolic BP will have high cholesterol levels and those with low BP will have low cholesterol levels.

The coefficient of determination (r2)here is 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.81. This indicates that around 80% of the variation in systolic BP among the patients can be explained by serum cholesterol levels.

questions.question: Among the given options, what can be the likely value of the coefficient of correlation between infant mortality rate and economic status?
questions.explanation:
Among the given options, the coefficient of correlation between infant mortality rate and economic status (r) is likely to be -0.8.

It is known that low economic status is associated with a high infant mortality rate. This indicates a negative correlation. However, the infant mortality rate is also influenced by other factors, indicating a moderate correlation (not equal to 1). This makes -0.8 the most likely value of correlation.

questions.question: High salt intake in individuals is associated with high blood pressure. What type of correlation is this?
questions.explanation:
An increase in blood pressure with salt intake is an example of a positive correlation.

The association of decreased life expectancy with increased smoking is an example of negative correlation.

questions.question: A scattergram was plotted as shown below to study the relationship between two variables. What is the correct interpretation?
options: There is correlation between both variables and the Pearson’s coefficient is 1
There is correlation between both variables and the Pearson’s coefficient is – 1
There is non-linear correlation between both variables
There is no association between both variables
questions.answer: C. There is non-linear correlation between both variables
questions.explanation:
The given scattergram depicts a non-linear correlation between the two variables.

Correlation expresses the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables in terms of a correlation coefficient. There are two types of correlation coefficients:

Pearson coefficient
Spearman coefficient

Used for data with continuous intervals
Used for data with discrete ordered intervals

Used to find linear relationships

(e.g. salt intake vs blood pressure)

Used to find linear or non-linear relationships

(e.g. socioeconomic status vs parity)

questions.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the following scattergram?
options: There is a perfect negative correlation between the two variables
There is a high positive correlation between the two variables
There is a high negative correlation between the two variables
There is a perfect positive correlation between the two variables
questions.answer: C. There is a high negative correlation between the two variables
questions.explanation: The given scattergram shows a high negative correlation between the two variables.

questions.question: The value of one parameter can be estimated from another related parameter by:
questions.explanation: The value of one parameter can be estimated from another related parameter by using regression techniques.

questions.question: If correlation is given by the equation y = a + bx, what would be the nature of the graph?
questions.explanation: The equation, y = a + bx indicates a straight line.

questions.question: In a study, the total cholesterol was calculated as a + b₁x₁ + b₂x₂ + b₃ x₃, where x₁ indicates calorie intake, x₂ indicates physical activity, and x₃ indicates body mass index. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation:
The given equation of y = a + b1x1 +b2x2…..bnxn is an example of multiple linear regression.

In this equation:

b1, b2…..bn represent different regression coefficients

x1, x2…….xn represent the known variables

questions.question: An epidemiologist has determined five independent factors influencing the outcome of a particular disease. Which of the following statistical methods can he use to compare these factors?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the outcome to be determined (dependent variable) is the occurrence of the disease, which is categorical (qualitative) in nature. Logistic regression can be used when a categorical dependent variable is being compared with either a categorical or numerical independent variable.

Linear regression is used when the outcome is numerical.

questions.question: What test is used to compare Kaplan-Meier survival curves?
questions.explanation:
The Cox proportional hazards test is used to compare Kaplan-Meier survival curves.

Survival analysis is used for analyzing the expected duration of time until one event occurs, such as death. The following methods are used for this are:

• Life table analysis

• Kaplan-Meier analysis - it involves calculating the survival function (the probability that a person will survive past a certain time)

Life tables and survival functions are graphically represented in a Kaplan-Meier plot or curve.

questions.question: Which of the following is not used to compare survival curves?
questions.explanation:
Fisher’s exact test is not used to compare survival curves. The following tests are used to compare the survival curves or Kaplan-Meier curves:

• Mantel-Haenszel test

• Log-rank test

• Cox regression or Cox proportional hazards analysis

questions.question: What is the Spearman coefficient used to determine?
questions.explanation:
Spearman coefficient is used to determine correlation. It is used to find linear or non-linear relationships for data with discrete ordered intervals.

Pearson correlation coefficient is used to find linear relationships for data with continuous intervals.

questions.question: A researcher wants to compare a newly developed test for COVID with the gold standard test. Which of the following methods can he use?
questions.explanation: The Bland-Altmann analysis is used for comparing a newly developed test with another test, which usually is the gold standard. This method involves the graphical construction of a Bland-Altmann plot which is used to compare the measurements from both methods.

chapters.chapter: Facets Of Clinical Research And Biostatistics

questions.question: Which of the following is true about simple random sampling?
options: It is the sampling method of choice for heterogenous population
Members are selected without specifying any criteria for selection
Every 5th or 10th member is picked at regular interval
Population is first divided into strata then sampled randomly
questions.answer: B. Members are selected without specifying any criteria for selection
questions.explanation: In simple random sampling, samples are drawn in such a way that every element in a population has equal chances of being included. In other words, the members are selected without specifying any criteria for selection.

questions.question: A study on the prevalence of diabetes was conducted and the sampling method shown below was used. Identify the sampling method used.
questions.explanation: In this study, the population is separated into homogenous sub-groups and from these, random samples are drawn. This sampling method is called stratified random sampling.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about cluster sampling?
options: Clusters are created based on similarities
It is a two stage sampling
It is cheaper than most other methods
It is a method used for rapid assessment
questions.answer: A. Clusters are created based on similarities
questions.explanation: In cluster sampling, the clusters are created randomly. On the contrary, in stratified random sampling, the strata or groups are created based on similarities.

questions.question: Which sampling method is used for assessing the immunization status of children under the immunization program?
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling is the method of sampling done in immunization programs for assessing the immunization status of children.

questions.question: A research is being conducted to assess the nutritional status of the children in a particular district. For this purpose, 2 children are randomly selected from every school in the district. What is this type of sampling known as?
questions.explanation: In the cluster sampling technique, the sub-groups of the population/ clusters are naturally occurring. These clusters are randomly made rather than based on any particular characteristic. The population of children here is naturally divided into various schools without being based on any characteristics.

questions.question: In which of the following sampling techniques is design effect used?
questions.explanation:
The design effect is used in cluster sampling to allow for design structure and correlation between clusters.

The design effect (DEFF) is used to decide the sample size needed for cluster sampling. This is done by calculating the difference in sampling variability to the variability expected with simple random sampling (SRS).

It can more simply be stated as the actual sample size divided by the effective sample size (what you would expect if you were using SRS). For example, let’s say you were using cluster sampling. A DEFF of 2 means the variance is twice as large as you would expect with SRS. It also means that if you used cluster sampling, you’d have to use twice the sample size.

questions.question: Simple random sampling is ideal for which of the following study groups?
options: A study being conducted on all vaccinated people of an area
A study on occupational exposure in all workers of the same factory
A study being conducted on prevalence of acute gastroenteritis in all school children of an area
A study on prevalence of hypertension in men aged 50-75 years in an area
questions.answer: B. A study on occupational exposure in all workers of the same factory
questions.explanation:
Simple random sampling is ideal for a homogeneous population as the sample would be completely representative of the population and it would eliminate the need for systematization or stratification. Here, workers of the same factory form a homogeneous population.

Option A: For a vaccinated population - cluster sampling

Options C and D: For a heterogeneous population - stratified sampling

questions.question: In a study, first schools were sampled, then sections and finally students. What is this type of sampling known as?
questions.explanation:
Multistage sampling is the taking of samples in stages using smaller and smaller sampling units at each stage. It involves dividing the population into groups (or clusters). Then, one or more clusters are chosen at random and everyone within the chosen cluster is sampled.

Snowball sampling is a type of non-random sampling preferred in case of diseases with social stigma (eg., alcoholism, iv drug abuse etc).

questions.question: For an epidemiological study, sampling was done as shown below. What is this type of sampling known as?
questions.explanation: Systematic sampling involves a systematic pattern to sampling, like choosing every 3rd person from an area or hospital, etc.

questions.question: In a study, subjects were assigned according to the potential factor that will influence the outcome of the study. What is this type of sampling known as?
questions.explanation:
In stratified random sampling, the population is first divided into homogeneous groups or strata. From these strata, random samples are drawn.

For example: If a researcher wants to conduct a research study to determine if alcohol consumption is a risk factor for lung cancer. He must first stratify the population into smokers and non-smokers because smoking is a known risk factor and also smoking is associated with alcohol consumption.

questions.explanation: The image shown is that of an asymmetric funnel plot. This usually occurs in meta-analysis due to publication bias or other reporting bias.

questions.question: What is Dixon’s Q test used for?
questions.explanation: The Dixon’s Q test is used for identification and rejection of outliers. It is usually used in normal distributions.
